title: Cybersecurity as a Professional Discipline: A Medical Model for Education, Practice, and Standards of Care

detail.title: Cybersecurity as a Professional Discipline: A Medical Model for Education, Practice, and Standards of Care
detail.abstract: Cybersecurity has become a foundational requirement for the stability and continuity of modern society, yet the field remains fragmented in its educational pathways, professional standards, and workforce structure. Unlike established disciplines such as medicine, cybersecurity lacks a unified framework for training, validating, and deploying practitioners. This paper argues that cybersecurity should be formalized as a professional discipline using the medical field as a primary institutional model. By examining the structural elements of medical education—including foundational training, supervised clinical practice, specialization pathways, and standards of care—this work proposes a corresponding framework for cybersecurity. The model introduces a lifecycle-based approach to digital system protection, encompassing prevention, detection, response, recovery, and long-term resilience. It further outlines the need for standardized competency validation, ethical obligations, and continuous professional development. While cybersecurity is inherently multidisciplinary and influenced by domains such as warfare, ecology, law, and engineering, medicine provides the most effective template for professionalization and workforce implementation. This paper presents a structured model for cybersecurity education and practice that aims to improve consistency, reliability, and trust in the field.

title: When Less Is More: Managing AI Adoption with Usage Targets
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics, , Faculty of Business and Economics, The University of Hong Kong, The university of HongKong and The University of Hong Kong

detail.title: When Less Is More: Managing AI Adoption with Usage Targets
detail.abstract: Usage mandates can accelerate AI adoption, but they also risk turning adoption into a metric to be gamed. We study a medical-device company that required roughly 5,000 employees to submit 200 AI queries per month, then reduced the target to 100 through a staggered branch rollout. Complete query logs show that the mandate increased first-time adoption, but 32% of queries are either repeated or non-work queries under the 200-query target. Lowering the target reduced query volume by 30%, improved query quality, and increased sales by 7% among sales employees. Our findings suggest that the design of usage targets shapes both how employees use AI and the returns from that use.

title: The New Dyad in Professional Services: Subject Matter Experts, AI Specialists, and the Architecture of Modern Professional Services

detail.title: The New Dyad in Professional Services: Subject Matter Experts, AI Specialists, and the Architecture of Modern Professional Services

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder and principal partner of WTL Governance, White, Turing & Lovelace LLC, an AI governance consulting firm. No external funding was received for this research. The analysis reflects the author's independent assessment.

detail.abstract:
Professional services firms are reorganizing around a structural partnership between subject matter experts and artificial intelligence specialists. This report traces the model to its origin in the physician and administrator dyad established at the Mayo Clinic in 1908, a governance structure that 77 percent of U.S. healthcare leaders still use today, and examines how the arrival of broadly capable generative AI has produced a modern successor in which the complementary partner is an AI expert rather than a human administrator.

The analysis draws on field evidence from the 2023 Harvard and Boston Consulting Group experiment, which found that consultants using GPT-4 completed 12.2 percent more tasks, worked 25.1 percent faster, and produced outputs rated 40 percent higher in quality for work inside the model's capability frontier. It surveys the adoption of the dyad across five sectors: healthcare consulting, where ambient AI scribes have reduced clinician burnout and increased physician productivity in randomized trials; private equity, where the AI Operating Partner has become a standard fund role; banking and capital markets, where proprietary AI platforms pair relationship bankers with embedded AI teams; legal services, where agentic AI platforms function as junior research associates under attorney supervision; and the Big Four professional advisory firms, where junior hiring reductions and technologist growth are reshaping the traditional workforce pyramid into a diamond.

The report examines the empirical complementarity framework that governs effective dyads, projects the transition from dyad to agentic network over 2026 to 2030, and offers practical guidance on structuring, measuring, and governing the new partnership.

title: Metaverse for Supply Chain Management and Operations

detail.title: Metaverse for Supply Chain Management and Operations
detail.abstract: In this chapter, we develop a framework that illustrates how the metaverse, a persistent multiuser environment that combines physical and digital elements, can enhance supply chain management and operations. We discuss its impact on five core activities: communication and collaboration, data analytics and planning, manufacturing and maintenance, logistics and transportation, and, finally, warehousing and inventory management. Additionally, the metaverse can strengthen relationships and skills by interacting with suppliers, engaging customers, and enhancing employees' skills. Finally, it can improve important supply chain properties: resilience, visibility and transparency, and sustainability. We conclude this chapter with recommendations for researchers, managers, and policymakers.

title: MARKO: A Pragmatic Protocol for Evaluating Operational Relevance in Scientic Publications

detail.title: MARKO: A Pragmatic Protocol for Evaluating Operational Relevance in Scientic Publications
detail.abstract: Scientic publications satisfy formal validity criteria while producing no operational consequence. The MARKO protocol introduces ve conjunctive conditions mechanism, application, reproducibility, cost, and outcomeas a stress test for implementability. Each dimension operates as a necessary condition; the absence of any one collapses the evaluative structure. The protocol targets applied research that borrows the rhetoric of implementation without specifying the conditions under which implementation would occur.

title: A Causally Disciplined Framework for Monetary Promises, Trust Architectures, and Structural Risk Allocation in Global Financial Systems

detail.title: A Causally Disciplined Framework for Monetary Promises, Trust Architectures, and Structural Risk Allocation in Global Financial Systems
detail.abstract: Theoretical Framework. This paper develops a causally disciplined framework for analysing modern monetary systems as layered promise–trust–risk architectures. It advances two testable hypotheses: (H1) that post-Bretton Woods monetary systems exhibit a structural shift from external redemption anchors to multi-anchor institutional credibility systems; and (H2) that this shift is associated with a measurable asymmetry in downside risk allocation, systematically redistributing financial losses toward actors with lower systemic policy leverage. The framework formalises three analytical layers (contractual, balance sheet, trust-coordination), operationalises the concepts of promise, breach, and risk allocation, and proposes a causal mechanism—asymmetric exit optionality—formalised as a two-player game-theoretic model with empirically calibrated payoff proxies. Evidence and Normative Synthesis. H2 is tested across four case studies: Southeast Asia (1997), Greece (2010), Egypt (2016–present, with detailed counterfactual analysis), and Zambia (2020), with a systematic cross-case comparison, invariance test, and a formalised Risk Allocation Ratio (RAR). A counterexample stress test (South Korea, 1997–2010) refines H2 by specifying the boundary conditions under which the asymmetry can be reversed. A normative module evaluates these structures against both Islamic economic principles (rib¯a, gharar, ‘adl) and secular justice theories (Rawls, Sen, Piketty), bridged through the balance-sheet mechanics of credit-money creation. The paper states explicit falsification conditions, proposes four econometric testing strategies, and finds that the system systematically produces asymmetric distributional outcomes that require structural explanation—while acknowledging that the distinction between structural injustice and efficient risk pricing is not yet resolved.

title: Exclusión juvenil en Honduras: un análisis descriptivo a partir de la EPHPM 2025

detail.title: Exclusión juvenil en Honduras: un análisis descriptivo a partir de la EPHPM 2025

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding

detail.abstract: Este estudio analiza el fenómeno de la exclusión juvenil en Honduras a partir de datos de la Encuesta Permanente de Hogares de Propósitos Múltiples (EPHPM) 2025. Se define como población en exclusión a aquellos jóvenes que no estudian ni trabajan, abordando el problema desde un enfoque descriptivo. El análisis identifica patrones asociados a variables como sexo, área geográfica, nivel educativo y acceso a tecnología, evidenciando desigualdades estructurales que limitan la inserción social y laboral de la juventud. Los resultados muestran una mayor incidencia de exclusión en mujeres, zonas rurales y hogares de bajos ingresos, así como una relación directa entre nivel educativo y participación laboral. Asimismo, se identifican brechas en el acceso y uso de tecnologías de información que refuerzan estas desigualdades. El estudio concluye que la exclusión juvenil constituye un fenómeno estructural que requiere intervenciones integrales centradas en educación, empleo y acceso a tecnología.

title: Recognition Lost: How AI-Generated Summaries Discourage Review Writing
affiliations: University of Western Ontario - Ivey Business School, University of Exeter, UMASS Amherst and University of Western Ontario - Ivey Business School

detail.title: Recognition Lost: How AI-Generated Summaries Discourage Review Writing
detail.abstract: Many platforms deploy AI to offer readers qualitative summaries of online reviews. By synthesizing different consumer perspectives into a brief synopsis, AI-generated summaries (AIGS) make the task of navigating a large volume of reviews easier and provide a service that appears to be popular with both marketers and readers. Taking the perspective of review writers, we document in four preregistered experiments an overlooked negative effect of AIGS. Drawing on Social Recognition Theory, we show that in the presence of AIGS, writers anticipate their reviews will receive less recognition, leading to a deterioration in review writing (i.e. less likely to leave a review, less writing effort). These effects are attenuated when external incentives for reviewing are offered. The current research offers timely insights into understanding a novel downside of AIGS and provides managerial insights regarding online review generation and information management for platforms.

title: Disentangling Greenwashing from Authentic Environmental Performance: A Double Machine Learning Approach to Corporate Sustainability Disclosure

detail.title: Disentangling Greenwashing from Authentic Environmental Performance: A Double Machine Learning Approach to Corporate Sustainability Disclosure
detail.abstract: Sustainability reports have become standard in corporate disclosure. Yet the relationship between disclosed environmental commitment and actual performance remains unclear. This paper develops and demonstrates a novel methodological framework combining Double Machine Learning with Natural Language Processing (BERT) to detect greenwashing through causal inference. We introduce an integrated approach: (1) BERT-based quantification of disclosure intensity from sustainability reports, (2) Double Machine Learning with 5-fold cross-fitting to handle 250+ high-dimensional controls, and (3) Causal forest estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects. Using synthetic panel data structured to match real-world characteristics (850 firms × 8 years = 6,800 observations), we demonstrate the complete methodology pipeline. Results show that our DML framework successfully recovers causal treatment effects with valid confidence intervals, and we identify approximately 6.5% of high-disclosing firms as potential greenwashers based on disclosure-outcome mismatch patterns. The framework is generalizable to real corporate data and other disclosure-outcome applications. We provide reproducible code and full transparency on data construction to enable future empirical applications with access to actual disclosure and environmental outcome data.

title: Why Systems Fail Before They Fail: The Double Translation Trap in the Boeing 737 MAX

detail.title: Why Systems Fail Before They Fail: The Double Translation Trap in the Boeing 737 MAX

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based exclusively on publicly available documents and does not involve human participants. Ethics approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently.

detail.abstract:
How can complex systems follow established procedures and still drift away from their intended purpose? This paper examines the certification of the Boeing 737 MAX to show how institutional intent—flight safety—was translated into a training-based proxy that came to guide both decisions and evaluation.

As this proxy became decision-authoritative, contradictory evidence no longer influenced the decision process. The paper introduces the Double Translation Trap: a structural condition in which an operational proxy, initially used to implement intent, becomes the standard for judging alignment. Under this condition, systems can remain internally coherent while progressively losing alignment with the conditions they are meant to represent.

Using a reproducible artefact-tracing protocol, the analysis reconstructs how certification criteria rendered internal test data non-decision-relevant within the formal decision chain. This allows misalignment to be identified within the formal record before outcomes change, as a mismatch between governing proxies and a system’s own evidence.

The findings have implications beyond aviation. The same structural pattern can arise in governance systems, regulatory frameworks, and AI-mediated decision environments where metrics, thresholds, or models both guide action and define evaluation. The paper provides a diagnostic lens for identifying when decision systems become closed to relevant evidence while continuing to function as designed.

title: Follow the leader: The effect of high-quality peers on turnover decisions

detail.title: Follow the leader: The effect of high-quality peers on turnover decisions

declarations.funderStatement: This work was funded by Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (UIDB/00124/2020, UIDP/00124/2020, UID/00124, Nova School of Business and Economics and Social Sciences DataLab - PINFRA/22209/2016), POR Lisboa and POR Norte (Social Sciences DataLab, PINFRA/22209/2016).

detail.abstract: This paper studies how coworker departures and former-peer links relate to (i) the decision to leave an employer, (ii) the choice of destination firm conditional on moving, and (iii) wages at the destination. Our analysis reveals that higher recent peer group turnover predicts a higher individual probability of leaving, and the composition of exits matters. Additionally, having at least one former peer at a candidate firm raises the probability of choosing that firm significantly, especially if at least one former peer is of high quality. Furthermore, movers earn higher wages at entry when the destination employs former peers, particularly if a high-quality former peer is present. Finally, peer-linked moves are associated with stronger positive assortative matching in wages. The results indicate that workplace networks materially shape retention, reallocation, and wage outcomes, and that peer quality is central to understanding these effects.

title: UNDERSTANDING FARMERS' APPROPRIATION OF AGRICULTURAL INSTITUTIONAL INNOVATIONS: INSIGHT FROM BENIN, WEST AFRICA
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, National Institute of Agricultural Research of Benin (INRAB), Agriculture Policy Analysis Programme, National Institute of Agricultural Research of Benin (INRAB), National Institute of Agricultural Research of Benin (INRAB) and National Institute of Agricultural Research of Benin (INRAB)

detail.title: UNDERSTANDING FARMERS' APPROPRIATION OF AGRICULTURAL INSTITUTIONAL INNOVATIONS: INSIGHT FROM BENIN, WEST AFRICA

publicationDetails.detailsText: Scientific Papers Series Management, Economic Engineering in Agriculture and Rural Development, Volume 26, No 1. Pp.55-64

detail.abstract: This study assessed the appropriation by Beninese farmers of major institutional reforms undertaken in 2016 to transform Benin's agriculture into a high-performing and resilient sector against exogenous shocks. Employing a descriptive approach and a logistic regression model applied to cross-sectional data collected from 1,501 farmers in 85 villages, the research examined the appropriation of the reforms of Territorialization of agricultural development and Agricultural sector governance. The findings reveal significant resignation among farmers due to insufficient consideration of their voices. Appropriation is influenced by socioeconomic factors such as literacy levels, diversification of agricultural activities, peer networks as a source of information, soybean cultivation (an alternative to cotton), access to agricultural services, understanding the importance of reforms, and the formulation process. Age influences the appropriation of Territorialization of agricultural development, while membership in a farmers' organization and cotton cultivation affect the appropriation of Agricultural sector governance. These results highlight the need for a strengthened participatory approach, supported by information sessions and community dialogues, to optimize reform adoption and enhance their impact on Benin's agricultural sector performance. This study offers crucial insights for agricultural policies in sub-Saharan Africa, where similar reforms are often implemented to bolster the resilience and performance of agricultural sectors.

title: Assessing stakeholder perceptions on institutional reforms in Benin's agricultural Sector: Relevance and social inclusion perspectives
affiliations: National Institute of Agricultural Research of Benin (INRAB), National Institute of Agricultural Research of Benin (INRAB), Agriculture Policy Analysis Programme, National Institute of Agricultural Research of Benin (INRAB), National Institute of Agricultural Research of Benin (INRAB), affiliation not provided to SSRN and National Institute of Agricultural Research of Benin (INRAB)

detail.title: Assessing stakeholder perceptions on institutional reforms in Benin's agricultural Sector: Relevance and social inclusion perspectives
detail.abstract: Existing literature about public policies in Sub-Saharan Africa predominantly focuses on international institutional and foreign power interference and limited attention has been paid to personal stakeholders' perspectives. This study examines stakeholders' perceptions regarding the major institutional changes that have occurred in Benin's agricultural sector since 2016 and the factors influencing these perceptions. Data were gathered from 1500 farmers and 383 key informants representing public and private institutions across Benin's Agricultural Development Poles. Continuous thematic content analyses and analytical questioning were employed to explore the stakeholders' social representations regarding institutional reform. Relative frequency distributions and polarity indices were calculated to determine the direction (positive or negative) of the stakeholder' perceptions. Additionally, the factors influencing stakeholder' perceptions were analyzed using logistic regression models. The results reveal that institutional stakeholders held positive opinions regarding the territorialization of agricultural development, both regarding its relevance and formulation approach. However, the approaches associated with the abolition of certain structures or agencies received negative connotations. The relevance of this reform was positively evaluated by institutional managers but viewed less favorably by non-managers. Stakeholders linked the positive aspects of the reforms to the shared vision of revitalizing agricultural sector development. To foster consensus and align reforms with stakeholders' aspirations, policymakers must expand consultation at all level.

title: Value vs. Cost Function Approximation: Environmental Impact and Profit Comparison in Production Planning Under Uncertainty
affiliations: Technical University Munich, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Center for Transportation & Logistics and Technische Universität München (TUM)

detail.title: Value vs. Cost Function Approximation: Environmental Impact and Profit Comparison in Production Planning Under Uncertainty

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We are reporting that T. Greil and M. Grunow received funding from SAP SE [contract number DE2021-043] that may be affected by the research reported in this paper. We have a plan in place for managing any potential conflicts arising from that involvement.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by SAP SE [contract number DE-2021-043].

detail.abstract: Industry practice typically relies on sequential planning, where inventory modules set static safety stocks through simple heuristics that are subsequently fed into sales and operations planning (S&OP) systems. While computationally fast, this siloed approach overlooks the environmental impact (EI) and economic benefits of integrated, state-dependent decision-making. As firms increasingly explore more sophisticated stochastic methods, this work compares two sequential decision analytics approaches: a parameterized cost function approximation (CFA) that tunes safety stocks in a deterministic optimization model, capturing the practical status quo, and a value function approximation (VFA), which applies value iteration to represent stochastic planning. We train policies and evaluate them out-of-sample in a food case with refrigeration-related emissions. Results show that VFA only outperforms slightly regarding profit (within 0.1-2.7%), yet reduces emissions by up to 47.9%, albeit with computation times 135 times longer. Robustness checks across stationary demand and forecast-update uncertainty levels reveal that higher forecast-update variability amplifies EIs more strongly than profits. VFA achieves lower EI variance than CFA, suggesting heteroskedasticity across planning paradigms. Overall, our findings demonstrate that when inventory imposes high environmental impact, static safety stocks should be replaced by state-dependent stochastic planning decisions. This requires the integration of corresponding IT systems and S&OP processes.

title:
Quantum Computing Applications in Big Data Mining: Leveraging Quantum Principles for Enhanced Data Analysis 
A Comprehensive Research Study
affiliations: Vikrant Institute of Technology and Management

detail.title:
Quantum Computing Applications in Big Data Mining: Leveraging Quantum Principles for Enhanced Data Analysis 
A Comprehensive Research Study
detail.abstract: The exponential growth of data generation in contemporary digital ecosystems presents unprecedented challenges for traditional computational paradigms. This research paper investigates the transformative potential of quantum computing principles applied to big data mining operations. We examine how quantum mechanical properties, including superposition, entanglement, and quantum interference, enable fundamentally different approaches to pattern recognition, classification, and knowledge discovery in massive datasets. Through theoretical analysis and algorithmic exploration, we demonstrate that quantum-enhanced data mining techniques offer substantial advantages in computational complexity, processing speed, and solution quality for specific problem classes. Our findings indicate that quantum algorithms can achieve exponential speedups for certain mining tasks, including similarity searches, clustering operations, and optimization problems that remain computationally intractable for classical systems. This study contributes to the emerging field of quantum machine learning by providing a comprehensive framework for understanding how quantum computational resources can be strategically deployed to address the scalability challenges inherent in big data analytics.

title: Power Distance and Gender Gap in Economic Participation: The Roles of Educational Attainment and Masculinity
affiliations: and University of Central Oklahoma - College of Business

detail.title: Power Distance and Gender Gap in Economic Participation: The Roles of Educational Attainment and Masculinity
detail.abstract: This study examines the association between national culture and the gender gap in economic participation, with a particular focus on the power distance (PD) dimension. We also explore how educational attainment and the masculinity (MAS) dimension interact with these factors. Our findings indicate that women's economic participation is significantly lower in high-PD societies. Moreover, the positive association of education and women's economic participation diminishes as PD increases, suggesting that hierarchical norms and tradition-driven expectations may constrain educated women from fully leveraging their qualifications. This moderating effect is more pronounced in high-MAS contexts, where traditional gender roles are strongly emphasized. In contrast, we find that in low-MAS societies, PD and educational attainment may exert limited influence on women's economic participation. From a managerial perspective, firms operating in high-MAS and high-PD societies should intentionally prioritize dismantling hierarchical practices, foster inclusive leadership, and implement transparent career advancement pathways. In high-MAS and low-PD societies, educational initiatives such as mentorship programs can further mitigate cultural constraints and enable women to realize their full economic potential.

title: Empirical Modelling of Truck Payload Variance as a Driver of Freight Costs, Efficiency, and Environmental Impact on the Transportation Networks in India

detail.title: Empirical Modelling of Truck Payload Variance as a Driver of Freight Costs, Efficiency, and Environmental Impact on the Transportation Networks in India

publicationDetails.detailsText: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF LOGISTICS MANAGEMENT, volume 4, issue 1, 2026[10.34218/IJLM_04_01_001]

detail.abstract: FreightFox is a data centric Transportation Management System focused on the logistics procure-to-pay platform for manufacturing industry segment. FreightFox processes ~4 Million+ Ewaybills (EWB) annually for over 16+ enterprise customers handling products worth ~US$ 1.50 Billion moved using the platform with an average revenue size of organization using the platform at ~USD 0.75 Billion+. This translates into tracking of ~4 BTKMs (Billion Ton-Kms) of goods moved through the FreightFox platform. Payload variance defined as the deviation between various trucks placed under the same category/Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) segment is a critical but an understudied factor impacting freight efficiency, costs, and sustainability. This research empirically investigates the relationship between payload variance and freight rate indices, addressing four key questions: (1) the correlation between payload variance and freight rates, (2) the influence of vehicle characteristics (category, make, dimensions) for specific application, (3) operational impacts on logistics budgets, warehousing, and cash flow and (4) increase / decrease on emissions from transportation and distribution networks as a result of this variance. Using operational freight data and vehicle performance metrics, we analyzed variance patterns across vehicle categories and developed predictive models using Machine Learning (ML). Results reveal a significant correlation between payload variance and freight index fluctuations, with specific vehicle categories exhibiting predictable variance trends. Critically, payload variance contributes to carbon emissions via relatively lower vehicle utilization in the similar segment of trucks. The study proposes an empirical formula to predict variance based on vehicle traits and introduces a novel metric to quantify operational impacts on planning, budgeting and execution. Key contributions include enabling dynamic freight contracts using variance predictions, optimizing vehicle selection, and reducing both logistics costs and environmental footprints. These insights equip managers with actionable tools to enhance efficiency and sustainability in freight transportation.

title: Interpretable ML and Text-Based LLMs in Finance: Regulatory Explainability and Portfolio Decision Transparency

detail.title: Interpretable ML and Text-Based LLMs in Finance: Regulatory Explainability and Portfolio Decision Transparency
detail.abstract: This paper reviews the literature on interpretable machine learning and text-based large language models in finance. It argues that explainability in finance serves two distinct but related purposes: meeting regulatory demands and improving transparency in portfolio decisions. Using this distinction, the paper synthesizes prior work on interpretable ML models, applications of LLM-based financial text systems, and grounding architectures that make outputs inspectable and usable. The review highlights common limitations in evidence reliability, point-in-time evaluation, explanation stability, and institutional deployment. It concludes that further progress will depend on linking transparent predictive structure with grounded language-based reasoning.

title: The Impact of Multiagent Systems on Autonomous Production and Supply Chain Networks: Use Cases, Barriers and Contributions to Logistics Network Resilience
affiliations: Technische Universität Berlin (TU Berlin), Technische Universität Berlin (TU Berlin), MODUL University Vienna and Technische Universität Berlin (TU Berlin)

detail.title: The Impact of Multiagent Systems on Autonomous Production and Supply Chain Networks: Use Cases, Barriers and Contributions to Logistics Network Resilience
detail.abstract:
Purpose-Academics and practitioners have long acknowledged the potential of multiagent systems (MAS) to automate and autonomize decisionmaking in logistics and supply chain networks. Despite the manifold promises of MAS, industry adoption is lagging behind, and the exact benefits of these systems remain unclear. This study aims to fill this knowledge gap by analyzing 11 specific MAS use cases, highlighting their benefits, clarifying how they can help enhance logistics network resilience and identifying existing barriers.

Design/methodology/approach-A three-stage Delphi study was conducted with 18 industry experts. In the first round, these experts identified 11 use cases of MAS and their potential benefits, as well as any barriers that could hinder their adoption. In the second round, they assessed the identified use cases with regard to their potential to enhance logistics network resilience and improve organizational productivity. Furthermore, they estimated the complexity of MAS implementation. In the third round, the experts reassessed their evaluations in light of the evaluations of the other study participants.

Findings-This study proposes 11 specific MAS use cases and illustrates their potential for increasing logistics network resilience and enhancing organizational performance due to autonomous decision-making in informational processes. Furthermore, this study discusses important barriers for MAS, such as lack of standardization, insufficient technological maturity, soaring costs, complex change management and a lack of existing use cases. From a theoretical perspective, it is shown how MAS can contribute to resilience research in supply chain management.

Practical implications-The identification and assessment of diverse MAS use cases informs managers about the potential of this technology and the barriers that need to be overcome.

Originality/value-This study fills a gap in the literature by providing a thorough and up-to-date assessment of the potential of MAS for logistics and supply chain management. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first study to investigate the relevance of MAS for logistics network resilience using the Delphi method.

title: Technorepublicanism: A Manifesto for Semantic Sovereignty

detail.title: Technorepublicanism: A Manifesto for Semantic Sovereignty

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships that may have influenced this work. This document was produced independently, without institutional affiliation or external funding.

contentFormat.other: Political manifesto and foundational doctrine paper introducing Technorepublicanism: a doctrine on semantic sovereignty, republican constraints on state AI governance, and its seven foundational principles.

detail.abstract:
This document introduces and defines Technorepublicanism, a political doctrine that holds that the modern State must maintain the classical republican values — separation of powers, representation, and citizen auditing — while sovereignly defining the semantic categories through which technology interprets and governs reality.

The document begins from a key diagnosis: 21st century sovereignty is not played out solely on territorial and legal dimensions, but on a new one: the semantic dimension. Whoever defines the ontologies through which artificial intelligence systems classify, infer, and act upon reality exercises a governing power that existing institutional frameworks neither regulate nor constrain. This displacement of definitional power, from constitutions and legal codes toward the proprietary ontologies of private and transnational actors, constitutes what is popularly known as technofeudalism.

As a structural response, the document proposes Sovereign Republican Ontologies (SRO): the creation of a public semantic architecture through which a nation defines how the State represents its own reality, what can be inferred from it, and the limits within which it can act. On this basis, it articulates the seven fundamental principles of technorepublicanism: semantic sovereignty, federated ontology, human primacy, continuous auditing, right to appeal, separation of functions, and algorithmic transparency.

The document argues that Argentina possesses unique structural conditions to lead this transition, and proposes the Technorenaissance as a civilizational horizon: the construction of state-level Organizational Cognitive Structures (OCS) that are simultaneously sovereign, republican, and open to challenge by citizens.


This is the English translation of the original Spanish version, published simultaneously on SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=6698858

title: Living Consensus: How AI Scientists are Reshaping Scholarly Publishing
affiliations: University of Science and Technology Beijing and

detail.title: Living Consensus: How AI Scientists are Reshaping Scholarly Publishing
detail.abstract: The architecture of scholarly communication was designed for an era when knowledge production was exclusively human, verification was deliberate, and publications were permanent records. The emergence of artificial superintelligence (ASI) and the prospect of humanmachine cognitive fusion challenge these foundational assumptions. This commentary argues that scholarly communication will evolve from repositories of static conclusions into dynamic networks of verified consensus. We trace this transformation across four structural dimensions: from articles to executable knowledge processes, from peer review to algorithmic consensus convergence, from authorship to contribution graphs, and from content ownership to certification protocol layers. We identify critical societal challenges, including epistemic equity, algorithmic bias in verification, the dissolution of traditional intellectual property, and the erosion of disciplinary boundaries. We argue that leading journals will become protocol layers for civilization-level consensus networks, deriving authority not from content monopolies but from the rigor and transparency of their verification algorithms. This paradigm shift carries profound implications for how societies codify, validate, and transmit collective understanding.

title: The Scent, Not the Hound: A User Epistemic Responsibility Framework for Prompt Engineering Failure

detail.title: The Scent, Not the Hound: A User Epistemic Responsibility Framework for Prompt Engineering Failure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests, financial or otherwise.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a theoretical research contribution; no human participants or primary data collection were involved.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Prompt engineering failures are routinely attributed to model limitations or technique selection. The more fundamental problem is unaddressed: users cannot diagnose which layer of the human-model system they are responsible for, and existing frameworks do not tell them. This paper proposes a User Epistemic Responsibility Framework built on a single boundary: users control immediate state (context window configuration) and do not control long-term state (parametric knowledge encoded in training weights). From this boundary, a four-type failure typology follows-absent, ambiguous, excessive, and false context-each mapped to epistemic coordinates derived from an eight-quadrant extension of the Johari Window (Luft & Ingham, 1955). The extension introduces four quadrants specific to human-AI coupling, including Q7 (epistemic self-misattribution) and Q8 (authority-miscalibrated output). Their compounding interaction constitutes the framework's most consequential finding: a selfreinforcing compound failure in which miscalibrated user goals receive high-confidence model validation, rendering execution-quality techniques ineffective at the point of application. User-side deference formation (algority, N=610) and model-side sycophancy persistence once triggered (SycEval: 78.5%) provide independent empirical grounding for each component. The Scent Model operationalizes the responsibility boundary as a two-variable retrieval problem. This paper is a theoretical research contribution; Section 5 identifies testable predictions for empirical validation.

title: Artificial Intelligence and International Arbitration: A Comprehensive Listing of Governing Laws, Institutional Rules, Professional Responsibility Standards, And Guidance

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and International Arbitration: A Comprehensive Listing of Governing Laws, Institutional Rules, Professional Responsibility Standards, And Guidance
detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence has transformed international arbitration from a future concern into a present compliance obligation. Arbitrators using AI tools to review documents or draft awards are deployers of regulated systems under the EU AI Act’s Annex III high-risk classification. Counsel submitting AI-generated research is subject to binding professional responsibility obligations under ABA Formal Opinion 512. Data processed in the course of a digitally distributed arbitration simultaneously engages multiple mandatory data protection regimes, each attaching through independent connecting factors, regardless of the seat or the parties’ agreement. And the cybersecurity landscape for arbitral proceedings has been materially altered by the disclosure of the Model Context Protocol vulnerability class and the April 2026 disclosure of the Anthropic Mythos AI model capability.

This listing report provides a comprehensive, practitioner-oriented catalog of regulatory and governance instruments applicable to AI in international arbitral proceedings as of April 21, 2026. It covers: (1) general AI laws, organized by jurisdiction; (2) arbitration-specific institutional rules and guidance from thirteen institutions; (3) ABA Model Rules and formal ethics opinions; (4) data protection and cybersecurity laws constituting the lex data framework; (5) leading cases; (6) emerging technology developments; and (7) a select scholarly bibliography.

The report is intended as a standing reference resource for arbitrators, counsel, arbitral institutions, and arbitration committee members. It is accurate as of April 21, 2026, and will require updating as the regulatory landscape continues to evolve. Readers with additions or observations should contact the author.

title: Transformasi Peranan Kesatuan Sekerja dalam Era Pasca Industri: Integrasi Dinamika Global dan Realiti Struktural Sabah, Malaysia dalam Kerangka Konseptual Hubungan Pekerjaan

detail.title: Transformasi Peranan Kesatuan Sekerja dalam Era Pasca Industri: Integrasi Dinamika Global dan Realiti Struktural Sabah, Malaysia dalam Kerangka Konseptual Hubungan Pekerjaan
detail.abstract: Peralihan ke arah masyarakat pasca industri yang dicirikan oleh ekonomi berasaskan pengetahuan, digitalisasi, dan fleksibiliti pekerjaan telah mengubah landskap hubungan pekerjaan secara global. Dalam konteks ini, kesatuan sekerja berdepan cabaran untuk menyesuaikan peranan tradisional mereka dalam mempertahankan hak pekerja. Artikel ini bertujuan mensintesis secara kritis literatur sedia ada bagi membina kerangka konseptual tentang peranan kesatuan sekerja dalam masyarakat pasca industri dengan fokus kepada Sabah, Malaysia. Pendekatan sintesis naratif digunakan dengan analisis tematik berdasarkan Braun dan Clarke (2006) bagi mengenal pasti pola utama dalam literatur terkini. Dapatan utama menunjukkan empat tema dominan: (i) perubahan struktur pekerjaan global, (ii) cabaran institusional kesatuan sekerja dalam ekonomi gig dan telekerja, (iii) kelemahan penglibatan pekerja tidak formal, dan (iv) keperluan reformasi dasar buruh yang lebih inklusif. Kajian ini juga mendapati bahawa kesatuan sekerja di Malaysia, khususnya Sabah, masih beroperasi dalam kerangka perundangan yang kurang responsif terhadap perubahan ekonomi digital. Kesimpulannya, kesatuan sekerja perlu menjalani transformasi strategik melalui pendekatan kolaboratif, inovasi organisasi, dan pengukuhan advokasi dasar. Implikasi kajian ini penting dalam memperkukuh teori hubungan pekerjaan serta menyediakan panduan praktikal kepada pembuat dasar dan pemegang taruh industri.

title: THE GOVERNANCE GAP: AI Integration in Resource-Prudent Organizations and the Frameworks That Don't Yet Exist

detail.title: THE GOVERNANCE GAP: AI Integration in Resource-Prudent Organizations and the Frameworks That Don't Yet Exist
detail.abstract:
This paper is about a specific problem affecting a specific population: organizations that carry real compliance obligations, are already running AI-connected tools, and have no governance infrastructure designed for either condition, let alone both at once.

The population is not defined by size, it is defined by function. A 200-person county 911 center, a 40-person GovTech vendor with a FedRAMP authorization, a regional healthcare network operating under HIPAA while billing automation quietly adds AI features: these organizations share three conditions simultaneously. They carry enforceable compliance obligations under sector-specific federal frameworks (CJIS, CMMC, HIPAA, FedRAMP, and their state-level
equivalents), they are already using AI-connected tools whether or not they made a deliberate decision to adopt them, and they have no dedicated governance function capable of managing the intersection.

The evidence base for this is sourced, not speculative. OECD and SBA data document that small organizations are adopting AI at a pace that now approaches large-firm adoption rates, primarily through embedded features in existing platforms rather than through deliberate AI procurement. Microsoft's H2 2025 AI Diffusion Report places US working-age AI tool usage at 28.3 percent of the population, a significant share of which belongs to organizations with no
formal AI governance at all. The compliance frameworks these organizations operate under (CJIS v6.0, CMMC 2.0, the HIPAA Privacy Rule, FedRAMP's finalized Significant Change Notification standard) are current, enforced, and contain no AI-specific implementation guidance. The best available legal analysis of the AI/HIPAA intersection identifies three layers of unresolved definitional questions that existing regulatory text does not answer. CJIS contains no AI provisions. CMMC 2.0 is in active contract rollout as of December 2024. FedRAMP's transformative change classification means that adding an AI feature to an authorized product
can trigger a months-long re-authorization process that a 35-person vendor may not survive financially.

The argument is direct: the governance frameworks currently available were not built for this population, and the frameworks that would be appropriate do not yet exist in usable form.

That hypothesis is supported. The evidence across six compliance frameworks, three primary sectors, and a consistent body of market and adoption research establishes that the gap is structural, not conjunctural. It exists not because organizations are negligent, but because the frameworks that would tell them what questions to ask (at procurement, at contract review, at product update stages) have not been written. The NIST AI RMF requires a Govern function.
ISO 42001 requires a management system. The EU AI Act requires conformity assessments. None of those prerequisites are realistic for the IT director who also manages the helpdesk, handles vendor renewals, and is on-call for dispatch system outages.

The clearest illustration of the problem is the scenario this population already faces: a county 911 communications center whose CAD vendor adds an AI-assisted feature through a software update. The county did not make an AI procurement decision. They accepted an update. The CJIS compliance question (does this AI component route CJI through an external API under AC-20?) was never asked, because no accessible framework specified it as a required question. That is the governance gap. Not a failure of intent, but a failure of infrastructure that does not yet exist.

This paper maps that terrain and delivers a verdict. It does not propose legislation, does not claim to resolve the open questions it identifies, and does not pretend the regulatory landscape it describes will look the same in eighteen months. What it does is source the evidence, name the gaps, and give the reader something to act on: a compliance crosswalk showing where AI-specific guidance exists, and where it doesn’t, across every major framework this population operates under, and four vendor triage questions that cost nothing and create a paper trail before an audit requires one. The organizations standing at this intersection deserve at least a starting point. This paper is one.

title: The Applicability of Utilitarianism to Ethical Decision-Making in Organizational Information Management

detail.title: The Applicability of Utilitarianism to Ethical Decision-Making in Organizational Information Management

declarations.funderStatement: The research was wholly funded by the researchers, who are all postgraduate students of the Information Technology Education department of the University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development.

detail.abstract: This article takes a closer look at how utilitarianism can be applied to ethical decision-making in the realm of organizational information management. The key question it tackles is whether a consequentialist approach, which aims for the greatest good for the greatest number, can effectively steer decisions related to privacy, surveillance, data governance, information security, algorithmic decision-making, and the use of artificial intelligence within organizations. The study employs a narrative literature review methodology, bolstered by normative analysis. It brings together peer-reviewed literature on utilitarianism, computer and information ethics, workplace monitoring, privacy, and automated decision-making, alongside authoritative governance and regulatory sources like the ACM Code of Ethics, OECD privacy principles, NIST riskmanagement frameworks, GDPR legal architecture, and recent industry risk reports. The findings suggest that utilitarianism is still quite appealing in organizational information management due to its practicality, focus on outcomes, scalability, and alignment with risk-based governance. It supports investments in information security, fraud prevention, breach response, and certain welldefined forms of monitoring when the overall benefits are significant and clear. However, the review also highlights that utilitarian reasoning can become ethically shaky when harms are hard to quantify, when benefits are unevenly distributed, when vulnerable minorities face disproportionate burdens, or when claims of efficiency mask violations of privacy, autonomy, transparency, and fairness. In contexts like employee surveillance and AI-driven automated decision-making, a strictly utilitarian stance can justify intrusive or discriminatory practices if organizations prioritize productivity and risk reduction over dignity, voice, and due process. The article makes the case that while utilitarianism has its merits, it can't stand alone. It's most effective when integrated into a hybrid governance model that weaves together welfare analysis with rights-based limitations, procedural fairness, accountability, transparency, proportionality, and human oversight. In conclusion, the paper suggests a practical ethical decision-making framework for managing organizational information, where utilitarian assessment remains a key decision-making tool, but isn't the only moral benchmark to consider.

title: Go Ninja, Go Ninja, Go! How Superstars Influence Content Liquidity on Live Platforms
affiliations: , University of Mannheim - Business School and George Mason University - Department of Information Systems and Operations Management

detail.title: Go Ninja, Go Ninja, Go! How Superstars Influence Content Liquidity on Live Platforms
detail.abstract: Live platforms such as Twitch and YouTube Live rely on independent creators to provide content when viewer demand arises, making content liquidity a central challenge. Because platforms do not directly control production, liquidity depends on whether decentralized creators choose to stream at the right time. Superstar creators complicate this process. They may increase liquidity by attracting audiences to the platform, but they may also reduce it by concentrating attention and discouraging others from broadcasting. We examine this tension by studying whether creators reallocate supply when superstar presence changes unexpectedly. Using Twitch data, we examine unanticipated absences of the superstar streamer Ninja by comparing days when he was expected to stream but did not with days when he streamed as usual. Results show that creators respond to his absence by increasing both their likelihood of streaming and duration of their broadcasts. This response is concentrated among close substitutes and occurs during Ninja's usual streaming hours, suggesting that creators strategically shift supply to capture newly available viewer demand. These results show that superstar presence can suppress content liquidity by reducing other creators' incentives to broadcast, although not permanently. When superstars are temporarily absent, decentralized creators rapidly adjust supply, preserving platform liquidity.

title: Operational AI Fabric: A Unified Runtime Architecture for Governed Enterprise AI Execution

detail.title: Operational AI Fabric: A Unified Runtime Architecture for Governed Enterprise AI Execution

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is Co-founder of Aion, the organization behind the system discussed in this paper. The manuscript reflects an architectural and practice-based perspective informed by anonymized enterprise deployments conducted in contexts associated with the author’s organization. This relationship is disclosed in the interest of transparency.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This work does not report research involving patients, human subjects, or identifiable participant data. The manuscript is based on architectural analysis and anonymized enterprise deployment cases presented under confidentiality constraints. No ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This work did not receive external research funding. It was developed independently by the author in the context of the author’s professional activity.

detail.abstract:
Recent advances in artificial intelligence have significantly improved model capabilities, yet enterprise adoption remains constrained by system architecture rather than model performance. In most deployments, AI, automation, data processing, and governance are implemented as separate components, resulting in fragmented systems that are difficult to scale, govern, and maintain.

This paper argues that these limitations stem from a common architectural assumption: AI systems are designed as pipelines, where reasoning, execution, and validation occur as sequential and loosely coupled steps.

We introduce the concept of an Operational AI Fabric, a unified runtime architecture in which AI is treated as an executable workload within a distributed system. In this model, orchestration, execution, and governance are integrated into a continuous control loop, enabling real-time evaluation, adaptive behavior, and policy-driven execution.

The architecture combines a composable orchestration layer, a distributed worker fabric, a dynamic control plane, and an embedded governance loop. Through anonymized enterprise deployments across banking, financial services, and global operations contexts, we report case-based operational evidence of improvements in implementation speed, operational efficiency, and runtime reliability.

The findings suggest that the primary barrier to scalable enterprise AI is not model capability, but system design. The Operational AI Fabric represents a shift from AI as a function to AI as an operational system, enabling organizations to build and govern executable intelligence at scale.

This shift has direct implications for enterprise adoption, particularly in regulated environments where auditability, execution control, and policy enforcement are critical. By integrating governance into the execution layer, organizations can reduce operational risk while maintaining system adaptability.

The empirical observations presented are derived from anonymized production deployments subject to confidentiality constraints and should therefore be interpreted as practice-based evidence supporting the architectural argument, rather than as results from a controlled comparative study.

title: Real-Time API Orchestration in Live Voice AI Systems: Architecture and Performance of Action-Capable Conversational Agents Across Enterprise Application Ecosystems

detail.title: Real-Time API Orchestration in Live Voice AI Systems: Architecture and Performance of Action-Capable Conversational Agents Across Enterprise Application Ecosystems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence that imitates human voice is quickly transforming into systems that can naturally converse with humans in context. Nonetheless, the vast majority of implementations are solely passive in nature, meaning that they only convey/provide information, and cannot perform tasks in the real world. In the enterprise domain, this logic makes sense; a voice AI does not add value operationally or strategically when it simply talks or conveys information. It engages and executes tasks within a system network. We propose a realtime on-the-fly API orchestration architecture for Actionable Voice AI Systems. It suggests a framework for evaluation driven by reliability based on execution and not based on the language or quality of conversation. It uses an experimental research design and is based on simulation. A test environment that simulates a customer relationship management (CRM) environment is what sets up the enterprise use case. The voice agent receives queries from the user and performs actions in the CRM system. The voice agent can also successfully execute multi-turn workflows. The voice agent's performance is rated using system-level metrics including latency, task success rate. The results indicate a marked distinction between voice AI systems that are passive and those that are active. While passive systems had lower latency, they were limited in completing the task and had a very high functional failure rate. On the other hand, action-capable ones managed their failure better but they had a much higher success rate albeit with a moderately higher response delay. The results highlight the fact that orchestration is essential for reliable execution and overall stability. The research proposes a structured classification framework to evaluate the dependability of API interactions. Enterprises with low growth rates require greater orchestration quality. The effectiveness of a voice AI system is determined not just by intent detection, but also by its ability to reliably execute intent in the wild.

title: PharmAI: An AI-Driven Pharmacy Management System -A UML-Based Approach
affiliations: Sinhgad Institute of Management and Sinhgad Institute of Management, Pune

detail.title: PharmAI: An AI-Driven Pharmacy Management System -A UML-Based Approach
detail.abstract: This research paper focuses on the analysis and design of an intelligent Pharmacy Management System named PharmAI, integrated with AI-based features to improve pharmacy operations. In modern healthcare environments, pharmacies play a critical role in managing medicines, inventory, billing, and customer interactions. Traditional pharmacy systems often face challenges such as manual errors, inefficient inventory tracking, lack of real-time data, and poor customer service. This study identifies these issues and proposes a smart, automated solution using modern technologies and system design methodologies. The research presents a detailed system design using UML diagrams, including use case, class, activity, sequence, and deployment diagrams, to model the structure and behavior of the system. The proposed system includes modules such as user management, medicine management, inventory tracking, supplier management, billing, sales history, and reporting. Additionally, an AI-based module is incorporated to provide predictive insights, assist in decision-making, and enhance operational efficiency. The system also supports pharmacist functionalities such as billing, medicine search, inventory checking, sales tracking, and customer feedback management. The integration of AI features helps in predicting medicine demand, improving stock management, and providing intelligent recommendations. The findings of this study highlight the importance of automation and intelligent systems in pharmacy management. The proposed PharmAI system improves accuracy, reduces workload, enhances transparency, and delivers a better user experience for both administrators and pharmacists. This work contributes to the advancement of smart healthcare solutions by combining traditional management systems with AI-driven capabilities.

title: Global Business Information Systems Today: Policy Recommendation

detail.title: Global Business Information Systems Today: Policy Recommendation
detail.abstract: Today, global business information systems are critical for gathering, processing, and distributing data that helps businesses make informed decisions. From multinational companies to educational institutions, information management systems help automate routine tasks, reduce or eliminate errors, and provide real-time data analytics that enable leaders to make informed, strategic choices rather than guesswork. Moreover, it also integrates communication, data management, and internal operational processes. Study shows that organizations that invest heavily in information technology and use information systems strategically and extensively gain a competitive advantage by improving operational efficiency, supporting decision-making, enhancing customer relationship management, ensuring data security, timely regulatory compliance, and enabling innovation. This chapter discusses how the key concepts of information systems in business strategy, digital transformation, globalization, and IT-driven business models apply to modern organizations, using the Asian College of Science and Technology (ACSAT) as a practical example in the context section

title: What Happens After the Signal: The Missing Layer in AI-Supported Decision-Making
affiliations: Indiana University, Indianapolis - Indiana University Indianapolis and Indiana University, Indianapolis - Indiana University Indianapolis

detail.title: What Happens After the Signal: The Missing Layer in AI-Supported Decision-Making

keywords: Justice Decision Observability AI Governance Human-in-the-Loop Decision-Making Execution Layer Accountability Corrections Courts Supervision Public Safety

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly deployed across justice environments to generate alerts, classifications, and risk signals intended to support human decision-making. Existing governance frameworks focus heavily on system design, validation, and pre-deployment oversight, while post-deployment monitoring emphasizes outcomes and system performance.

However, a critical layer remains insufficiently defined: what occurs between the moment a system produces a signal and the moment institutional authority is exercised.

This paper defines that gap as the execution-layer decision space the operational environment in which human actors interpret, prioritize, defer, or act upon system outputs under real-world conditions. It argues that without structured mechanisms to document and reconstruct decision pathways, institutions remain unable to fully explain, defend, or systematically improve decisions made in AI-supported environments.

Positioned within the Justice Decision Observability™ (JDO™) canon, this work establishes execution-layer governance as a distinct and necessary component of AI oversight in justice systems.

This paper is part of the Justice Decision Observability™ (JDO™) Canon Series (JDO-2026-000 through JDO-2026-015), a structured body of work defining execution-layer governance in AI-supported systems.

title: The Governance Tuple: An Atomic Record for Auditable Agentic AI Decision-Making

detail.title: The Governance Tuple: An Atomic Record for Auditable Agentic AI Decision-Making

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Reuben Bowlby is the founder and sole member of HUMMBL, LLC, which develops AI governance tooling. The governance tuple formalized in this paper is implemented in HUMMBL's open-source founder-mode platform. No external funding, grants, or third-party compensation influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study involves no human participants, patient data, or animal subjects. The research is purely theoretical and computational.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. All work was self-funded by the author.

detail.abstract: Current AI governance frameworks produce documentation but not proof. A system that logs its decisions, maintains an audit trail, or records compliance checks has produced evidence that logging happened-not evidence that governance happened. We argue this distinction is not semantic but architectural: proof of governance requires an atomic, tamper-evident record that links the authority authorizing a decision (CONTRACT), the delegation chain establishing who acted and under what constraints (DCT-Delegation Capability Token), and the evidence of what was actually done and at what cost (EVIDENCE). We call this three-field structure a governance tuple. We formalize the governance tuple, prove four properties it satisfies that append-only logs cannot satisfy independently, and show that sequential tuples form auditable chains in which hash-linking creates tamper-evident retrospective accountability even when each individual decision appeared correct at the time it was made. We ground our analysis in a deployed implementation-the Intelligent Delegation Profile (IDP)-whose core data structures (DelegationContext , DelegationCapabilityToken , GovernanceEntry) directly instantiate the tuple schema. We connect the tuple to two companion governance layers: Base120 (reasoning operator governance) and VERUM (append-only audit sovereignty). The governance tuple is the bridge between them-the artifact that records which reasoning was authorized, by whom, and what it cost. We evaluate the tuple against existing audit frameworks and show that it satisfies five accountability properties that log-based approaches cannot.

title: Adaptive Trust Decay Models for AI-Driven Information Security Systems - A Continuous Validation

detail.title: Adaptive Trust Decay Models for AI-Driven Information Security Systems - A Continuous Validation
detail.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in modern information systems to support and automate organizational decision-making.

While these systems improve efficiency, existing security models assume that trust in AI systems, data sources, and users remains constant once approval is granted. In practice, system behaviour, data quality, and human actions change over time, which can reduce reliability and increase risk.

This research addresses a critical gap with Adaptive Trust Decay Models for AI-driven information systems, where trust is treated as a dynamic and measurable security factor.

Using a Design Science Research approach, the study aims to design and evaluate an Information Systems Security Framework that adjusts trust levels based on observable system behaviour, data quality, and human intervention patterns.

The expected outcome will improve security governance, better decision reliability, and stronger organizational resilience against evolving threats in AI-enabled information systems.

title: AI-Driven Cloud Security Frameworks for SMEs

detail.title: AI-Driven Cloud Security Frameworks for SMEs
detail.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are moving critical workloads, data, development pipelines, and customer-facing services into public and hybrid cloud environments at the same time that the cyber threat landscape is being reshaped by identity-centric attacks, software supply chain compromise, and the rapid operationalization of generative artificial intelligence. This paper presents a broad, coverage-oriented review of AI-driven cloud security frameworks for SMEs from 2023 to March 2026. Rather than testing a single hypothesis, the study organizes the current landscape around SME constraints, cloud-native attack surfaces, recent regulatory developments, and the practical role of artificial intelligence in threat detection, triage, prioritization, response, and governance. Recent official guidance and peer-reviewed literature show that SMEs remain disproportionately affected by skills shortages, fragmented tooling, and compliance burden, while attackers continue to exploit weak credentials, misconfigurations, exposed assets, and human trust. At the same time, AI-enabled security operations are becoming more viable for smaller organizations through managed telemetry pipelines, cloud-native application protection platforms, anomaly detection, and LLM-assisted security workflows. Based on the review, the paper proposes a vendor-neutral reference framework for SMEs built on five layers: telemetry and asset visibility, AI analytics, policy and access control, orchestrated response, and governance and assurance. The paper also examines implementation barriers including model drift, privacy risk, cost control, false positives, data sovereignty, and adversarial abuse of AI systems. Finally, it identifies research opportunities in real-time virtual machine protection, explainable risk scoring, cross-cloud identity graphing, privacy-preserving analytics, and blockchain-assisted evidence trails. The paper concludes that AI can materially improve SME cloud security when deployed as a disciplined augmentation layer inside zero-trust, cloud-native, and compliance-aware architectures rather than as a standalone replacement for security fundamentals.

title: Perceived Structural Value and Tension Blind Spots: Modeling V p in the ZTH Framework

detail.title: Perceived Structural Value and Tension Blind Spots: Modeling V p in the ZTH Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants or personal data and therefore does not require ethical approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
In tension-based systems, structural value V may differ markedly from how decision-makers perceive value. This fourth paper in the ZTH series introduces perceived structural value Vp and analyzes its misalignment with V. Perception is modeled as a visibility-weighted projection of the six-dimensional tension vector τ = (R, Q, I, C, D, Ri) onto a perceived vector τ̂. Applying the same promoter-inhibitor operator to τ̂ yields a perceived value Vp. Misalignment between V and Vp is measured by differences ΔV and ratios M = Vp / V. We define several perception regimes based on visibility profiles, including full-hexagon, QCD-centered, risk-blind and impact-blind views, and show how they generate systematic patterns of overestimation or underestimation. A stylized numerical example illustrates how the same structural state can lead to divergent perceived values under different regimes. This provides a formal basis for analyzing blind spots and for extending ZTH to perceived value trajectories Vp(t).

This paper is also available on Zenodo (DOI): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18707568

title: Autonomous Cyber Defense: Integrating Intelligent Automation and Zero Trust for Resilient Cybersecurity Operations

detail.title: Autonomous Cyber Defense: Integrating Intelligent Automation and Zero Trust for Resilient Cybersecurity Operations
detail.abstract: Cybersecurity has evolved into a discipline that requires speed, consistency, and operational discipline. Traditional approaches based on manual monitoring, static rules, and perimeter defenses are no longer sufficient against modern threats that are automated, persistent, and increasingly adaptive. At the center of this transformation is the use of automation to handle repetitive and timesensitive tasks. Technologies such as Python and PowerShell play a critical role in enabling organizations to monitor systems, analyze activity, and respond to threats in a consistent manner. However, automation alone is not enough. It must be guided by intelligent analysis and supported by clear control structures. This paper argues that organizations must combine automation with data-driven decision-making and continuous verification practices to create resilient cybersecurity operations.

title: A Comprehensive Research Framework for Bitcoin’s Energy Use: Fundamentals, Economic Rationale, and a Pinch of Thermodynamics

detail.title: A Comprehensive Research Framework for Bitcoin’s Energy Use: Fundamentals, Economic Rationale, and a Pinch of Thermodynamics

publicationDetails.detailsText: Blockchain: Research and Applications, volume 4, issue 3, 2023[10.1016/j.bcra.2023.100149]

detail.abstract: The energy use of Bitcoin is fiercely debated among academics, practitioners, and the general public. This debate is often biased and characterized by a lack of understanding. Therefore, I start this paper with a discussion of the fundamentals of Bitcoin, which includes the clarification of widely held misconceptions. Next, I illustrate how Bitcoin is related to energy and describe the underlying incentive mechanism. In the main body of the paper, I discuss various components of Bitcoin's energy use, including the amount, composition, and geographical distribution of the energy, as well as emerging positive and negative effects. These components are then combined into a comprehensive framework that provides a solid foundation for future academic research and presents practitioners with the big picture of how and why Bitcoin requires energy and whether this can be justified from an environmental point of view.

title: Time Series Forecasting of Walmart Weekly Sales
affiliations: and Sinhgad Institute of Management, Pune

detail.title: Time Series Forecasting of Walmart Weekly Sales
detail.abstract: Sales forecasting is a vital function in retail for improving inventory control, supply chain efficiency, and strategic planning. This study focuses on predicting Walmart's weekly sales using time series forecasting techniques applied to structured historical data. The dataset includes weekly sales records along with external variables such as temperature, fuel prices, consumer price index (CPI), unemployment, and holiday indicators, which influence sales patterns. The research involves data preprocessing and exploratory analysis to identify trends, seasonality, and relationships among variables. Statistical models, particularly Auto Regressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), are used to capture temporal dependencies and forecast future sales. Model performance is evaluated using metrics like Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). The results show that time series models effectively identify seasonal trends and provide reliable forecasts. The study highlights the importance of incorporating external factors and maintaining consistent time-based data for accurate predictions in retail analytics.

detail.abstract: Community-based elderly care increasingly depends on digital communication environments in which messaging tools, reminder modules, and platform-mediated coordination systems continuously generate interaction records. However, existing studies have paid limited attention to how these non-clinical communication traces can be structured as computable variables for analyzing older adults' social participation. Using longitudinal data from 36 communities in 12 U.S. states, this study builds a three-level database covering 1,248 older adults, 624 family caregivers, and 216 service providers, and develops a computational analysis pipeline that integrates interaction-log structuring, temporal event alignment, graph-based relational modeling, multilevel linear modeling, and structural equation modeling. Tool-use intensity, weekly interaction frequency, response latency, session duration, modality composition, and network embeddedness are encoded as measurable digital indicators. The results show that tool-use intensity, weekly interaction frequency, and mixed-mode communication ratio positively predict social participation, whereas response latency shows a negative effect. The indirect effect of communication accessibility through relational trust and expressive efficacy is 0.097, accounting for 27.3% of the total effect. These findings support the optimization of agefriendly communication platforms and participation-oriented community interaction systems from a computer application perspective. Keywords community-based elderly care; non-clinical communication tools; multimodal interaction logging; graph-based relational modeling; social participation; structural equation modeling 1 Introduction Community-based elderly care is increasingly supported by digital platforms, caregiver terminals, reminder systems, and lightweight messaging applications. In this setting, a substantial part of older adults' everyday social interaction is recorded as platform events rather than remaining only in offline contact. This shift creates a new analytical problem for computer applications: how to convert non-clinical communication behaviors into structured data that can be used to explain variation in social participation.Existing studies have mainly focused on health intervention outcomes, formal service delivery, or general social prescribing practices. Far less attention has been given to the computational representation of routine communication traces, such as message exchanges, reminder responses, coordination records, and time-varying relational links. As a result, the digital pathway through which communication tools shape older adults' participation has not been clearly modeled. This study addresses that gap by building a three-level analytical framework linking older adults, family caregivers, and community service contexts. It constructs a unified data-processing pipeline that combines interaction-log structuring, temporal event alignment, graph-based relational modeling, multilevel linear modeling, and structural equation modeling. The analysis focuses on how communication accessibility, encoded from measurable digital indicators, influences social participation directly and indirectly through relational trust and expressive efficacy, and further compares this pathway across digital competence, functional limitation, age band, living arrangement, and community type. 2. title: Computable Trust Architecture: A Formal Framework for Runtime AI Governance

detail.title: Computable Trust Architecture: A Formal Framework for Runtime AI Governance
