detail.title: Η Σκιά του Μέλλοντος (v.2) στην Δημόσια Διοίκηση: Από Παράδοξο σε Εργαλείο Διακυβέρνησης
detail.abstract: Η «σκιά του μέλλοντος», η προσδοκία συνεχούς αλληλεπίδρασης, αναγνωρίζεται ως μηχανισμός προώθησης της συνεργασίας. Ωστόσο, μπορεί παράδοξα να εντείνει τη σύγκρουση, καθώς οι δρώντες ανταγωνίζονται για μελλοντική υπεροχή. Το άρθρο αντιμετωπίζει αυτό το αίνιγμα μέσω συστηματικής ποιοτικής επισκόπησης 101 μελετών. Υποστηρίζουμε ότι η σκιά του μέλλοντος δεν είναι στατική συνθήκη, αλλά ενδογενής μεταβλητή που υπόκειται σε στρατηγική διαμόρφωση. Αναδεικνύουμε τους διαμεσολαβητικούς μηχανισμούς και προτείνουμε ένα νέο, πολυεπίπεδο εννοιολογικό πλαίσιο για τη διάγνωση και διαχείριση της, μετατρέποντάς την από θεωρητικό παράδοξο σε αναλυτικό εργαλείο διακυβέρνησης.

reference: Institute for New Economic Thinking Working Paper Series No. 249
title: Russell's Teapot: Dispatches From the Final Stage of the AI Bubble
affiliations: Delft University of Technology - Department of Economics

detail.title: Russell's Teapot: Dispatches From the Final Stage of the AI Bubble

publicationDetails.detailsText: Institute for New Economic Thinking Working Paper Series No. 249
publicationDetails.journalName: Institute for New Economic Thinking Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Four red flags signal that the U.S. economy has reached the peak of the AI bubble: (i) escalating liquidity shortages for key AI firms, unable to recoup rising capital and operational costs; (ii) growing competition and a building AI price war; (iii) a budding private credit crisis, related to its overexposure to software firms and AI data centers; and (iv) stagflation, caused by Trump's tariffs and the Iran war and leading to higher energy costs and higher interest rates. However, even absent these headwinds, the AI boom cannot be sustained, because the aggregate net productivity impacts of the novel AI tools will be disappointingly small, will peter out rather quickly over time and will not be large enough to justify the stratospheric capital expenditures on AI models and AI infrastructure. The AI-driven 'white-collar bloodbath' will not happen, because even though AI tools will replace some tasks, these will also create new (often unproductive overhead) tasks, and augment and transform occupations, rather than completely destroy them. The productivity impacts of AI will disappoint, because AI tools do not just have positive effects on labor productivity, but also generate significant negative impacts — mostly because the use of AI creates new tasks and jobs, because the AI tools have to be monitored, supervised and curated, as the AI tools generate errors, slop, cybersecurity risks, brittle code and mounting technical debt that could kill businesses and institutions if it concerns mission-critical activities.

title: Assessing the Reliability of Using R-Squared for Selecting the Sector Index in Securities Litigation Event Studies

detail.title: Assessing the Reliability of Using R-Squared for Selecting the Sector Index in Securities Litigation Event Studies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest by any of the coauthors.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding received.

detail.abstract: This study assesses the reliability of the often-used R-squared methodology for selecting an event study industry sector index. The choice of sector index is a highly contested subject of debate between forensic finance experts in securities fraud litigation. An alleged securities fraud may appear to have caused significant damages when the econometrics are conducted with one particular sector index, but may appear to have little or no damages when an alternative sector index is used. The R-squared index selection criterion picks a sector index on the basis of statistical fit, while alternative methods choose based on fundamental considerations or a company's self-identified sector index. This study designs and executes an experiment to gauge how often the R-squared methodology succeeds in selecting the correct sector index in a controlled setting. We run and compare regressions and event studies for each Dow Jones Industrial Average stock, using alternatively each of the ten S&P Dow Jones high-level industry indices, one of which is deemed to be the correct index by S&P Dow Jones. We find that the R-squared methodology failed to identify the correct index more than 50% of the time. Moreover, the incorrect but higher R-squared models more often than not produced a lower event day absolute residual return when compared to the correct model, which could bias damage estimates downward. This study reviews the statistics literature and econometric theory that explains this high failure rate.

title: The Inniss Data Nullius Framework: A Legal and Institutional Instrument for Contesting Vacant Data Claims in Global South Digital Governance

detail.title: The Inniss Data Nullius Framework: A Legal and Institutional Instrument for Contesting Vacant Data Claims in Global South Digital Governance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: There was no funding .

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Inniss Data Nullius Framework-a legal-doctrinal instrument identifying and contesting the treatment of Global South data as ownerless, jurisdiction-free, and freely appropriable. Drawing on the colonial doctrine of terra nullius and its repudiation in Mabo v Queensland (No 2) [1992] HCA 23, the framework argues that digital infrastructures reproduce an analogous fiction of vacancy over data, erasing the authorship, sovereignty, and economic value of data generated by Global South states. Three pillars operationalize this fiction: legal instruments circumventing local jurisdiction; technical architectures removing data from regulatory reach; and institutional silence, perpetuated by the Execution Gap-the failure to translate governance commitments into operational reality. Legal-doctrinal and policy-actionable where data colonialism scholarship is sociological, the framework advances the Principle of Data Reversion and recommendations for governments, regional bodies, and judicial institutions in the Caribbean and Global South, filling a documented gap in digital sovereignty literature.

title: Ethical Dissonance Theory (EDT): A Multi-Level Framework Explaining Psychological and Institutional Drivers of Scientific Conformity (Original Conceptual Framework and Authorship Record Preprint)

detail.title: Ethical Dissonance Theory (EDT): A Multi-Level Framework Explaining Psychological and Institutional Drivers of Scientific Conformity (Original Conceptual Framework and Authorship Record Preprint)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. No personal, financial, or institutional relationships influenced the development of this conceptual preprint.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This preprint presents a conceptual theoretical framework and does not involve human participants, clinical data, or empirical research. Therefore, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The development of Ethical Dissonance Theory (EDT) was conducted independently without financial support from any organisation.

detail.abstract:
Scientific objectivity is widely upheld as a foundational principle of modern research, yet individuals operating within scientific systems remain subject to psychological, social, and institutional pressures. This preprint introduces Ethical Dissonance Theory (EDT), a multi‑level conceptual framework explaining how tensions arise between the normative ideals of objectivity and the practical realities of academic life. EDT integrates cognitive dissonance, moral disengagement, social conformity, and institutional reinforcement into a unified explanatory model of scientific behaviour.

The framework proposes that ethical dissonance is not an anomaly but a predictable outcome of interacting psychological and structural forces. By outlining the core architecture and theoretical propositions of EDT, this preprint establishes the original formulation of the model and its relevance for understanding conformity, bias, and psychological strain within academia.

This document serves to establish authorship, priority, and conceptual ownership of Ethical Dissonance Theory (EDT) while reserving full theoretical elaboration for future publications.

Affiliation clarification: This preprint is an independent conceptual work and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or produced under the supervision of Auckland University of Technology or any other institution. The author’s current university enrollment is listed for biographical accuracy only.

title: The factors affecting on non-performing loans in selected branches of Sepah Bank

detail.title: The factors affecting on non-performing loans in selected branches of Sepah Bank
detail.abstract: The banking system in Iran has always been faced by non-performing loans. Non-performing loans have many consequences such as the lack of liquidity and reduction in the volume of credits in Iran’s banking system. Based on the importance and the role of the non-performing loans in the banking system, this study investigates the impact of some banking and economic factors affecting on them in various branches of Sepah Bank in the framework of panel data in the period of 2004-2014. The results indicate that banking variable such as total facilities, risk index, and bank size and the economic variable such as loans interest rate and inflation rate have a positive and significant effect on the non-performing loans of Sepah Bank while economic growth has a negative and significant effect.

title: Comparative Conflict of Laws between Form and Substance
affiliations: University of Turin - Faculty of Law, SciencesPo, Ecole de Droit

detail.title: Comparative Conflict of Laws between Form and Substance
detail.abstract:
This paper develops a comparative and quantitative framework for analyzing conflict of laws through the classical divide between form and substance. Moving beyond traditional doctrinal taxonomies, it reconstructs the field through a set of functional variables—autonomy versus sovereignty, flexibility versus certainty, global harmonization versus local adaptation, substantive justice versus procedural regularity, and market versus state orientation.


Drawing on a cross-jurisdictional case analysis (including English, U.S., EU, Chinese, and mixed systems), the article proposes two ideal-type models: the “Cathedral of Codes”, associated with civil law systems, and “Pilgrim’s Progress”, associated with common law reasoning. These models are further extended toward theoretical extremes—Free Market Nomos and Codified State Fortress—to capture the structural tensions of contemporary legal orders.


The paper introduces a quantitative methodology based on Euclidean distance to measure the relative positioning of legal systems along these dimensions. The results suggest a moderate but significant divergence (approximately 40%) between civil and common law traditions, coupled with an underlying convergence driven by globalization and economic pressures.


The core argument is that the real divide in conflict of laws is not formal (sources of law), but substantive: legal systems differ in how they balance flexibility and certainty, autonomy and state control. Ultimately, both traditions operate within an intermediate zone, optimizing different forms of economic efficiency depending on market conditions.

title: Dottin | Multi-Asset Commodities Volatility Portfolio

detail.title: Dottin | Multi-Asset Commodities Volatility Portfolio
detail.abstract: We present a systematic equal-risk long-short volatility and relative value portfolio across a basket of commodity underlyings. The strategy monetizes the persistent volatility risk premium embedded in commodity options by selling delta-hedged straddles while selffinancing tail protection through long out-of-the-money put positions. Position sizing is conditioned on an inventory-based signal derived from rolling five-year z-scores of U.S. commodity inventory data, allowing the portfolio to scale exposure dynamically in response to physical market conditions. In addition to the directional volatility sleeve, the portfolio incorporates relative value trades between structurally linked commodities: WTI versus Brent crude oil and corn versus soybeans. These positions isolate persistent gaps in implied volatility pricing that arise from differences in physical market structure, inventory elasticity, and demand composition. Back-tested over a ten-year period, the risk-weighted portfolio produced a cumulative return of approximately 120%, translating to an annualized return of 8% with 9% annualized volatility and a Sharpe ratio of 0.9. The results demonstrate that combining volatility carry with cross-commodity relative value produces a diversified, regime-resilient return stream with limited drawdowns.

title: Kalem Değiştiren Maliyet: Akıllı Telefon ve Mobil Veri Paketi Kanalında Tamamlayıcı Enflasyon

title: Financial Development and Renewable Energy Technology Development in Different Sectors: Application of Panel Tobit Model
affiliations: , University of Mazandaran (UMZ) and University of Mazandaran (UMZ)

detail.title: Financial Development and Renewable Energy Technology Development in Different Sectors: Application of Panel Tobit Model
detail.abstract: The importance of renewable energies in sustainable development, greenhouse gas reduction and increase energy supply security on the one hand and required high level of financing for Renewable energy projects, on the other hand, have enhanced the role and importance of financial development in renewable energy deployment. Due to the importance of this issue, this study tried to evaluate the impact of financial development in the stock market, credit market and whole financial markets on renewable energy technologies (in the four energy sectors including biomass, hydropower, wind and solar) over the period 2002 till 2015, based on Tobit regression in developed and developing countries. Based on the Results, financial development has a significant effect on renewable technology development regardless of which kind of renewable energy was used. It also led to a reduction in environmental pollution and climate changes, especially in developed countries. The results also indicated that stock market development, credit market development and whole financial market development has the most impact on the renewable technology installation capacity development of solar, biomass, wind and hydropower energies in developed countries, respectively. While financial market development has the most impact on technology installation capacity development of wind, biomass and solar energies in developing countries.

detail.title: AI-Based Slow and Fast Learner Identification System with Personalized Course Recommendation
detail.abstract: Traditional educational systems often struggle to identify individual learning patterns in students, leading to a one-size-fits-all approach that fails both fast and slow learners. Slow learners receive insufficient support, while fast learners remain under-challenged, ultimately impacting overall academic outcomes. Built to address these gaps, this AI-Based Slow and Fast Learner Detection System is a web-based platform designed to assess students through quizzes, analyse their performance patterns, and classify them as slow or fast learners using intelligent algorithms. Instead of relying solely on teachers' subjective judgment, the system provides data-driven insights - tracking quiz scores, time taken per question, accuracy rates, and engagement levels in real time. From quiz attempt to performance analysis, each step follows a structured pipeline, where educators can monitor student progress and personalize their teaching strategies. Past attempts stay stored and ready for longitudinal trend analysis with just a few clicks. The platform incorporates machine learning-based classification to differentiate learning speeds, supporting targeted interventions. Tests show improved classification accuracy, reduced teacher workload, and enhanced student engagement among daily users. The results suggest strong relevance for modernizing traditional assessment models widely found in schools and colleges.

title: Primum Non Nocere: The Unintended Consequences of Financial Reporting Frequency in Healthcare
affiliations: Vanderbilt University - Owen Graduate School of Management, Duke University - Fuqua School of Business,  and Santa Clara University - Accounting

detail.title: Primum Non Nocere: The Unintended Consequences of Financial Reporting Frequency in Healthcare

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted without external funding.

detail.abstract: Does a change in financial reporting frequency affect managerial decisions in the healthcare sector? The answer is yes, and notably, such decisions can have detrimental societal outcomes. Using a regulatory change that required Massachusetts hospitals to move from annual to quarterly financial reporting, we document that more frequent reporting shifts managerial attention and resource allocation toward near-term financial outcomes. Following the mandate, hospitals earn higher profitability and improve operating efficiency. Further analysis reveals that these outcomes stem from scaling back labor and capital investment, rather than from improved revenues. More importantly, these changes are accompanied by a deterioration in patient care quality, reflected in higher patient mortality rates, increased hospital readmissions, and lower patient satisfaction. Our paper highlights a negative externality associated with a well-intentioned change in the frequency of financial statement reporting.

publicationDetails.detailsText:

detail.abstract: Adoption of agricultural technologies is crucial for sustainable development, yet adoption of many relevant technologies remains low, especially among smallholder farmers in Africa. While there is an extensive literature aimed at understanding drivers of adoption, intra-household factors have received much less attention. In this study, we examine the relationship between spousal cooperation, an important intra-household factor, and the adoption of agricultural technologies among smallholder farmers in Cameroon. Specifically, we focus on improved seed varieties, inorganic fertilizers, intercropping, and minimum tillage as technologies. We combine survey and lab-in-the-field experimental data and employ multivariate probit models to account for simultaneous adoption. We also estimate associations between cooperation and the number of technologies adopted. The results suggest that spousal cooperation is positively associated with the adoption of improved varieties and intercropping. However, we find no associations between cooperation and adoption of inorganic fertilizers and minimum tillage, although the coefficients are positive. We also find that cooperation is positively associated with the number of technologies adopted. Lastly, we find interesting complementarities between the various technologies. Our findings suggest that promoting spousal cooperation could serve as an important leverage point for the adoption of modern agricultural technologies.

title: Resolvent Cascade Exposure: A Unied Node-Level Risk Score for Networked Systems with Cross-Domain Validation

detail.title: Resolvent Cascade Exposure: A Unied Node-Level Risk Score for Networked Systems with Cross-Domain Validation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal relationships that could have influenced this work. This research was conducted independently without external funding.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses only publicly available, aggregated data from the FDIC (bank call reports), Our World in Data (COVID-19 statistics), OpenSky Network (flight data), and DeFi Llama (protocol TVL). No human subjects, patient data, or personally identifiable information are involved.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific funding. The work was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: We introduce a node-level risk score derived from resolvent analysis of linear cascade dynamics on networks. The score, Ξ(k) = [(I-β Ŵ)-1 • r] k , measures the total cascade exposure of each node by propagating an initial shock vector r through a fragility-weighted interaction operator Ŵ. The formulation yields two analytically tractable limits: when the eective coupling β eff is well below the critical threshold β eff = 1, the score is dominated by the direct shock (seed); when β eff approaches or exceeds the threshold, it converges to eigenvector centrality of the network. We validate the model on three independent real-world domains without recalibrating the functional form. In the 2023 U.S. regional banking crisis (subcritical, β eff = 0.87), the resolvent score achieves Spearman ρ = 0.728 against deposit outows, outperforming the best single-feature baseline (ρ = 0.671) and correctly identifying all three failed institutions in the top three ranks. In the COVID-19 rst wave, the theory-implied coupling places the model in the seed-dominated limit (β eff = 0.001), where the resolvent (connected-country Spearman ρ = 0.516) closely tracks the initial case seed; eigenvector centrality of the same air-trac network is a stronger predictor (ρ = 0.683), consistent with the theoretical prediction that centrality dominates at higher coupling. A pre-registered test on DeFi protocol cascades (Terra/Luna, May 2022) yields a negative result (ρ = 0.022), identifying a structural boundary: the framework requires network-mediated contagion and does not apply to common-substrate failures where a simple chain-exposure predictor dominates (ρ = 0.408). The basic reproduction number R 0 is shown to be a special case of the system-level threshold under homogeneous fragility. The exact calibration of β from rst principles remains an open problem; the COVID result demonstrates that this gap materially aects regime selection.

detail.title: Beyond CAGR: Sum-Matching CAGR for Uneven Growth Series

detail.abstract: CAGR is a simple and useful way to compress a growth history into a single endpoint-to-endpoint rate. However, it can represent uneven windows poorly because it does not use the observations between the first and last dates. This paper defines Sum-Matching CAGR (SM-CAGR), a cumulative-equivalent annualized growth summary. Given a positive starting observation and an equally spaced series, SM-CAGR is the constant annual rate whose smooth compounding path reproduces the same cumulative or weighted cumulative exposure as the observed path. SM-CAGR retains CAGR's compound annual-rate format while changing the matching object from terminal value to full-window cumulative exposure. If CAGR summarizes the change from starting value to terminal value, SM-CAGR summarizes the cumulative exposure realized over the selected window. Discounted SM-CAGR matches present-value exposure instead of raw cumulative exposure, making timing differences visible. The statistic is especially suited to level or flow variables for which cumulative exposure over time is meaningful, such as market forecasts, subscribers or users, shipments, capacity, revenue, earnings, free cash flow, and dividends. For ratio-type variables, the unweighted statistic is a path-exposure summary unless an explicit exposure base is used; when an economic denominator such as revenue, invested capital, principal, or market size is available, weighted SM-CAGR can express that exposure directly. Illustrations using Burford Capital, Meta Platforms, and Netflix show how CAGR, SM-CAGR, and discounted SM-CAGR can be read together to distinguish endpoint dependence, cumulative full-window delivery, and timing.

title: Stablecoin-based Remittance and Adoption in India Efficiency, Barriers, and Financial Inclusion Impact
affiliations: Parul Institute of Engineering and Technology, Parul University

detail.title: Stablecoin-based Remittance and Adoption in India Efficiency, Barriers, and Financial Inclusion Impact
detail.abstract: India received $125 billion in inward remittances in 2023, making it the world's largest recipient of migrant worker transfers. The bulk of these flows traverse traditional channels-SWIFT-based bank wires, money transfer operators such as Western Union, and informal hawala networksthat charge between 5% and 12.66% of transfer value and require one to five business days for settlement. Stablecoin rails, operating on blockchain networks such as Tron (USDT) and Stellar (USDC), complete transfers in seconds at fees below one US dollar, offering a structural cost advantage of four to thirteen times over conventional banking. Yet widespread adoption in India faces compounding barriers: an unresolved regulatory framework under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, persistent last-mile cash-out deficits affecting 52% of the rural population, and the Reserve Bank of India's explicit concern that dollar-pegged stablecoin adoption could trigger currency substitution and erode monetary sovereignty. This paper compares stablecoin rails against traditional remittance channels across cost, speed, and accessibility dimensions; examines India's current regulatory environment; and analyses the financial inclusion implications of stablecoin-based remittance for India's 13 million overseas workers and their rural households. The findings suggest that stablecoins offer meaningful efficiency gains for high-value, urban-recipient corridors, but face structural constraints that limit their near-term applicability to India's financially excluded population without targeted regulatory and infrastructure interventions.

title: Energy, economic growth, inequality, and poverty in Iran

detail.title: Energy, economic growth, inequality, and poverty in Iran

keywords: simultaneous equation system. JEL Classification: Q43

detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationships among energy consumption, economic growth, inequality, and poverty in Iran. We estimate these relationships at both the aggregate and sectoral level using instrumental variables to address endogeneity and simultaneous equation models to enhance efficiency. Results show that decreasing inequality will be beneficial for economic growth, poverty alleviation and energy access. Inequality can negatively affect GDP directly, as well as indirectly through its negative effect on energy consumption. Similarly, inequality can increase poverty both directly as well as indirectly through its negative effect on energy consumption. We also find that increasing energy consumption has multiple benefits: it increases GDP, tends to decrease inequality and decreases poverty. Energy consumption decreases poverty both directly as well as indirectly via its effect on decreasing inequality. Our results therefore suggest that policies to improve energy access are important, and will have the benefits of increasing GDP, decreasing inequality and decreasing poverty.

detail.title: Understanding Firms' AI Efforts and Their Economic Impact

detail.abstract: This paper reviews firm-level data on artificial intelligence and the emerging evidence on AI's economic effects. It argues that measurement is central: different AI datasets capture different objects-including invention versus use, internal capability building versus outsourcing, and realized activity versus investor perceptions-and can therefore lead to different conclusions. The paper develops a framework for choosing among these measures and surveys available data sources on firm AI efforts. It synthesizes evidence on AI's effects on firm growth, valuation, productivity, risk, labor, competition, financial markets and applications. The paper concludes by suggesting some ideas for future research.

detail.abstract: This article examines current issues in the legal regulation of responsibility for violations of subsoil legislation in the Russian Federation. Based on an analysis of legislative acts (the Law of the Russian Federation "On Subsoil," the Code of Administrative Offenses of the Russian Federation, and the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation) and law enforcement practice, the article systematizes the types of legal responsibility: administrative, criminal, and civil. Particular attention is paid to administrative sanctions for environmental offenses, criminal offenses in the field of subsoil use, as well as the role of forensic ecology and forensic environmental expertise in proving the harm caused. The conclusion is drawn that a comprehensive application of all types of responsibility y is necessary to ensure the rational use and protection of subsoil resources.

title: Most-Favored-Nation Clauses as Entry Invitation
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen - School of Management and Economics, University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management, University of Toronto - Institute for Policy Analysis and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Most-Favored-Nation Clauses as Entry Invitation
detail.abstract: Most-Favored-Nation (MFN) clauses are traditionally analyzed as instruments of collusion or foreclosure. We identify a third mechanism in vertical supply contracts: MFNs as commitment devices for strategic entry accommodation. An MFN granted to a major buyer constrains the incumbent's pricing flexibility, transforming a winner-take-all contest into a segmented equilibrium in which a small entrant voluntarily occupies a niche, even when it could costlessly serve the entire market. The mechanism reverses the conclusions of the platform-MFN literature: in physical supply chains, MFNs can invite entry rather than foreclose it. The welfare effects are ambiguous, supporting a rule-of-reason antitrust approach.

This study proposes a quantum-inspired framework to analyze decision-making behavior in financial markets under uncertainty. It introduces the Quantum Cognitive Coherence Index (ICCQ), which measures the interference between rational and emotional components and enables the identification of market stress and crisis phases. title: Symbiotic Supply Chains: Expanding the Scope of Sustainable Supply Chain Management
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, , CEG - IST, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Lisbon - Instituto Superior Técnico

detail.title: Symbiotic Supply Chains: Expanding the Scope of Sustainable Supply Chain Management

declarations.funderStatement: This work is financed by Portuguese funds through the FCT - Foundation for Science and Technology, I.P., under project UID/97/2025 (CEGIST), and Ph.D. grants SFRH/BD/149017/2019 and 2021.09014.BD.

detail.abstract: Supply chains (SCs) face increasing vulnerability due to geopolitical volatility, macroeconomic instability, climate change, technological disruptions, and evolving consumer expectations. In this setting, SCs struggle to balance agility, resilience, and sustainability, as enhancing one often comes at the expense of the others. This study addresses these challenges through the lens of symbiotic supply chains (SymSCs). Our research identifies conceptual and managerial limitations in current definitions of SymSCs, which focus primarily on substitution synergies, where waste or by-products from one entity replace inputs for another. This narrow view overlooks the broader potential of mutualization synergies, where assets such as infrastructure, services, or human resources are shared. To address this gap, we adopt a qualitative multi-methodological approach, combining a literature review, expert brainstorming, and focus group sessions with SC scholars. We make three key contributions. First, we propose an enriched definition of SymSCs that emphasizes resource exchange and sharing, highlighting the interconnectivity between SCs, the dynamic nature of resource flows, and the pivotal role of collaboration. Second, we develop a comprehensive framework to support the strategic and tactical planning of SymSCs, capturing key inputs, decisions, and interactions between SC activities. Third, we outline future research streams to guide further theoretical and practical exploration in this emerging field. Our study demonstrates that rethinking traditional SC practices through a symbiotic perspective can yield significant improvements in SC agility, resilience, and sustainability. These contributions provide conceptual clarity, acknowledge the complexity of such systems, and establish a solid foundation for future decision-support tools.

title: Market Dynamics Across the Value Chain (MDAVC): A Traceable Two-Tier Diagnostic Method for Executional Misalignment Under Institutional Volatility

detail.title: Market Dynamics Across the Value Chain (MDAVC): A Traceable Two-Tier Diagnostic Method for Executional Misalignment Under Institutional Volatility

keywords: Two-Tier Scoring and Traceability Protocol executional misalignment

detail.abstract: Firms operating in emerging economies frequently encounter executional misalignment, the breakdown between strategic intent and operational delivery, when institutional volatility disrupts value-chain interfaces. Existing diagnostic approaches remain largely firm-centric and often lack a standardized segment-level protocol that links documented external shocks to where bottlenecks form and how lag propagates through internal handoffs. This paper presents MDAVC (Market Dynamics Across the Value Chain), a middle-range diagnostic framework specified as a traceable procedure rather than a forecasting model. MDAVC rests on two methodological elements: a twotier scoring architecture that characterizes exposure through interface-anchored driver profiles and assesses responsiveness through Detection, Interpretation, and Adjustment, using fixed tier conversions to produce comparable diagnostic placements; and a traceability protocol that links scenario-anchored volatility episodes to segment-level interpretations through explicit interface mapping and documented scoring trails. The protocol is demonstrated through replication-oriented application across nine sector-country scenarios (Egypt, Kenya, Indonesia) spanning fintech, agribusiness, and pharmaceutical distribution, showing how volatility concentrates at binding MDAVC: Two-Tier Scoring and Traceability Protocol 2 interfaces and clusters in specific functional segments as gates. The contribution is a disciplined diagnostic method that bridges institutional conditions and operational execution, enabling auditable diagnosis of where misalignment forms, how it propagates, and which leading indicators provide earlier visibility than lagging outcomes.

title: Welfare Identity and Institutional Incentives

detail.title: Welfare Identity and Institutional Incentives

contentType.other: This paper is currently under review at Review of Political Economy. Comments are welcome.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a framework linking welfare outcomes to institutional incentives within the standard surplus-based approach. It shows that social welfare depends on utility and production cost, and increases only when productivity improves. From this perspective, profit can arise either from productivity improvements or from surplus extraction. The framework explains why similar policies-such as regulation, privatization, and platform governance-produce different welfare outcomes across institutional environments. It provides a unified basis for interpreting welfare outcomes and a general criterion for evaluating institutions.

title: Evaluating Synthetic Financial Time Series for Model Risk Management in Financial Institutions

detail.title: Evaluating Synthetic Financial Time Series for Model Risk Management in Financial Institutions
detail.abstract: Financial institutions are beginning to use synthetic time series to extend stress tests, train trading and hedging systems, test model changes, develop challenger models, and share market data with lower con dentiality risk. The model risk question is not whether generated paths look plausible, but whether they preserve the structures required for a controlled institutional use case. This paper reframes synthetic nancial data evaluation as a methodological review for model risk management and model validation. It contributes three additions to existing synthetic data, time-series generation, and nancial-generator reviews. First, it maps generative evaluation to institutional risk uses, including market risk, stress testing, liquidity and execution, hedging, portfolio risk, privacy-preserving data sharing, and model validation. Second, it converts common statistical tests into a decision framework linking data regime, required market structure, metric layer, failure mode, and governance action. Third, it proposes a reproducible benchmark protocol that records search boundaries, dataset lineage, generator con guration, random seeds, privacy checks, challenger baselines, and downstream validation evidence. A two-tier pilot illustrates the protocol. The rst tier uses S&P 500 daily returns to show that Gaussian, block-bootstrap, and GARCH-t baselines rank di erently under stylized facts, distance metrics, memorization checks, and 1 value-at-risk backtesting. The second tier uses a public ve-asset equity sample to test correlation, joint-tail, and portfolio value-at-risk preservation. The pilot is illustrative only: it supports the claim that the framework is executable and exposes metric disagreement, but it does not prove universal validity or production readiness. The paper concludes that synthetic data should be considered for institutional use only for named use cases, with explicit restrictions, validation evidence, challenger comparisons, monitoring triggers, and approval, restricted-use, or rejection decisions.

title: Enhancing Workplace Performance: A Study of Organizational Behavior in M Tractor Dealerships

detail.title: Enhancing Workplace Performance: A Study of Organizational Behavior in M Tractor Dealerships
detail.abstract: Organizational behavior functions as an essential component that establishes employee work output and workplace connections together with total organizational performance. The process of enhancing organizational performance needs organizations to assess employee attitudes and leadership styles and communication systems and employee motivation methods. The research investigates major organizational behavior problems that exist among M dealerships and service centers and their staff members. The study investigates important aspects which include managerial communication, employee participation in decision-making, workplace autonomy, coordination between departments, and recognition systems. The research uses a descriptive design to gather primary data through structured questionnaires which researchers distribute to employees working at various organizational levels. Researchers collected secondary data from books, academic journals, and recent research publications. The findings show that employees maintain effective communication with management while they receive appropriate freedom to perform their job duties. However, the organization faces difficulties in three main areas which include employee awareness and interdepartmental collaboration and career development paths. The study recommends that organizations should develop stronger recognition programs while they should implement management practices that involve employees and enhance their internal communication systems to boost employee motivation and workplace efficiency.

detail.abstract:
This study examines the impact of Human Resource (HR) Analytics on decision-making in the Information Technology (IT) sector, with a particular focus on the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI). In today’s data-driven business environment, organizations increasingly rely on HR analytics to enhance workforce planning, recruitment efficiency, employee performance management, and retention strategies. The integration of AI further strengthens these capabilities by enabling predictive and prescriptive analytics, automation of routine HR processes, and improved accuracy in talent acquisition.

The research adopts a descriptive and analytical approach, utilizing both primary and secondary data sources to evaluate how IT organizations leverage HR analytics tools and AI-driven systems. Key findings indicate that organizations implementing AI-enabled HR analytics experience improved decision quality, reduced bias in recruitment, enhanced employee engagement, and better alignment between HR strategies and organizational goals.

However, the study also identifies challenges such as data privacy concerns, lack of skilled professionals, high implementation costs, and resistance to technological change. The paper concludes that while AI-integrated HR analytics significantly enhances managerial decision-making, its effectiveness depends on proper data management practices, organizational readiness, and continuous skill development.

The study provides practical recommendations for HR professionals and organizations to effectively adopt AI-driven analytics, thereby improving strategic decision-making and gaining a competitive advantage in the IT sector.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes and architecturally defines the Autonomous Agentic Store: a physical retail and hospitality environment in which every customer interaction, operational function, and back-office business process is orchestrated by LLM agents, with no human staff required on premises during standard operations. Two structural forces make 2026 the deployment window: frontier LLM capability has crossed the behavioral threshold required for retail floor operation, and a 31% increase in US retail labor costs since 2019 makes human-staffed retail economically unsustainable at existing margins. The central thesis distinguishes this from prior automated retail: the AI agent is not a layer beneath a human brand — it is the brand. The paper presents a six-layer store intelligence stack; scope-bounded agent role and escalation contracts for eight named agents; a two-phase physical actuation model transitioning from agent-directed human task workers to narrow-scope robotic actuators on existing infrastructure; a full business intelligence stack replacing inventory management, omnichannel commerce, financial management, and strategic growth functions; an after-hours autonomous operations framework; and a self-sustaining economic model demonstrating 8.3-month payback with annual operating cost dropping to $42,100 at Month 30 against a $227,475 human-staffed baseline. With patenting and publishing experience across ML, edge intelligence, IoT, and context-aware systems, directly applicable to the proposed architecture.

detail.title: Inovasi Tempat Kerja dan Pengurusan Algoritma di Era Pasca Industri: Mengintegrasikan Teori Sistem Sosioteknikal (Socio-Technical Systems) untuk
detail.abstract: Perkembangan pesat teknologi digital dalam era pasca industri telah mendorong transformasi signifikan dalam struktur tempat kerja melalui penggunaan pengurusan algoritma. Sistem ini bukan sahaja mengubah cara kerja diorganisasikan, malah turut mempengaruhi hubungan pekerjaan, autonomi pekerja, serta kesejahteraan secara keseluruhan. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mensintesis secara kritis literatur berkaitan inovasi tempat kerja dan pengurusan algoritma dengan mengintegrasikan teori sistem sosioteknikal sebagai kerangka analisis utama. Pendekatan ulasan naratif digunakan bagi membolehkan pemetaan konseptual yang luas terhadap kajian terkini daripada pangkalan data Scopus, Web of Science dan Google Scholar. Analisis tematik mengenal pasti empat tema utama: (i) transformasi struktur organisasi kerja melalui algoritma, (ii) paradoks autonomi dan kawalan pekerja, (iii) kepentingan integrasi sosioteknikal dalam reka bentuk kerja, dan (iv) cabaran dasar dalam memastikan kesejahteraan pekerja. Dalam konteks Malaysia dan Sabah, isu utama termasuk jurang kemahiran digital, kekurangan perlindungan institusi, serta dominasi pekerjaan platform. Artikel ini menyimpulkan bahawa pengurusan algoritma berpotensi meningkatkan kecekapan organisasi, namun berisiko menjejaskan kesejahteraan pekerja jika tidak disokong oleh pendekatan berorientasikan manusia. Implikasi kajian menekankan keperluan reformasi dasar, ketelusan algoritma, dan pembangunan kapasiti tenaga kerja digital.

detail.abstract: Global corporate AI investment reached $252.3 billion in 2024, yet only 6% of firms report significant earnings impact. This article argues that AI project failure is fundamentally an organizational learning problem rather than a technology deficit. Drawing on a systematic synthesis of 21 foundational sources, including surveys of nearly 10,000 organizational leaders, we identify critical failure vectors across organizational culture, leadership alignment, and technical infrastructure. We introduce the Orchestration Maturity Framework, a model that maps enterprise AI capability across five pillars: Culture & Leadership, Human Capital & Operations, Data Architecture, Systems & Infrastructure, and Governance & Regulatory Compliance. The framework provides prescriptive guidance for transitioning from isolated experimentation to an orchestrated agentic enterprise, reframing AI investment as a multi-dimensional capability development challenge rather than a static IT procurement.

title: When CSR/ESG Pays - and When It Doesn't: Risk Mitigation, Materiality, and the Governance Conditions for Financial Performance

detail.title: When CSR/ESG Pays - and When It Doesn't: Risk Mitigation, Materiality, and the Governance Conditions for Financial Performance
detail.abstract: Debate over corporate social responsibility (CSR) and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investing has often been framed in binary terms: either as a source of systematic outperformance or as a distraction from fiduciary duty. This paper evaluates the empirical literature and reframes the discussion through a governance lens. The evidence does not support universal claims of excess returns. Instead, it suggests that financial effects are conditional and arise through identifiable mechanisms, most consistently through downside risk mitigation. Financial relevance depends on economic materiality-meaning whether an ESG issue is structurally linked to a firm's financial outcomes through revenue, cost, regulatory exposure, or competitive positioning-governance integration, and horizon alignment. By synthesizing meta-analytic research, ratings disagreement studies, event-based evidence, and materialityfocused findings, the paper proposes a structured framework for boards and investment committees. Rather than advocating or dismissing ESG, it positions stakeholder governance as a conditional component of disciplined capital allocation.

detail.abstract:
The period 2021–2025 marked a deep structural transformation of Albania's labour market. The restructuring of wage distribution has shifted the workforce from lower segments towards middle and upper ones, increasing the tax base and personal income tax revenues from ALL 39.3 billion in 2021 to ALL 82.5 billion in 2025. Growth has been disproportionate due to progressivity and the bracket creep effect, while the divergence between wage tax and social contributions reveals structural limitations in social schemes.

Paketa "Formal Employment 2027" offers a strategic approach to deeper formalisation, reducing the labour burden on low and middle wages, increasing progressive taxation on real estate and creating incentives for economic formalisation. The optimistic scenario projects 4–6% growth in formal employment in labour-intensive sectors, strengthening the sustainability of pension schemes and advancing European integration objectives (Chapter 19 and the European Pillar of Social Rights). Without structural reforms, informality stabilises at high levels and pressure on the social system increases.

Policy proposals include a review of tax thresholds and contribution ceilings, active policies for productivity growth and digitalisation, stronger links between contributions and benefits, proactive anti-emigration strategies and smart fiscal administration.

The implementation of a National Action Plan for Formal Employment and Fiscal Convergence 2027–2030 is key to a modern, inclusive and sustainable labour market, transforming demographic and fiscal challenges into opportunities for European development.

detail.abstract: This paper documents a sequence of failed literacy interventions at a Ramakrishna Mission ashram school in North Burdwan district, West Bengal, serving primarily Santali and Adivasi children from Classes 5 through 9. We describe eight sequentially tested approaches to English literacy acquisition and explain why each failed. We argue that the central failure was a consistent misdiagnosis: each approach treated a structural vocabulary deficit as a motivation or engagement problem. The most instructive failure was Duolingo, which children used voluntarily across two discontinuous phases spanning approximately twelve months, with high engagement throughout. Informal recall testing revealed that children could not retrieve vocabulary the platform had drilled; speaking transfer was absent. Pre-post reading assessment using the Pratham ASER framework (n=22, outlier-stripped) showed improvement in reading levels (median 1.0 to 2.0, p<0.001, Wilcoxon signed-rank test), but this improvement occurred under multiple concurrent interventions and cannot be attributed to any single component. Analysis reveals a threshold effect: all six children who began at Level 2 (word reading) improved, compared with only 7 of 15 at Level 1 (Fisher exact p=0.004 for reaching Level 3+). IQ showed a suggestive positive association with improvement among Level 1 children (Spearman r=0.50, p=0.056, not reaching conventional significance) but was irrelevant among Level 2 children, where all improved regardless of IQ. Teacher-rated parental attitude did not predict improvement within the critical Level 1 subgroup. These failures were predicted by established SLA research: Laufer (1989) and Hu and Nation (2000) demonstrated that reading comprehension drops sharply below a 95-98% vocabulary coverage threshold. In a context of functional English absence, every text falls below this threshold. We propose the term motivated comprehension illusion and discuss implications for teacher reward structures, equity in universal intervention design, and the interaction between India's no-detention policy and foundational literacy failure.

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces Jamallo Entropy Bars (JEB), a novel financial charting methodology designed specifically for discretionary human traders. Unlike time-based candlesticks, JEB employs a hybrid information flux metric combining Parkinson volatility (70%), linear regression quality (15%), and permutation entropy (15%) to determine candlestick formation boundaries.

In empirical comparison with human-readable charting alternatives, JEB achieves the highest human-focused quality score while uniquely preserving actual OHLC data. Key findings include:
*   73x noise compression vs 1x for Heikin-Ashi
*   6x higher signal-to-noise ratio (0.023 vs 0.004)
*   Real prices preserved for accurate limit order placement
*   Particle ladder visualization showing price micro-structure

While Heikin-Ashi achieves higher trend clarity (77% vs 47%), this comes at the cost of replacing actual prices with calculated averages—a fundamental limitation for execution-focused traders. JEB offers the visual clarity of smoothed chart types while preserving the precision of actual price data.

title: THE STRUCTURAL GAP AND ITS FINANCIAL SOLUTION: VALUE CREATION CHAIN TOKENIZATION AS THE INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER OF KAZAKHSTAN'S EURASIAN HUB ECONOMY SSRN Working Paper

detail.title: THE STRUCTURAL GAP AND ITS FINANCIAL SOLUTION: VALUE CREATION CHAIN TOKENIZATION AS THE INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER OF KAZAKHSTAN'S EURASIAN HUB ECONOMY SSRN Working Paper
detail.abstract: This paper synthesises the author's previously published body of research on the SDA (Structured Digital Assets) Methodology and examines its application within the systemic objective of transforming Kazakhstan into a technological and logistics hub at the centre of Eurasia. The central argument is as follows: Kazakhstan's aspiration to hub status rests on genuine geopolitical and infrastructural foundations, yet remains structurally unfulfilled due to the chronic gap between resource extraction and deep in-country processing. SDA tokenization of value creation chains offers the missing financial infrastructure layer that renders deep processing investable, transparent, and competitive — without administrative coercion. The paper conducts an original analysis along three axes: (i) the Middle Corridor as a geopolitical opportunity and its current constraints; (ii) the six systemic effects of SDA projected onto the specific requirements of hub formation — from comprehensive by-product extraction to cost-of-capital reduction; and (iii) the regulatory framework of the Republic of Kazakhstan as it stood by May 2026, constituting a genuine first-mover competitive advantage. In answering the question of whether Kazakhstan can and should deploy this instrument, the paper systematically analyses the arguments for and against, and concludes that the coincidence of geopolitical moment, regulatory readiness, and methodological maturity is a rare historical condition with a limited window of availability.

detail.title: Regulation of Electronic Commerce in Mega-Regional Trade Agreements
detail.abstract: E-commerce is one of the most actively developing and complex aspects of the digital transformation of the international trade. Its regulation within the multilateral trade system framework is mostly limited to the WPEC WTO, WTO JSI on e-commerce and the well-known Moratorium on the Imposition of Customs Duties on Electronic Transmissions. Much more successful and effective examples of e-commerce regulation are the e-commerce sections of Regional Trade Agreements, including Mega-Regional Trade Agreements whose e-commerce chapters significantly inspired both the JSI agreement on e-commerce provisions and non-trade digital agreements like Singapore's DEPA, DEAs and DTAs.

detail.abstract: The current research examines how the various dimensions of the overconfidence bias among potential investors such as overprecision, overestimation, and overplacement differentially influence resistance to financial advice seeking through their influence on various dimensions of trust. Intriguing insights include: 1) overprecision positively influencing resistance to FAS through increased focus on the self, 2) overestimation reducing resistance to FAS through increased trust in financial advisors, and 3) debiased overprecision (genuine confidence/authentic pride) reducing resistance to FAS through both increased trust on financial advisors, and reduced focus on the self. Given these findings, we conducted two experimental studies, where we developed marketing nudges on overprecision and overestimation, and examined their influence on FAS. Outcomes from the experiments provided confirmatory evidence of both debiased overprecision, and overestimation positively influencing FAS. These findings carry implications for research on FAS, overconfidence, and provide novel insights into the underlying relationship between overconfidence and trust in services context.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Context of International Political and Security Challenge

The analysis indicates the existence of a relationship between the development of technology in this direction and the change in the balance between world powers.

detail.abstract: Economic systems constitute the most complex dissipative structures known in the universe. Sustained by billions of agents continuously exchanging energy and information through value flows, information flows, and institutional flows, they maintain ordered structures far from equilibrium. Yet a fundamental scientific question remains systematically unexplored: can the causal integration degree of this dissipative network-the irreducible information content of the system as a whole that cannot be reduced to the sum of its parts-be rigorously defined, axiomatically derived, and empirically computed and validated in real-world data? tables, and micro-behavioral datasets, all five core falsifiable predictions receive strong empirical support. This work provides a physically first-principles and axiomatically grounded framework for quantifying causal integration in economic systems. While the conclusions are strongly supported within the available data range, their applicability and boundary conditions in broader dissipative systems await rigorous future scrutiny.

title: The Role of Location in Shaping Competitive Dynamics: Evidence from Philippine Warehouse Club Retailers

detail.title: The Role of Location in Shaping Competitive Dynamics: Evidence from Philippine Warehouse Club Retailers

keywords: Resource-Based View (RBV) Paper Type: Literature review

detail.abstract:
Purpose-This research intends to explore how location decisions influence competitive actions among warehouse club retailers in the Philippines. It also aims to analyze how these businesses utilize their presence as a weapon in competition, relying on major strategic and economic theories.
Design/methodology/approach-This research follows a qualitative descriptive case study methodology that includes a systematic literature review. Theory-based thematic analysis was conducted on secondary data extracted from academic publications, industry reports, and reputable news articles. The study is thus based on the concepts of Porter's Five Forces, Resource-Based View (RBV), Central Place Theory, Hotelling's Model of Spatial Competition, and First-Mover Advantage.
Findings-The results indicate that the combination of worsening competition, market opening, and activities of new entrants bring about the defensive and retaliatory expansion from incumbents. Companies choose their outlets very carefully and speed up their geographical growth as a way of (1) preserving their market share and (2) scaring off competitors. Besides that, internal resources that include brand awareness, very efficient supply chain and portfolio of prime locations further enhance their capabilities to maintain a competitive edge. As a result, location choices become simultaneously reactive and proactive instruments guiding the strategy. 
Originality/value-Through the integration of spatial and strategic management perspectives, this investigation extends to warehouse club retailing in the Philippines, which so far has a limited coverage in the literature, and shows the pivotal role of location as a competitive tool, while also offering a framework for unraveling the location-induced competitive behavior in retail markets of emerging economies.

title: The Development Threshold: Demographics and the Middle-Income Transition

detail.title: The Development Threshold: Demographics and the Middle-Income Transition
detail.abstract: Which countries successfully transition from middle-income to high-income status, and why? Using a 140-country panel spanning 1950-2024, I identify a critical development threshold zone between $9,000 and $25,000 GDP per capita (PPP) and show that demographic structure at the point of entry is the single strongest predictor of whether a country crosses to high-income status. The first principal component of the age distribution (Z₁) explains 27% of crossing outcomes in univariate logit-nearly double the explanatory power of income level itself (17%). In Cox proportional hazard models, each unit increase in Z₁ more than doubles the hazard of crossing (HR=2.13, p<0.0001); conditioning on income sharpens this (HR=1.77, p=0.006) while log GDP per capita independently predicts crossing speed (HR=4.04, p=0.035). Critically, the Z₁ × log GDP per capita interaction is null in both the logit (β=-0.06, p=0.959) and the Cox model (p=0.428), confirming that demographics and income are additively separable predictors of threshold crossing-they operate through independent channels. Within the zone, however, income conditions the demographic mechanism: the Z₁ × log GDP interaction is significant for savings (-3.77, p=0.016), the S-I gap (-5.02, p=0.006), and investment (+2.59, p=0.041), meaning demographics bite harder at higher income levels during transit. The mechanism operates through the savings channel: 72% of the demographic effect on the current account within the zone is mediated by savings behavior. Of 57 countries currently in the threshold zone, only 14 are well-positioned demographically. China, at $23,800, has a 99% predicted crossing probability but its demographic window has already closed-its Z₁ exceeds the historical crosser mean at exit, and its savings rate is declining at 0.44 percentage points per year. The middle-income trap, I argue, is substantially a demographic trap: countries that cannot generate a sustained savings surplus before their populations age past the critical threshold face a structurally narrowing path to high-income status.

title: Sectoral Savings Decomposition: Where Does Demographic Capital Come From?

detail.title: Sectoral Savings Decomposition: Where Does Demographic Capital Come From?
detail.abstract: Paper 1 in this series established that aging populations generate excess savings that flow abroad as current account surpluses. This paper asks: which sector generates the excess savings? Using a panel of up to 185 countries from 1990 to 2024, we decompose the demographic savings effect into government and private components using the Higgins (1998) polynomial specification (Z₁, Z₂, Z₃). The key innovation is an income-conditioned specification that replaces capital account openness with log GDP per capita and a Z₁ × log GDP per capita interaction, testing whether the demographic-savings link operates independently of income or merely proxies for it. The results overturn the baseline narrative. National savings: Z₁ drops from +90.2 (p < 0.001) to +41.7 (p = 0.062), halved and marginal. Government saving collapses entirely: Z₁ falls from +22.3 (p < 0.001) to-2.1 (not significant)-the baseline government saving result was an income proxy, not a demographic effect. Private saving halves: Z₁ drops from +60.0 (p < 0.001) to +33.6 (not significant). But investment survives and strengthens: Z₁ rises from +32.2 (p < 0.01) to +42.0 (p < 0.001). The current account flips sign: Z₁ moves from +27.7 (p < 0.05) to-26.9 (not significant), with the Z₁ × log GDP per capita interaction at +1.013 (p < 0.05) capturing the sign reversal-demographics predict current account surpluses only in richer economies. The OECD government saving result deepens dramatically: Z₁ =-65.9 (p = 0.002), more than doubling relative to the baseline (-43.1). Income tercile analysis confirms the gradient: high-income national savings Z₁ = +98.1 (p < 0.001), with private saving Z₁ = +70.7 (p < 0.001); low-income effects are uniformly null. The income-conditioned results reveal that the demographic-savings link is not a universal lifecycle phenomenon but is fundamentally income-dependent: investment is the robust demographic channel, government saving was an income proxy, private saving operates only in wealthy economies, and the current account sign reversal is captured by Z₁ × income.

title: Farmer’s preferences for different Crop Residue Management practices: Evidence from Choice Experiment in Punjab India
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, The Nature Conservancy, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and The Nature Conservancy

detail.title: Farmer’s preferences for different Crop Residue Management practices: Evidence from Choice Experiment in Punjab India
detail.abstract: This study employs a Discrete Choice Experiment with 1,224 rice-growing farmers across Punjab to quantify preferences for no-burn crop residue management (CRM) technologies relative to the status quo of residue burning. Using a Random Parameter Logit framework, we find that the persistence of burning reflects a constrained equilibrium driven by service-market risks rather than farmer inertia. While farmers prefer incorporation-based (Super Seeder) or hybrid (Smart Seeder) technologies, the mulching-based Happy Seeder faces a significant valuation gap due to perceived agronomic uncertainty. Logistical reliability is the dominant driver; a 1–3 day machinery window commands a substantial positive willingness-to-pay (INR 307/acre), identifying time certainty as a primary operational constraint. Adoption is further hindered by a strong aversion to digital-only advisory services (INR-313/acre), which suggests a deep reliance on physical accountability for technically sensitive transitions. Institutional trust remains a critical barrier: farmers significantly prefer informal farmer-to-farmer rentals over cooperatives, while Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs) lack a statisticallysignificant ”trust premium” over informal providers. Adoption is further hindered by larger landholdings and high perceived costs, but bolstered by expectations of yield and fuel gains. To enable sustainable biomass management, policy must shift from equipment subsidies toward de-risking the transition through professionalized service guarantees and hybrid, human-centric advisory systems that bridge the reliability gap.

title: Structural Limits of OHLCV-Based Intraday Signals in MNQ Futures: A Systematic Falsification Study

detail.title: Structural Limits of OHLCV-Based Intraday Signals in MNQ Futures: A Systematic Falsification Study

detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether intraday momentum signals derived from open-high-low-close-volume (OHLCV) data generate statistically significant trading edge in Micro E-Mini Nasdaq 100 futures (ticker: MNQ) under realistic execution constraints. Using 947 regular trading hours (RTH) trading days of five-minute bar data spanning 2021 through 2025, we construct and systematically test fourteen distinct signal families. These include opening range breakouts at multiple horizons, gap-based continuation and fade strategies, volume signature signals, cross-session momentum from the Asia session, liquidity grab reversals, volatility-regime-conditioned classifiers, and news-event-driven directional strategies. Every signal is evaluated against a consistent institutional standard: a minimum T-statistic of 2.0 on out-of-sample walk-forward results, a minimum of 30 out-of-sample trades, positive net return after a fixed two-point round-trip friction cost, and multi-year stability across all available years. No tested signal survives these combined criteria simultaneously. The gross edge available to next-bar-open systematic execution is structurally constrained to approximately 0.07 to 1.50 points across all signal families-a ceiling that is insufficient to clear two-point round-trip transaction costs. One signal family-gap continuation short-produces a T-statistic of 3.23 and a mean net return of 14.52 points but on only 22 trades across three years, falling below the minimum sample threshold and therefore failing deployment criteria. Two separately validated signals-the RTH Confluence Signal (T = 5.83, mean net +15.77 pts, N = 538) and London Session Signal B (T = 5.15, mean net +5.77 pts, N = 289)-are presented as positive controls confirming the methodology is capable of detecting genuine edge when it exists. The primary contribution of this paper is methodological: a reproducible, documented falsification framework applied consistently across a broad signal universe on a liquid modern futures instrument. This contributes to a systematic null result that is underrepresented in both retail and academic trading literature, where survivorship bias tends to publish only strategies that appear to work. All results are based on strictly out-of-sample walk-forward validation.

title: The role of information and communication technology in the relationship between foreign direct investment and income inequality: Evidence from selected countries

detail.title: The role of information and communication technology in the relationship between foreign direct investment and income inequality: Evidence from selected countries
detail.abstract:
The main purpose of this paper is to investigate the impact of foreign direct investment (FDI) on income inequality with an emphasis on Information and Communication Technology (ICT). Under the division of International Telecommunications Union, underlying countries have been differentiated in two groups of the high and average level of information and communication technology. The research modeling is based on Panel data over the time period of 2001-2016.
The results indicate that foreign direct investment (FDI) and ICT have a negative and significant effect on inequality in two groups of countries. Also, the impact of (FDI) and ICT on income inequality in countries with high level of ICT is more than those with an average level of ICT but the effect is the same in both countries. Based on the results, ICT in each group of countries can change the stable relationship between FDI and inequality.

title: Do the trophic impacts which jaguars have on wildlife communities matter to farmers?,Diverging farmer preferences for jaguar-associated benefits and costs

detail.title: Do the trophic impacts which jaguars have on wildlife communities matter to farmers?,Diverging farmer preferences for jaguar-associated benefits and costs
detail.abstract: Farmers who live near jaguars (Panthera onca) can experience various benefits and costs associated with both the jaguars themselves (direct impacts) and the ways jaguars alter wildlife communities (indirect impacts). In order to understand the trade-offs farmers face in communities that are important for maintaining jaguar population connectivity, I conducted a Discrete Choice Experiment (DCE) in the corridor communities of the Montes Azules Biosphere Reserve in Mexico. This DCE quantified the relative value placed on: (i) maintaining jaguars inside and surrounding these communities; (ii) avoiding maize losses caused by herbivores that jaguars may prey upon; (iii) avoiding livestock losses caused by jaguars and other predators with which they interact; and (iv) gaining additional income through ecotourism. The indirect benefit of preventing maize losses was valued by a majority of respondents, but not by those who most highly valued jaguar conservation for other reasons. Understanding the magnitude of jaguars' indirect impacts on agriculture would likely affect choices regarding jaguar conservation among a minority of respondents. In contrast, all respondents valued jaguar conservation in the reserve, and a majority would like jaguars in their communities, all else equal. A dislike of attacks on livestock and of having jaguars nearby are negative impacts of jaguars on human welfare. Jaguar conservation can broadly benefit the welfare of neighboring farming communities, and the benefits are potentially more evenly spread among households if the indirect benefit of maize protection is considered.

title: Assessing the coexistence between snowmaking and other mountain water uses: a biocentric socio-ecological systems approach

detail.title: Assessing the coexistence between snowmaking and other mountain water uses: a biocentric socio-ecological systems approach
detail.abstract: Snowmaking is the most widespread adaptation strategy used by winter tourism in response to climate change, yet it requires increasingly large volumes of water. Public and scientific concerns are growing regarding the potentially unsustainable use of water for snowmaking. However, only a few studies have examined this issue, and most adopt an anthropocentric perspective, operate at broad spatio‐temporal scales, and focus primarily on interactions between demand and water resources. A systemic, non-anthropocentric and fine-scale framework is nevertheless required to analyse and compare the extent to which snowmaking may threaten coexistence among mountain water uses, including the needs of non-human beings. This article adapts the ”robustness of socio-ecological systems” framework to the specific features of snowmaking, integrating these requirements. Using this new framework, we analysed potential coexistence issues among water uses that may be highly localised in time and space, as illustrated by the case of Gresse-en-Vercors in the French Alps.

title: Beyond Demographics: How Environmental Attitudes and Nature Contact Shape Urban Landscape Preferences
affiliations: University of Reims Champagne-Ardenne, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond Demographics: How Environmental Attitudes and Nature Contact Shape Urban Landscape Preferences
detail.abstract: As cities expand, the design of urban landscapes affects both environmental quality and residents’ well-being. Yet, people’s preferences for urban features are far from uniform. In this study, we integrate attitudinal and experiential factors into a hybrid choice framework to investigate how environmental attitudes and habitual contact with nature shape preferences for green spaces and built-up areas. Our results show that both pro-environmental attitudes and strong nature contact enhance the utility of green spaces while reducing that of built-up areas, whereas socio-demographic characteristics explain surprisingly little. In particular, these psychological factors account for a substantial share of the heterogeneity in preferences for trees. The findings suggest that urban planning policies for sustainable cities may be more effective if they move beyond purely demographic targeting and instead draw on psychological and experiential insights.

title: Demographics and Bank Risk: Population Aging, Margin Compression, and Financial Stability

detail.title: Demographics and Bank Risk: Population Aging, Margin Compression, and Financial Stability
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how demographic structure affects bank risk-taking and financial stability using a panel of up to 140 countries from 1990 to 2024. The headline finding is net interest margin (NIM) compression: the Higgins (1998) demographic polynomial Z₁ predicts NIM with a coefficient of-47.0 (p = 0.005, R² = 0.260), indicating that aging populations are associated with significantly lower bank profitability margins. Baseline controls include real GDP growth, fiscal balance/GDP, log GDP per capita, and the Z₁ × log GDP/cap interaction (income-conditioning required to avoid confounding aging with development level). This result is robust to 5-year lagged demographics (Z₁_lag5 =-63.1, p < 0.001), cluster-bootstrap standard errors, permutation tests, leave-one-out country analysis, and regional jackknife. The NIM compression is concentrated in non-OECD countries (Z₁ =-47.0, p = 0.013) and middle-income economies (Z₁ =-150.1, p < 0.001), while OECD countries now show a borderline significant effect (Z₁ =-56.5, p = 0.094). A second novel finding is the OECD/non-OECD bifurcation in non-performing loan ratios: in non-OECD countries, aging increases credit risk (Z₁ = +71.8, p = 0.022), while in OECD countries the protective effect is directional but no longer significant at conventional levels under income-conditioned controls (Z₁ =-48.1, p = 0.32). Full-sample bank stability measures (Z-scores, NPL ratios) mask this directional heterogeneity; the full-sample NPL coefficient is now marginally significant (Z₁ = +39.8, p = 0.083). effects (all Z × KAOPEN interactions null, tested as hypothesis-specific rather than baseline controls). These findings extend the US-county evidence of Doerr et al. (JFQA 2024) and the advanced-economy focus of IMF WP/2024/118 to a global panel, revealing a post-crisis institutional bifurcation invisible in geographically restricted samples.

title: Integrated Financial Security Framework for Banking Systems: A Risk-Based and Managerial Approach to Financial Stability

detail.title: Integrated Financial Security Framework for Banking Systems: A Risk-Based and Managerial Approach to Financial Stability
