detail.abstract:
This paper develops an integrated framework for assessing the financial security of banking institutions by combining capital adequacy, liquidity, asset quality, market risk, operational resilience, and managerial capacity into a unified analytical model. The study introduces a novel managerial component captured through a human capital stability coefficient (K_hr) to reflect the impact of personnel quality and governance on institutional resilience.
The methodology applies normalization and weighted aggregation techniques to construct a composite Financial Security Index (FSI), enabling cross-institutional comparability and dynamic monitoring. Unlike conventional approaches focused primarily on financial ratios, the proposed model integrates qualitative and institutional dimensions, enhancing diagnostic precision and early-warning capabilities.
The framework is aligned with international regulatory standards and supervisory practices and is applicable to advanced financial systems, including the United States. The proposed approach contributes to strengthening financial stability assessment and improving risk governance in complex economic environments.

title: How Well do Economic Games Model Collective Climate Action?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, ESRI and Trinity College (Dublin)

detail.title: How Well do Economic Games Model Collective Climate Action?
detail.abstract: This study critically and constructively assesses the use of economics games as a methodological tool to understand how people behave in climate collective action problems. Economic games (such as public goods games) are widely used to empirically measure cooperative behaviour while experimentally manipulating potential influencing factors. While these games illuminate trade-offs between individual and collective interests, translating their findings to the multi-dimensional and global nature of climate change and climate cooperation is not straightforward. Drawing on a pre-registered systematic scoping review of 165 sources, this article systematically evaluates the most significant challenges in aligning the economic games methodologies currently used in climate research with real-world climate cooperation problems. It identifies seven challenges. Unlike climate collective action problems, economic game designs usually (1) begin at a neutral starting point; (2) refer to abstract or symbolic outcomes; (3) do not involve cooperating towards a true public good; (4) do not involve refraining from causing harm; (5) use salient, direct choices between private and public payoffs (6) focus on binary, probabilistic catastrophes; and (7) involve a single homogeneous cooperative behaviour. The article offers constructive suggestions to improve the design of economic games, with clear implications for research and policy, and identifies new research questions that methodological improvements can help answer.

title: BRIDGING THE GAP BETWEEN ACADEMIA AND INDUSTRY IN PLATFORM ENGINEERING RESEARCH

detail.title: BRIDGING THE GAP BETWEEN ACADEMIA AND INDUSTRY IN PLATFORM ENGINEERING RESEARCH
detail.abstract: Platform engineering has emerged as a critical discipline in modern software development, addressing the increasing complexity of distributed systems and the need for scalable, reliable, and developer-centric infrastructure. Despite its rapid adoption in industry, there remains a noticeable disconnect between academic research and industry practice, particularly in areas such as internal developer platforms, automation, and developer experience optimization. Academic literature tends to focus on theoretical models, conceptual frameworks, and foundational principles, while industry contributions emphasize practical implementation, tooling decisions, and real-world architectural solutions. This study examines the gap between academia and industry in platform engineering research, with a focus on understanding why this divide exists and how it impacts the advancement of knowledge in the field. It explores how internal developer platforms (IDPs), DevOps practices, and platform engineering architectures are represented differently across scholarly publications and industrial sources such as technical blogs, whitepapers, and engineering case studies. The study adopts a comparative analytical approach to synthesize insights from both domains and identify areas of alignment, divergence, and mutual influence. The findings indicate that while academia provides strong theoretical grounding in software architecture, systems design, and socio-technical principles, it often lacks empirical validation and real-world applicability in the context of rapidly evolving platform engineering practices. Conversely, industry research offers rich, experience-driven insights and practical solutions but frequently lacks methodological rigor and generalizability. This imbalance contributes to fragmented understanding and limits the development of standardized frameworks for platform engineering. The study highlights the need for stronger collaboration between researchers and practitioners to bridge this gap through empirical studies, shared datasets, open-source platform research, and co-developed reference architectures. By integrating academic rigor with industry relevance, platform engineering research can evolve into a more cohesive and impactful discipline that better supports the needs of modern software organizations.

detail.title: Investigating the Relationship between Energy Consumption and Economic Growth in Iran’s Provinces Using Cointegration and Multivariate Panel Error Correction Model

keywords: Dynamic Ordinary Least Square and Pooled Mean Group

detail.abstract: Energy consumption as one of the most important factors in economic growth has a significant role in the economic development. In this study, there was on attempt to estimate the impact of energy consumption on economic growth in Iran's provinces to answer this question: Whether or not an increase in energy consumption lead to economic growth? We estimated the relationship between energy consumption and economic growth in tree groups of Iran’s provinces (developed, less developed and undeveloped provinces) using economic theory and based on Panel Error Correction Model and panel cointegration and causality tests in the period of 1381 to 1389. Long-run and short-run coefficient estimations have been done using Dynamic Ordinary Least Square and Pooled Mean Group respectively. The results indicate that increasing (decreasing) energy consumption in three kinds of provinces causes an increase (decrease) in economic growth. Thus, we accepted Feedback hypothesis in this study because of the bidirectional relationship between energy consumption and economic growth in Iran’s provinces. Moreover, the effect of energy consumption on economic growth in developed provinces is more than two other kinds of provinces, so part of the development gap among three different groups of provinces could be explain by the gap in their energy consumption

detail.abstract: The claim that AI-enabled transparency, immutable audit trails, and protocol-mediated dispute resolution transform one-shot political games into iterated games-and thereby shift the governance Nash equilibrium from capture to accountability-is defensible, but only under carefully stated conditions. The condition set is not trivial. The Folk Theorem establishes that infinitely repeated n-player games sustain a multiplicity of equilibria, many of them exploitative, so the naive Axelrod-tit-for-tat story cannot carry the argument on its own. This paper isolates the architectural properties that select a cooperative equilibrium rather than a surveillance or elite-collusion one; defends those properties against four standard objections (n-player extension, asymmetric punishment capacity, noise, the reputation-system empirical record); and presents an incentivecompatibility analysis of an Intelligent Negotiation System (INS) protocol that discharges the mechanism-design vocabulary precisely. The paper's contribution is synthesis: it applies the imperfect-public-monitoring framework of Fudenberg, Levine, and Maskin (1994) to the governance case with nested principal-agent structure, and identifies the architectural properties that select cooperation. It does not claim a novel theoretical extension of the Folk Theorem. It names the conditions under which the formal defense holds, acknowledges where those conditions may fail, and delivers a rigorous treatment that stands on its own.

title: Investigation the Dynamic Relationship Between Energy and Economic Growth in Different Energy Carriers and Various Economic Sectors: Application of ARDL Bounding Test

detail.title: Investigation the Dynamic Relationship Between Energy and Economic Growth in Different Energy Carriers and Various Economic Sectors: Application of ARDL Bounding Test
detail.abstract: In this study, the relationship between energy and economic growth is examined within the framework of the Douglas production function. Using the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) approach, the relationship is analyzed both at the aggregate and sectoral levels, as well as across different energy carriers, over the period 1389–1353 (1974–2010) for the Iranian economy. The short-run and long-run relationships between energy consumption and economic growth are estimated for the total economy and for the agriculture, industry, and services sectors, as well as by disaggregating energy carriers including electricity, kerosene, gasoline, gas oil, fuel oil, and natural gas. The results indicate that energy consumption has a positive impact on economic growth in both the short run and the long run for the overall economy and across different sectors. However, the positive effect of all energy carriers on economic growth in the total economy and in different sectors is not confirmed for the industrial sector. Additionally, the positive impact of gas oil in the agriculture sector, and gasoline in the services sector as well as in the total economy, is not statistically supported.

title: Knowledge-Driven Endogenous Growth in Open Economy: A Grand Synthetic Approach

detail.title: Knowledge-Driven Endogenous Growth in Open Economy: A Grand Synthetic Approach
detail.abstract: This paper develops a Knowledge-driven Endogenous Growth (KEG) model for an open economy. It is written as an extension to the Grand Synthetic Model (GSM) paper (Ye, 2026) and therefore does not restate the GSM architecture, its ten-equation baseline, or the previously presented figures and tables. Instead, the article adds a new dynamic innovation module that connects heterogeneous household demand, New Keynesian price adjustment, open-economy financial conditions, research labor allocation, and knowledge accumulation. The central contribution is to show how the real-to-imaginary wealth-expansion diagnostic introduced in the GSM paper can become a state constraint inside a dynamic innovation model. When financial valuation returns dominate innovation returns, research labor is reallocated away from knowledge production, which lowers the balanced-growth rate and may create a self-reinforcing low-real-growth equilibrium. The KEG thus sharpens the efficiency-equity-innovation trilemma: monetary policy affects financing costs and asset valuation, fiscal policy affects both redistribution and research incentives, exchangerate policy affects external balance and technology diffusion, and knowledge policy determines whether stabilization remains compatible with long-run wealth expansion. The model yields testable implications for dynamic-panel, threshold, and Bayesian structural estimation.

title: Decentralized Policy-making and Market Distortions: Evidence from China's Drug Formulary Design
affiliations: , Tsinghua University - Tsinghua University School of Economics and Management and

detail.title: Decentralized Policy-making and Market Distortions: Evidence from China's Drug Formulary Design
detail.abstract: Should public health insurance be administered at the national or sub-national level? This paper examines the issue in China's public health insurance drug formulary design. Before 2019, the central government allowed provinces to design their own public insurance drug lists. We find that provincial governments are more likely to include locally produced drugs in their insurance coverage, even after accounting for demand. We also find that the covered local drugs have a lower quality. We illustrate that a unified national formulary could eliminate such distortions, but may induce welfare losses due to the central government's incomplete information and disregard for local demand heterogeneity.

title: Value, Bluff, and Cyclic Dominance: Completing the Von Neumann Poker Project

detail.title: Value, Bluff, and Cyclic Dominance: Completing the Von Neumann Poker Project
detail.abstract: Game theory was born in a poker game. In 1928, John von Neumann published a model of two-player poker that established the minimax theorem, the existence of mixedstrategy equilibria, and a clean mathematical account of bluffing. His model required three simplifying assumptions for analytic tractability: scalar hand strength, deterministic outcomes, and fixed bet size, none of which apply to real poker. A century of subsequent literature has relaxed each assumption individually and in pairs. I complete the project by relaxing all three simultaneously. I compute for the first time the game-theory optimal (GTO) equilibrium of the von Neumann betting game on the actual 169×169 equity matrix of heads-up Texas Hold'em (THE) across the full range of bet-to-pot ratios. This reveals strategic insights obscured by von Neumann's assumptions. These insights been uncovered in other domains and are documented in poker manuals. My contribution is to tie the results together in a unified theoretic framework with a rigorous derivation.

detail.abstract: This study aimed to determine the influence of perceived organizational effectiveness and work readiness of police officers on their job performance. The study results are as follows: all respondents remarked "agree" in all domains of organizational effectiveness as perceived by police-respondents particularly international communication, external communication, technology/resources, empowerment, employee satisfaction, loyalty, teamwork, involvement, development, initiative, leadership ability and ability to motivate; respondents responded "occasionally" in the stress response measure of the respondents; the general performance assessment for the respondents of the study was 3.87 which corresponds to a "very satisfactory" performance; according to the study's computation, the perceived organizational effectiveness significantly influences the job performance of the respondents since the study obtained a B-coefficient value of 0.461 (p = .000); the study did not generate substantial evidence to prove that stress response measure has a significant influence on the job performance of the respondents since the computation generated a B-coefficient result of 0.071 (p = .202); and the researcher proposed a training program geared towards improving organizational effectiveness and promoting physiological and psychological well-being among the respondents..

title: Leverage Discipline and Board Governance in Construction and Real Estate

detail.title: Leverage Discipline and Board Governance in Construction and Real Estate

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests. No funding was received for this research. The data used in this study are publicly available through Yahoo Finance and the Kenneth R. French Data Library at Dartmouth College.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether celebrity board governance signals financial discipline in cyclical sectors, using the COVID-19 demand shock as a quasi-natural experiment applied to publicly traded construction and real estate (C&RE) firms. A three-dimensional Celebrity Governance Score (CGS) is constructed from firm visibility, market influence, and revenue scale for 93 C&RE companies drawn from the Russell 3000 universe over January 2015 through April 2025. Using Fama-French three-factor (FF3) regressions, difference-indifferences (DiD) estimation, and propensity score matching (PSM), we find that celebrity-governed firms carry significantly lower leverage (Debt/Equity: 87 versus 240, p = 0.027; Debt/EBITDA: 3.4 versus 6.2, p = 0.028) and generate substantially higher post-COVID risk-adjusted returns (FF3 alpha: +9.06%/yr, p = 0.036) relative to matched non-celebrity peers (-3.33%/yr, p = 0.404). A DiD estimator confirms that post-COVID out-performance is orthogonal to market, size, and value risk factors (Treat×Post: 0.0084, p = 0.003). Leverage signal analysis reveals a suppression effect: controlling for leverage strengthens the celebrity coefficient while leverage independently predicts post-COVID returns (β =-0.064, p = 0.019), indicating that CGS functions as a governance screening signal identifying financially conservative firms before a credit shock materializes. Robustness checks using alternative CGS cutoffs, placebo time splits, and a point-in-time historical CGS reconstruction confirm the results. These findings suggest that celebrity board governance is a tractable pre-shock indicator of leverage discipline, with direct implications for construction firm governance, capital structure management, and institutional investment strategy.

detail.title: Schools' Level of Practice and Awareness in the Implementation of Child Protection Policy
detail.abstract: This study aimed to determine the influence of schools' level of practice, awareness, and engagement of teachers in the implementation of the Child Protection Policy (CCP). The study results are as follows: the respondents remarked that they were "extremely aware" of the implementation of the Child Protection Policy; the level of practice of schools collectively got a "highly practiced" response among the respondents of the study for the implementation of the Child Protection Policy; all of the respondents remarked "always" on the level of engagement of teachers as regards emotional engagement, social engagement with colleagues, cognitive engagement, and social engagement with learners; statistical analysis showed that teachers' level of awareness significantly influences teachers' level of engagement in implementing CPP; teachers' level of practice significantly influences their level of engagement in implementing CPP.

title: Anger Under Pressure: The LEAK Model of Life Energy Accumulation and Kinetic Release in Organizations

detail.title: Anger Under Pressure: The LEAK Model of Life Energy Accumulation and Kinetic Release in Organizations
detail.abstract: This study reexamines the mechanism through which anger arises and proposes the Anger LEAK Model, which conceptualizes anger as the outward release of life-derived energy accumulated in domains where evaluation dependence is concentrated. Previous research has primarily explained anger as either a reaction to external stimuli (Lazarus, 1991) or as an issue of emotion regulation (Gross, 1998). However, these perspectives do not adequately explain the mismatch between stimulus intensity and anger intensity, such as strong reactions to minor events or weak reactions to more serious situations. Building on the premise that anger intensity depends not on external events but on internal pressure, this study redefines anger as the release of energy accumulated within the individual. This internal pressure is assumed to develop through the accumulation of unprocessed emotions and desires under conditions of concentrated evaluation dependence. The present study conceptualizes this process as Life Energy Accumulation and Kinetic Release (LEAK) and provides a simplified mathematical representation of the conditions under which anger emerges and varies in intensity. In addition, this study argues that anger should not be treated as a single form of expression but as a structural phenomenon that can take multiple forms. A classification framework is proposed, including emotional outbursts, displacement, compensatory expressions aimed at gaining recognition, and normative internalization. This framework allows behaviors such as aggression, dominance displays, and excessive self-assertion, which have often been treated separately, to be understood within a unified structure. Furthermore, through a comparative analysis of subsystems within the same organization, this study shows that the occurrence of anger is shaped not by individual traits but by structures of evaluation dependence and patterns of interaction. These findings suggest that anger should be reconsidered not only as an individual issue but also as a structural phenomenon embedded in organizational contexts. This framework may be useful for understanding emotional dynamics in organizational settings, including workplace conflict, leadership behavior, and psychological safety. Overall, this study offers an integrative perspective on the emergence, amplification, and propagation of anger and contributes to a broader understanding of emotion in organizational behavior research.

detail.abstract: Operations management in media plays a critical role in reshaping how content is produced, structured, and optimized for generative search engines and agentic AI systems. In this context, operations management is no longer limited to coordinating workflows or supervising editorial processes; it has become a strategic intelligence layer that connects content architecture, data engineering, and algorithmic behavior. Modern media operations focus on designing intelligent workflows that ensure content is machine-readable, semantically structured, and contextually optimized. This includes the use of metadata frameworks, hierarchical information design, and semantic tagging systems that allow generative search engines to interpret, summarize, and recompose content into direct, AI-generated answers. As a result, content visibility is no longer determined only by traditional SEO factors, but by how well it aligns with generative interpretation models and retrieval-augmented generation systems. At the same time, operations management enables the integration of agentic AI systems into media ecosystems, transforming them into semi-autonomous operational environments. These agentic systems can analyze performance data, monitor audience behavior, and adjust content distribution strategies in real time without continuous human intervention. title: Algorithmic Tax Auditing and Due Process: Accountability, transparency, and Taxpayer Rights in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: University of Coimbra Institute for Legal Research

detail.title: Algorithmic Tax Auditing and Due Process: Accountability, transparency, and Taxpayer Rights in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: The growing digitization of tax administration, with the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for massive data cross-referencing and automated detection of irregularities, calls for a review of the taxpayer's fundamental procedural safeguards. This article examines the legal challenges arising from the use of algorithmic systems by the Brazilian Federal Revenue Service, with a focus on the integration of data from Pix and the e-Financeira platform into predictive risk models. It analyzes the tension between the efficiency of automated enforcement and the constitutional principles of the adversarial process, full defense, the requirement to state reasons for administrative acts, and the protection of personal data. In light of the recent Complementary Law No. 225/2026, which establishes the Taxpayer Defense Code, and Bill No. 2,338/2023 (Legal Framework for Artificial Intelligence), the new regulatory parameters for the relationship between the tax authorities and the taxpayer in an algorithmic environment are discussed. Based on a comparative analysis of experiences in the European Union, the United States, Australia, and the Netherlands, this paper proposes minimum procedural safeguards to ensure due process in algorithmic tax assessments, including algorithmic transparency, qualified human review, log preservation, and the right to technical challenge. It is concluded that responsible algorithmic tax governance requires a balance between technological innovation and full respect for taxpayers' fundamental rights.

title: The Sunglasses Protocol: A Procedural Framework for Temporal Normalization and Algorithmic Contrast in Automated Regulatory Environments

detail.title: The Sunglasses Protocol: A Procedural Framework for Temporal Normalization and Algorithmic Contrast in Automated Regulatory Environments
detail.abstract: As institutional oversight transitions toward high-velocity automated auditing, a systemic failure occurs when algorithmic "intensity" encounters administrative "fog" (latency). This paper introduces the Sunglasses Protocol, a methodology for Temporal Normalization. Derived from 21 years of forensic field experience, the Protocol addresses the "backscatter" effect-where automated systems generate false-positive cascades by failing to account for the inherent data lag in agency processing. By integrating perspectives on Information Signaling (Ross, 1988) and Asymmetric Information (Admati, 2026), this framework restores human Human Review to the audit process.

detail.abstract: The advent of automation and artificial intelligence (AI) in the hospitality sector has inaugurated novel service paradigms, exemplified by the deployment of humanoid robots in a café in Seeduwa, Sri Lanka, in 2020. While such innovations signify progress in operational efficiency and customer engagement, they simultaneously engender profound challenges to informational privacy and ethical governance. This study critically interrogates the intersection of café automation and customer privacy within the Sri Lankan context, situating its analysis within the framework of the Personal Data Protection Act No. 9 of 2022 (PDPA), global data protection regimes such as the GDPR, and international AI ethics guidelines. Drawing on a qualitative case study approach, the research identifies salient risks including inadvertent biometric data capture, opaque consent practices, surveillance-oriented profiling, and cybersecurity vulnerabilities that underscore the fragility of personal autonomy in technologically mediated hospitality environments. The findings reveal regulatory and ethical lacunae that, if unaddressed, may erode public trust and compromise legal compliance. To mitigate these concerns, the study advances a suite of recommendations: embedding Privacy by Design principles into robotic infrastructures, instituting transparent and participatory consent mechanisms, fortifying cybersecurity practices, and establishing robust governance frameworks anchored in accountability and ethical stewardship. By foregrounding both normative and practical considerations, the analysis underscores the imperative for Sri Lanka's hospitality sector to reconcile technological innovation with privacy preservation, ensuring that automation serves as an instrument of progress without subverting individual rights or dignity.

title: Network State Environmental, Social, and Governance Framework (NS-ESG): A Composite Sustainability Reporting Standard for Digitally-Native Communities Operating Across Sovereign Jurisdictions

detail.abstract: This paper proposes the Network State Environmental, Social, and Governance Framework (NS-ESG), the first composite sustainability reporting standard purpose-built for Network States — geographically distributed, voluntary, digitally-native communities that operate across multiple sovereign jurisdictions without a contiguous territory or a single recognised legal form. NS-ESG completes a four-paper research programme that began with the Network State Classification Framework (NSCF v2.1, 10.5281/zenodo.19561980), continued with the Network State Credit Rating Framework (NSCRF v1.1, 10.5281/zenodo.19562422), and was extended to output measurement by the Network State Economic Index (NSEI v1.0, 10.5281/zenodo.19563284). The existing global ESG architecture — the International Sustainability Standards Board's IFRS S1 and S2, the European Financial Reporting Advisory Group's ESRS suite under the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (post-Omnibus), the Global Reporting Initiative's Universal and Sector Standards, B Lab's V7 B Corp Standards, the United Nations Global Compact, and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials — was designed for two reporting entity archetypes: the corporate and the sovereign state. Network States are neither. They have no single jurisdiction of incorporation, no contiguous territory, no recognised treaty standing, a membership population that is fluid across borders, and a capital stack that routinely combines corporate equity, decentralised autonomous organisation (DAO) treasury, tokenised membership, and special economic zone (SEZ) leasehold. When existing ESG frameworks are applied to Network States, they fail on five structural dimensions: the legal-form problem, the cross-jurisdictional problem, the protocol-emissions allocation gap, the member-welfare portability gap, and the census-integrity (proof-of-personhood) gap. The NS-ESG addresses these gaps with a 13-indicator framework organised across four pillars: Environmental (E, 3 indicators — total network footprint including protocol emissions, chain carbon intensity, and physical-node sustainability); Social (S, 4 indicators — member welfare portability, cross-jurisdictional labour compliance, diversity of membership and governance, and dispute resolution integrity); Governance (G, 4 indicators — tokenomic equity via Nakamoto coefficient, treasury transparency, proposal integrity, and regulatory posture); and Digital Sovereignty (D, 2 indicators — data residency and proof-of-personhood integrity) — the novel fourth pillar that distinguishes NS-ESG from all adjacent frameworks. Each indicator is defined with calculation procedure, data source, validation method, normalisation anchor, and pillar weight. The composite NS-ESG score is a weighted aggregate that maps to a ten-notch rating scale (NS-ESG-AAA through NS-ESG-D) mirroring the NSCRF architecture, with suggested pillar weights of 25% Environmental, 25% Social, 30% Governance, and 20% Digital Sovereignty. The framework is applied illustratively to the same 32 Network States rated under NSCRF and scored under NSEI: Network School, Prospera/Infinita City, Zuzalu, Praxis, CityDAO, Liberland, and Afropolitan. Network School achieves the highest illustrative NS-ESG score by virtue of its operational footprint in the Forest City SFZ, formal lease agreements, and visible membership diversity, while Zuzalu scores lowest on governance continuity owing to its pop-up structure. A cross-framework dashboard — integrating NSCF taxonomic classification, NSCRF credit tier, NSEI economic score, and NS-ESG composite — is presented for each entity, demonstrating the complementarity of the four frameworks. NS-ESG is designed to be proposed as an ISO International Workshop Agreement through Standards Australia (target Technical Committee 207 Environmental Management or Technical Committee 322 Sustainable Finance), as a candidate GRI Sector Standard for Digital Communities, and as a submission to the ISSB's Sustainability Working Group when the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures technical work transfers to ISSB in Q3 2026. The framework is also aligned to the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board's ISSA 5000 Sustainability Assurance Standard, effective 15 December 2026, which provides the first global baseline for limited and reasonable assurance over sustainability information.

title: Peranan Kesatuan Sekerja dalam Masyarakat Pasca Industri di Malaysia: Sintesis Naratif dan Kerangka Konseptual Berteraskan Dinamika Global dan Konteks Sabah AMIERA NATASYA | PROGRAM HUBUNGAN INDUSTRI | FAKULTI SAINS SOSIAL DAN

detail.title: Peranan Kesatuan Sekerja dalam Masyarakat Pasca Industri di Malaysia: Sintesis Naratif dan Kerangka Konseptual Berteraskan Dinamika Global dan Konteks Sabah AMIERA NATASYA | PROGRAM HUBUNGAN INDUSTRI | FAKULTI SAINS SOSIAL DAN
detail.abstract: Peralihan kepada masyarakat pasca industri yang dicirikan oleh dominasi sektor perkhidmatan, digitalisasi ekonomi, dan kemunculan ekonomi gig telah mentransformasikan landskap hubungan pekerjaan secara global. Dalam konteks ini, kesatuan sekerja berhadapan dengan cabaran struktural yang signifikan, termasuk penurunan kadar keahlian, fragmentasi tenaga kerja, serta kesukaran dalam mewakili pekerja tidak formal. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mensintesis secara kritis peranan kesatuan sekerja dalam masyarakat pasca industri dengan memberi fokus kepada konteks Malaysia, khususnya Sabah yang mempunyai ciri ekonomi dualistik dan ketidakseimbangan pembangunan wilayah. Menggunakan pendekatan ulasan naratif, artikel ini menganalisis literatur daripada pangkalan data Scopus, Web of Science, dan Google Scholar bagi tempoh 2015-2025. Analisis tematik berdasarkan Braun dan Clarke (2006) digunakan bagi mengenal pasti pola utama dalam literatur. Dapatan menunjukkan empat tema utama: (i) transformasi struktur pasaran buruh global, (ii) cabaran representasi dalam ekonomi fleksibel, (iii) kapasiti institusi dan inovasi kesatuan, serta (iv) kerangka dasar dan perundangan. Artikel ini mencadangkan satu kerangka konseptual yang mengintegrasikan dimensi struktur ekonomi, institusi, dan strategi adaptif kesatuan sekerja. Implikasi dasar menekankan keperluan reformasi perlindungan sosial, pengukuhan dialog sosial, dan digitalisasi kesatuan. Kajian ini menyumbang kepada literatur hubungan pekerjaan dengan menawarkan perspektif kontekstual yang relevan untuk negara membangun.

title: Efficient Public Good Provision via Fundraising

detail.title: Efficient Public Good Provision via Fundraising
detail.abstract: This paper provides an institutional reinterpretation of the Green-Laffont impossibility. I show that the failure of budget balance arises from a mismatch between the bounded surplus generated by efficient provision and the informational rents required under centralized, report-dependent cost assignment. I develop a decentralized fundraising mechanism in which monetary contributions are determined through voluntary participation. Under a set of natural incentive axioms, the mechanism implements efficient public-good provision without full valuation reports. The results suggest that the impossibility reflects centralized cost assignment rather than a fundamental inefficiency of public-good environments.

title: The scope of judicial review of administrative delays: the experience of the United States

detail.title: The scope of judicial review of administrative delays: the experience of the United States
detail.abstract: Administrative delay is one of the main challenges of modern administrative law. Administrative agencies are the government bodies that interact with citizens most frequently, and the enforcement of their rights and freedoms depends on the actions of these agencies. In the United States, a special mechanism has been developed for resolving cases involving administrative delay. However, the analysis revealed that this mechanism is essentially incapable of resolving the problems it faces; nevertheless, the courts attempt to find a balance between the interests of private individuals and the agencies’ ability to solve the issues they face.

title: DO ASSETS MIGRATE? EVIDENCE BASED ON 5.9 MILLION PRICE OBSERVATIONS

detail.title: DO ASSETS MIGRATE? EVIDENCE BASED ON 5.9 MILLION PRICE OBSERVATIONS
detail.abstract: Do state transitions across the risk-return coordinates (RRC) occur randomly? We compiled a panel of 2,172 stocks and zero-coupon bonds for the period 2015-2025. Using about 5.9 million daily price observations over 2,705 trading days, the RRC was mapped onto a two-dimensional plane guided by Kernel Density Estimation (KDE). The state transitions were modeled using a fuzzified Markov chain. Based on realized risk-return state transitions, we reject three null hypotheses and find statistical support for (1) zone dependence, (2) non-random state transitions, and (3) rejection of first-order adequacy. The GARCH-filtering robustness process, based on realworld and synthetic panels with 11.4 million observations, reconfirmed our primary statistical results. The Market Migration Hypothesis posits that these movements exhibit non-random, geometric characteristics with memory. These outcomes have a profound economic impact on portfolio construction and asset pricing. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study on state transitions with memory across the KDE-guided risk-return plane.

title: Future Design Practice Framework for Creating an Action Plan toward Carbon Neutrality in a Local City: A Case Study of the Kyoto Miraimon Project
affiliations: The University of Osaka, Tohoku University and The University of Osaka - Graduate School of Engineering

detail.title: Future Design Practice Framework for Creating an Action Plan toward Carbon Neutrality in a Local City: A Case Study of the Kyoto Miraimon Project
detail.abstract: To tackle climate change toward carbon neutrality, this paper proposes a Future Design (FD)based practice framework that enables diverse stakeholders to co-create actionable plans. FD refers to the design and praxis of social systems that generate judgments and decisions considering the preferences of both current and future generations by activating a human trait called "futurability." The framework introduces two key features: developing and updating a historical timeline, which we refer to as a roadmap, and applying systems thinking through causal loop diagrams. The framework was examined in the Kyoto Miraimon Project, a platform that brings together governments, universities, companies, and public-interest organizations working toward carbon neutrality in Kyoto. We held four online workshops from July to November 2024 with a total of 13 participants from academia, government, industry, research institutions, and publicinterest foundations. The post-workshop questionnaires suggested that the framework enhanced futurability, systems thinking, and stakeholder engagement, while supporting the co-creation of 2 sustainable action plans. This study contributes both theoretically and practically to the field of futures studies. Theoretically, it extends FD research by integrating temporal (roadmap) and structural (CLD) tools into participatory workshops, showing how futurability can be translated into actionable strategies. Practically, it provides a methodology for local governments and stakeholder platforms to design shared roadmaps and action plans for sustainability transitions.

title: 3G Internet and Information Frictions in Childhood Vaccination: Evidence from India
affiliations: Masaryk University, University of Pavia - Department of Economics and Management and Sapienza University of Rome

detail.title: 3G Internet and Information Frictions in Childhood Vaccination: Evidence from India

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses secondary, de-identified survey data combined with secondary data on 3G coverage. No new data were collected from human participants for the purposes of this study. Ethical approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Vaccination rates remain high for doses delivered during routine early-life contacts, yet fall sharply for vaccines scheduled months later in low-and middle-income countries. We study whether mobile internet helps parents keep track of the immunization schedule in settings where completing later doses requires active follow-up. Using data on about 101,000 children from India's National Family Health Survey (2019-21) and an instrumental-variable strategy based on terrain ruggedness, we estimate the effect of local 3G coverage on childhood vaccination. We find that positive effects are concentrated in vaccines scheduled at 16 months, when parents must remember the timing of a return visit, while earlier doses delivered during routine contacts show little systematic response. In particular, estimated effects are positive for second-dose measles vaccination (MCV-2), Japanese encephalitis vaccination (JE-2), and the DPT booster, and become larger when the sample is restricted to age-eligible children. A timing test shows that, for JE-2, the estimated effect of 3G is negative before 16 months and positive thereafter, consistent with improved schedule adherence. Effects are also larger among less educated mothers, suggesting that digital connectivity matters more where households have fewer baseline information resources. Overall, the results indicate that gaps in later childhood vaccination partly reflect information frictions and that mobile internet can help reduce them in low-and middle-income settings.

title: The Economics of "Betting on Blood": How the US-Israeli War on Iran Turned into an Arena for Geopolitical Speculation

detail.title: The Economics of "Betting on Blood": How the US-Israeli War on Iran Turned into an Arena for Geopolitical Speculation
detail.abstract: This analytical study explores the unprecedented structural shift in the global capitalist system by 2026, wherein geopolitical crises, including the US-Israeli war on Iran, have been commodified into financial assets via "Prediction Markets" such as Polymarket and Kalshi. The paper deconstructs the architecture of "Geopolitical Casino Capitalism," highlighting the profound conflict of interest involving political elites-notably the Trump administration's inner circle-who simultaneously invest in these platforms and engineer the regulatory frameworks shielding them from state-level legal prosecution. Furthermore, the analysis exposes the critical national security threat of geopolitical insider trading, evidenced by the scandal of Israeli military officers leaking classified strike timings for financial gain. Ultimately, the study assesses how this systemic financialization of conflict creates structural incentives to prolong wars, breaches diplomatic secrecy, and severely complicates regional mediation efforts in the Middle East.

title: When Do Carbon Prices Bite? Scope 1 Exposure, Import Competition, and Firm Growth under the EU ETS

detail.title: When Do Carbon Prices Bite? Scope 1 Exposure, Import Competition, and Firm Growth under the EU ETS

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses secondary firm-level financial, emissions, price, and trade data and does not involve human participants, patients, or personal medical data. Ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
EUA carbon prices do not appear to bite all industrial firms in the same way. Using listed
industrial firms drawn from an EU27 screening universe from 2015 to 2024, I combine LSEG
firm-level financial and Scope 1 emissions data with annual EUA prices and Eurostat-based
import penetration. The empirical design compares firms facing the same annual carbon-price
environment but differing in direct emissions intensity and in the import exposure of their
country-industry cell. Import exposure is measured using capped 2015–2017 baseline import
penetration constructed from Eurostat production, import, and export data.
The main finding is that firms with higher Scope 1 intensity grow more slowly when EUA
prices are higher and when they operate in country-industry cells with higher baseline import
penetration. The result is negative and statistically significant for both sales growth and
asset growth in the baseline specification and remains negative in timing checks that exclude
2021 or exclude 2020–2021. Firm fixed-effect estimates are weaker, so I interpret the evidence
as an exposure-based pattern rather than as a fully within-firm causal estimate. I find no
consistent evidence of an immediate CAPEX response.
The evidence points to a conditional pattern: carbon prices become more visible when
direct emissions exposure meets a weaker pass-through margin. This real-side channel provides
the foundation for a broader corporate-finance question: whether banks and investors price
carbon-cost exposure, emissions-information quality, and disclosure credibility in financial
contracts.

title: Applying Regulatory Concepts to China's Deep Synthesis Regulation

detail.title: Applying Regulatory Concepts to China's Deep Synthesis Regulation
detail.abstract: This article critically examines China's Deep Synthesis Regulation using the following regulatory theories: Decision Trees, Origins of Power, Pareto Principle, Political Ideologies, Hutter & Braithwaite, Sanctions, and Command and Control. The regulation seeks to control the potential risks of deepfake use in creating fake news and misinformation. The main aim here is to access how these concepts apply to the regulation while discussing the potential positives and negatives. Decisions trees are a structured way to implement risk assessment but issues may arise because it is limited. The regulation itself gets its legal authority and power from China's national laws and the pareto principle helps to enhance public welfare without causing problems for others by reducing the risks of misinformation but could be a disadvantage to legitimate deep synthesis companies. The regulation calls for self-regulation within the industry, but this can be argued to be overshadowed by the command-and-control tone used throughout. Sanctions within the regulation are to serve as deterrents, but the offences and punishments are not clearly defined with the use of vague words which could lead to issues with enforcement later. Overall, the regulation shows the nature of China's regulatory governance, in terms of the communist nature that prioritises censorship and control of emerging technologies while trying to create a balance and promote innovation. This can be contrasted with liberal ideology of some other countries that believes in free markets and limiting intervention of the state. This regulation is the first of its kind in this area of law, and while there are some criticisms, it is an adequate start to regulating the deepfake space.

title: Uncertainty and Sticky Prices

detail.title: Uncertainty and Sticky Prices

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have no personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced this study.

detail.abstract: Economic theory conventionally treats sticky prices as an impediment to the full utilization of economic resources. This paper explores a technical approach to the opposite approach: based on the axiom of fundamental uncertainty—which replaces the axiom of perfect foresight—a link is constructed from the reduction of uncertainty to the increase in economic activity. This link provides a missing piece of the puzzle to permanently replace the prevailing perfect-foresight axiom with an uncertainty-based microeconomic foundation for uncertainty-based macroeconomics.

title: Financial Analysis of the Participation of Islamic Banking Companies in Dhaka Stock Exchange During 2005-2008

detail.title: Financial Analysis of the Participation of Islamic Banking Companies in Dhaka Stock Exchange During 2005-2008
detail.abstract: The study evaluates performance of seven full fledged private commercial Islamic banks listed in Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) in terms of Dividend policies, dividend ratios, EPS, P/E ratios and other profitability indicators, liquidity, risk and solvency for the period 2005-2008. Financial tools and techniques are applied in measuring these performances. The study found that some Islamic Banks are doing well while two Banks i.e. ICB Islami Bank and First Security Islami Bank are somehow shown poor performance in DSE. But all Islamic banks have greater opportunity to show better performance in the Stock exchange. The analysis mostly depends on secondary data. Only customers' views are taken from conversation and observation methods. Finally the study has recommended some policies for the selected banks to do well in future in the capital market.

title: Cooperation under Comparison
affiliations: University of Bonn and Cracow Univeristy of Economics

detail.title: Cooperation under Comparison

publicationDetails.detailsText:
ZEF – Discussion Papers on Development Policy No. 367, Center for Development Research, Bonn

detail.abstract: We establish a new approach to the modeling of cooperation, and we formulate a new solution concept for cooperative games. We do this by constructing a game of cooperation between individuals who exhibit distaste for relative deprivation, RD, in the sense that they experience stress when their income is lower than that of their comparators. In such a game, the sharing out of the jointly earned income between these individuals when they cooperate, as prescribed by standard solutions of cooperative games, might not be acceptable to the individuals. The stress from RD may have the upper hand. Measuring stress by RD, we thus model a setting in which two individuals who are concerned with being relatively deprived need to decide whether or not to cooperate. We term this setting an RD cooperative game, and we design a rule, the RD solution, for the distribution of the income yielded in this game. The RD solution prescribes cooperation in spite of cooperation-induced stress and preserves the spirit of standardness (an equal sharing of the gain that accrues from cooperation) for two-player games (a property shared by the main solution concepts for cooperative games).

title: China's Big Four Banks: ICBC, BOC, ABC, and CCB

detail.title: China's Big Four Banks: ICBC, BOC, ABC, and CCB
detail.abstract: Despite being a “socialist” country, China has developed an immense banking and financial sector. In particular, the “Big Four” state-owned banks of China (ICBC, BOC, ABC, and CCB) dominate the banking sector of the world’s second-largest economy. ICBC is the world's largest bank by assets and it boasts over US$220 billion in annual revenues. While there are other banks besides the Big Four active in China, the largest of which are the Bank of Communications and China Merchants Bank, these banks have much smaller scale than the Big Four at less than US$80 billion in annual revenues each. Therefore, any discussion of China’s banking and financial sector starts with the Big Four. Yet, the Big Four are somewhat inscrutable to most foreigners as their business activities are mostly limited to the China market. This article endeavors to pull back the curtain of four of the world's largest financial institutions while explaining their significance to China's industrial policy.

title: Endogenous Prizes in Security Contests

detail.title: Endogenous Prizes in Security Contests
detail.abstract: In many environments, a contest protects an activity whose revenue finances the contest: policing funded by property taxes, platform security funded by usage fees, insurance solvency funded by premiums. The prize is endogenous to the protection level. This article characterises the resulting fixed-point problem. Under primitive conditions on cost convexity, demand regularity, and attack technology, the equilibrium set forms a complete lattice with a shutdown state, a stable highsecurity equilibrium, and an unstable tipping threshold. Interior equilibria appear and vanish via saddle-node bifurcation, and all comparative statics inherit a common amplification denominator that diverges at the fold. The welfare-maximising fee lies below the revenue-maximising fee when the security externality is moderate. A continuous-time extension nests the static equilibria as stationary points.

title: When Systems Fail: The Critical Gap Between Rising Mental Health Diagnoses and Developmental Trauma Training

detail.title: When Systems Fail: The Critical Gap Between Rising Mental Health Diagnoses and Developmental Trauma Training

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This paper represents independent scholarly work with no external funding or organizational affiliations that influenced its content.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted as independent scholarly work.

detail.abstract: Over the past two decades, mental health diagnoses have risen at rates that defy explanation as simply 'an increase in illness'. This paper argues that this trajectory reflects not an epidemic of mental disorder, but a profound, systemic failure, rooted in the absence of a formal diagnostic and training framework for Developmental Trauma Disorder (DTD). Drawing on empirical research in developmental psychology, trauma science, and clinical ethics, this paper examines three interconnected systemic gaps: (1) the absence of formal DTD recognition produces critical blind spots in licensed mental health professional (LMHP) training; (2) the resulting disconnect between interpersonal trauma and emotional development drives symptom-focused rather than etiologically grounded care; and (3) unaddressed mental and developmental disruptions then cascade across the lifespan in predictable, compounding patterns. The convergence of these three systemic failures constitutes what the author terms The Trauma Gap™: the structural gap between what the mental health system is designed to deliver and what individuals actually need in order to heal. Secondary impacts, including ethical liability concerns arising from the American Psychiatric Association's documented awareness of DTD evidence, alongside its continued non-recognition, are also examined. The paper concludes with a call for transformative systemic reform: formal DTD diagnostic inclusion, restructured professional training, and a trauma-prevention paradigm that addresses the developmental origins of mental health challenges rather than managing their surface symptoms.

title: The Role of Financial Development and Financial Technology in Driving Renewable Energy Technologies: Evidence from Developed and Developing Countries

detail.title: The Role of Financial Development and Financial Technology in Driving Renewable Energy Technologies: Evidence from Developed and Developing Countries
detail.abstract: The transition to renewable energy technologies (RETs) is crucial for mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and advancing sustainable development. This study investigates the role of financial development (FD) and financial technology (FinTech) in fostering RET deployment across developed and developing economies, while also assessing the moderating effect of FinTech on the FD-RET nexus. Using annual panel data from 2000 to 2022 and applying robust econometric techniques, namely Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares (FMOLS) and Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares (DOLS), the analysis reveals that FD exerts a significant positive influence on RET deployment in both groups of countries. FinTech directly promotes RET adoption, and in developed economies, it further amplifies the effectiveness of FD through the interaction effect. By contrast, in developing economies, institutional weaknesses and structural barriers constrain FinTech's ability to reinforce the role of FD. Moreover, real GDP per capita, population growth, and energy prices emerge as additional drivers of RET deployment, although the effect of energy prices remains muted in contexts with fossil fuel subsidies. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of strong financial markets, effective regulatory frameworks, and institutional quality in facilitating clean energy transitions, providing actionable policy insights for accelerating renewable energy adoption worldwide.

title: Digital Money, Artificial Intelligence, and the Architecture of National Power: A Framework for Zambia's Sovereign Positioning in the Global Restructuring of Money, Technology, and Minerals - 2026 to 2035

detail.title: Digital Money, Artificial Intelligence, and the Architecture of National Power: A Framework for Zambia's Sovereign Positioning in the Global Restructuring of Money, Technology, and Minerals - 2026 to 2035

No employer, client, contracting entity, or institutional affiliation has commissioned, reviewed, approved, directed, or in any way influenced the content, findings, or recommendations of this Series. The views expressed are solely those of the Author in a strictly independent research and analytical capacity.

detail.abstract:
Three concurrent structural transformations are reshaping the global economy: the artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout, the transition to programmable tokenised settlement systems for international trade, and the intensified geopolitical competition for critical minerals. This five-volume series argues that these forces are not independent trends but mutually constituting layers of a single emerging system and that the physical centre of that system is copper, placing the Zambian Copperbelt at the strategic intersection of the 21st century's defining economic transition.

Drawing on primary data from the IMF, BIS, World Bank, IEA, and Zambian government sources, the series develops an evidence-based Five-Pillar Sovereign Positioning Framework for transforming Zambia from a passive resource exporter into an active architect of its own economic future. The framework covers: a Copper Sovereign Wealth Fund structured on the IMF Santiago Principles; a phased beneficiation mandate modelled on the Indonesian nickel precedent; an Energy Transition Industrial Zone anchored by emergency renewable energy procurement; a Bank of Zambia payment sovereignty programme including wholesale CBDC development and mBridge observer engagement; and an Al-assisted geological intelligence programme. All recommendations are explicitly aligned with Zambia's National Critical Minerals Strategy 2024-2028, 8th National Development Plan 2026-2030, National Al Strategy 2024-2026, and Vision 2030.

title: Wait-for-Discount: Strategic Deferral, Health Deterioration, and the Hidden Costs of Cost-Sharing Design

Additionally, Oikawa received funding from the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS, 23K12494).

keywords: Administrative Claims Data (NDB) JEL Classification Codes: I11

detail.abstract: We investigate strategic responses to anticipated healthcare price reductions. Exploiting Japan's age-70 threshold, we document significant wait-for-discount behavior within universal health insurance. Using administrative claims and a balanced panel, we show that standard regression discontinuity overstates price elasticity by conflating structural demand with intertemporal substitution. The immediate elasticity (-0.200) reflects a transitory spike, while the steady-state stabilizes at -0.088. Heterogeneity analysis reveals a behavioral decoupling: healthy individuals strategically time elective procedures, exhibiting a 5% drop in admissions pre-threshold and an 8.5% spike post-threshold. Crucially, deferral triggers a deterioration mechanism: inpatient expenditures surge by 4.3% later in the post-reform year, suggesting that forgoing routine maintenance care necessitates intensive treatment. Cost-benefit analysis reveals severe targeting inefficiency: every 1 yen saved by a patient through deferral incurs approximately 47 yen in additional social costs.

title: INTERNAL DEVELOPER PORTALS AS ENABLERS OF DEVELOPER EXPERIENCE: A SYSTEMATIC AND GREY LITERATURE REVIEW

detail.title: INTERNAL DEVELOPER PORTALS AS ENABLERS OF DEVELOPER EXPERIENCE: A SYSTEMATIC AND GREY LITERATURE REVIEW

keywords: of Computer Science Internal Developer Portals

detail.abstract: Internal Developer Portals (IDPs) have emerged as a key component of modern platform engineering practices, aimed at improving Developer Experience (DevEx) by providing centralized, self-service access to tools, services, documentation, and infrastructure. As software systems grow in complexity and development teams become increasingly distributed, organizations are adopting IDPs to reduce cognitive load, streamline workflows, and enhance productivity. Despite growing industry adoption, the academic understanding of how internal developer portals influence developer experience remains fragmented, with limited integration of empirical research and practitioner insights. This study presents a systematic and grey literature review that synthesizes evidence from peer-reviewed academic sources and industry-driven grey literature, including technical reports, engineering blogs, and organizational case studies. The objective is to examine how internal developer portals function as enablers of developer experience and to identify the mechanisms through which they impact efficiency, satisfaction, and workflow optimization. The findings indicate that IDPs significantly enhance developer experience by enabling self-service capabilities, reducing dependency on platform teams, and standardizing development workflows through concepts such as golden paths and automation pipelines. They also contribute to faster onboarding, improved collaboration, and more consistent software delivery processes. However, the study identifies several challenges, including integration complexity, organizational resistance, and the lack of standardized evaluation metrics for DevEx improvements. By combining academic rigor with industry perspectives, this review provides a comprehensive understanding of internal developer portals and their role in shaping modern software engineering practices. The study highlights the need for further empirical research to establish standardized frameworks for measuring developer experience and to evaluate the long-term impact of IDPs on organizational performance.

title: Digital Illicit Trade and the Geography of Retail Drug Markets: Evidence from Cryptomarkets Using a Gravity Framework

detail.title: Digital Illicit Trade and the Geography of Retail Drug Markets: Evidence from Cryptomarkets Using a Gravity Framework

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses publicly available scraped data from darknet market archives obtained through academic data-sharing agreements with Nicolas Christin (Carnegie Mellon University), David Décary-Hétu (Université de Montréal), and Judith Aldridge (University of Manchester). No human subjects were recruited or contacted. IRB review was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether bilateral retail drug transactions on darknet cryptomarkets conform to gravitymodel predictions, and whether geographic distance frictions differ across production-technology classes. Using listing-level data from the Hikari darknet market archive, collapsed to a bilateral country-pair × drug-type × month panel, I estimate Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood (PPML) gravity models with high-dimensional fixed effects. A strong distance elasticity of approximately-2.05 is confirmed in the pooled baseline-a lower bound on the true friction, given nonclassical measurement error in the advertised-destination variable. Contrary to expectations, the interaction between the synthetic drug indicator and log distance is economically negligible and statistically insignificant across all specifications. More substantively, contiguity, common official language, and colonial ties-variables that enter positive in virtually every licit-goods gravity study-carry large negative coefficients here. An extensive-intensive margin decomposition reveals that these negative facilitation effects operate almost entirely through the intensive margin: conditional on a bilateral route being active, trade volumes are dramatically lower between proximate and linguistically similar countries. This pattern is consistent with enforcement coordination risk suppressing realized transactions on short, jurisdictionally familiar corridors. Together, the distance elasticity and the negative facilitation effects suggest that the geography of illicit online drug trade is shaped as much by interdiction risk as by shipping cost.

title: The Fatherhood Development Platform: A Systems Framework for Father Engagement in Maternal and Child Health

detail.title: The Fatherhood Development Platform: A Systems Framework for Father Engagement in Maternal and Child Health

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is employed as a community health worker with Healthy Start Inc., Pittsburgh, PA. The framework presented in this paper was developed through direct field experience in that role. No financial relationships with external organizations influenced this work. No external funding was received in support of this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

keywords: fatherhood as a determinant of health
fatherhood in maternal and child health

detail.abstract:
Father engagement in maternal and child health remains inconsistent, despite substantial evidence that involved fathers improve outcomes for mothers, infants, and families. Current approaches rely predominantly on voluntary participation and programs. These often fail to address the broader culture of fatherhood or account for variability in men’s readiness, stability, and identity.

This paper introduces the Fatherhood Development Platform, a stage-based and systems-oriented framework that positions fatherhood as a measurable determinant of health. Central to this model is the Fatherhood Archetype Framework, which identifies five dynamic operating states: Wounded, Disconnected, Emerging, Builder, and Mentor. For the purposes of this framework: 'Wounded' refers to a state where a man is affected by prior trauma or emotional injury; 'Disconnected' indicates physical or emotional absence from family or systems; 'Emerging' describes a father beginning to engage or uncertain in his role; 'Builder' is an actively involved father shaping his family environment; and 'Mentor' refers to a father who guides others based on accumulated experience. These states influence how fathers engage with their families and health systems.

The platform integrates behavioral observation, cultural engagement, and system design. It aims to improve father participation in maternal and child health outcomes. It also introduces a cultural engagement model rooted in Third Space environments, allowing for upstream influence on identity and behavior beyond clinical or programmatic settings.

This framework provides a scalable approach for public health systems seeking to improve maternal and infant outcomes by engaging fathers as active contributors to family stability and health.

title: The Effect of Macroeconomic Variables, Banking Variables, and Institutional Quality on Banking Lending Power in Iraq
affiliations: , University of Mazandaran (UMZ) and University of Mazandaran (UMZ)

detail.title: The Effect of Macroeconomic Variables, Banking Variables, and Institutional Quality on Banking Lending Power in Iraq

keywords: system generalized method of moment (SGMM) approach

detail.abstract: The primary aim of this research is to examine the factors influencing the performance of banking loans in Iraq. The study utilizes unbalanced panel data over eighteen years, from 2005 to 2022, focusing on eighteen selected listed banks at the Iraq Stock Exchange (ISX) based on data availability. Data sources include annual financial reports from selected banks, the Central Bank of Iraq, and World Bank indicators (WDI) covering banking, macroeconomic, and institutional quality information. The relationship is estimated using a system generalized method of moment (SGMM) approach. The results indicate that certain banking variables such as bank assets, return on assets (ROA), and deposit-to-capital ratio have a positive and significant impact on lending power in Iraq, while the real deposit rate has a negative influence. Among macroeconomic variables, the inflation rate, real exchange rate, and liquidity growth have significant adverse effects on lending power, while economic prosperity and GDP growth yield positive effects. During economic booms, bank lending power increases, while it decreases during recessions. The study also highlights the positive and significant impact of institutional quality on bank lending power, indicating the importance of robust legal and regulatory institutions in establishing a stable and predictable financial environment, and fostering confidence among banks to engage in lending activities within the Iraqi economy.

title: The Hungry Mind of US Youth: How Universal Free Meals Narrow Student Achievement Gaps

detail.title: The Hungry Mind of US Youth: How Universal Free Meals Narrow Student Achievement Gaps
detail.abstract: State-wide universal free meal (UFM) policies promote both educational equity and child well being by ensuring that all students have access to nutritious meals at school. With eight states having implemented UFMs in either 2022 or 2023, I employ a state-level staggered difference-in-differences design to estimate the effect of UFMs on mean test scores for students in grades 3–8 over pre- and post-pandemic years. I find that standardized test scores increased by 0.028 standard deviations (s.d.), on average, in states that implement UFMs. Mean math scores increased by 0.035 s.d. and reading language arts (RLA) raised by 0.020 s.d.. Most notably, economically disadvantaged students saw a 0.062 s.d. increase in overall test performance, with a 0.064 s.d. and 0.062 s.d. raise to math and RLA, respectively. The effects are driven by non-white males from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.

title: Optimal Bonus Structure under Strategic Communication

detail.title: Optimal Bonus Structure under Strategic Communication
detail.abstract: Bonus structures are a common tool used by organizations to incentivize workers' efforts. Halac, Lipnowski, and Rappoport (2021) assumes workers cannot observe each others' contracts and derives the optimal bonus structure that uniquely implements work. In reality, however, workers can strategically communicate with each other before exerting effort. If workers are allowed to talk to each other, could the entire structure collapse, leaving them stuck in an uninformative equilibrium? I study the optimal bonus structure that uniquely implements work when communication is allowed. I model the interaction as a two-stage game: a communication stage where workers communicate with each other, and an action stage where workers choose whether to work. I show that the optimal bonus structure is robust to communication that takes the form of Bayesian persuasion and cheap talk, in the sense that the unique equilibrium involves workers sharing no information in the communication stage and always working in the action stage.

title: The Other Iranian Energy Crisis: How Israeli Gas Disruptions Will Reshape East Mediterranean Energy Infrastructure
affiliations: Bar-Ilan University - Department of Political Studies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest to declare

detail.abstract: The global oil shock created by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz obscured a second energy crisis that unfolded much closer to Israel's borders. The month-long shutdown of Israel's Leviathan and Karish gas fields, caused by repeated Iranian and Hezbollah missile attacks, was the longest gas export disruption since Israel began supplying gas to Jordan and Egypt. This interruption, the third in the past two years, exposed how dependent Israel's neighbors have become on Israeli gas for electricity generation, and reinforced a broader strategic lesson for them. Viewing Israeli supplies as unreliable, Jordan, Egypt and even Syria are now more likely to deepen hedging strategies by expanding renewables, maintaining costly backup fuels, increasing LNG flexibility, and looking for alternative regional transport and energy corridors. The bright side is that this shift may strengthen the case for IMEC by reframing it less as a Europe-oriented transit initiative and more as a domestic infrastructure project for ensuring intra-regional energy security.

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is conceptual in nature and does not involve human participants, personal data, or experimental subjects. Therefore, no ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
The global payments ecosystem has evolved into a fragmented network of heterogeneous financial rails, including traditional banking systems, card networks, real-time payment infrastructures, and blockchain-based settlement layers. Prior work introduced intelligent payment systems as decision-driven architectures capable of optimizing transaction routing across these rails using an intelligence layer (Nandi, 2026).

This paper extends that foundation by proposing a conceptual framework for AI-native payment systems, in which financial transactions are autonomously executed by intelligent agents based on intent, policy, and real-time contextual signals. The framework introduces an Agentic Layer that enables continuous evaluation and independent execution of financial transactions without direct human intervention.

By reframing payments as autonomous decision-execution systems, this study contributes to the evolving discourse on intelligent financial infrastructure. The paper outlines the architectural components of AI-native systems, presents a detailed scenario walkthrough illustrating autonomous execution, and highlights key limitations and areas for further research.

title: On the Story of the Blind Men and the Elephant

detail.title: On the Story of the Blind Men and the Elephant

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no conflicts of interest associated with this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. It was conducted as an independent study.

detail.abstract: This essay reexamines the classic parable of the "Blind Men and the Elephant" from an epistemological perspective. The author suggests that in a world of infinite complexity-be it in economics, science, or philosophy-every observer is essentially a "blind man" limited by their own perspective. Rather than seeking a definitive "whole," the essay explores the validity and interconnectedness of individual, primal moments of cognition. It reflects on the commonality between the "groping" of a scholar and the intuition of a chef, emphasizing the value of raw, direct perception over the rush to logical conclusions.
