reference: Eagle Intel Reports, 13 March 2026
title: Nuclear Tests-Again? Great-Power Competition and the Fraying of the Nuclear Testing Moratorium

detail.title: Nuclear Tests-Again? Great-Power Competition and the Fraying of the Nuclear Testing Moratorium
detail.abstract: Intensified competition and distrust among the great powers-manifested in regional wars and a stalled arms control environment-have increased the possibility of renewed nuclear testing. This paper examines the structural and strategic conditions under which China, Russia, or the United States might resume yield-producing tests of their nuclear weapons, despite the collective self-imposed moratorium in place since the 1990s. It traces the collapse of Cold War arms control architecture, the weakening of institutional constraints and normative taboos, and the asymmetric incentives created by China's rapid nuclear expansion. The paper analyses the legal framework surrounding the Comprehensive Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) and its failure to enter into force, and examines three plausible resumption scenarios: a North Korean tipping point, a South Asian chain reaction, and an equilibrium restoration dynamic. It concludes that the forecast for nuclear testing will ultimately depend on the balance between Washington's commitment to uphold the international status quo and Beijing's determination to revise it, with the war in Iran further underlining how nuclear issues continue to drive great-power strategy.

title: Improving Students' Understanding of Bank Reconciliation Statements Through Participatory Teaching Methods: An Action Research Study

detail.title: Improving Students' Understanding of Bank Reconciliation Statements Through Participatory Teaching Methods: An Action Research Study
detail.abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of participatory teaching methods in improving students' understanding of bank reconciliation statements, a foundational yet persistently challenging topic in accounting education. Despite its importance to financial accuracy, internal controls, and audit readiness, bank reconciliation is often taught using traditional lecture-based approaches that limit student engagement and hinder conceptual understanding. As a result, many students struggle to analyze reconciliation items and apply procedures accurately. Using a descriptive action research design, this study implemented a range of participatory instructional strategies, including structured classroom discussions, regular individual assignments, small-group learning activities, guidance and counseling, and continuous supervision. Data were collected from multiple sources, including questionnaires, interviews, classroom observations, assignments, and test results and assessment records, both before and after the intervention. The use of multiple data sources allowed for triangulation and strengthened the reliability of the findings. The results indicate substantial improvements in student participation, confidence, conceptual understanding, and performance in preparing bank reconciliation statements following the implementation of participatory teaching methods. Students demonstrated greater analytical reasoning, reduced error frequency, and increased willingness to engage actively in accounting lessons. The findings contribute to the accounting education literature by providing classroom-based evidence that learner-centered pedagogical approaches enhance understanding of core accounting procedures. The study offers practical implications for accounting educators seeking to improve student engagement, develop analytical skills, and strengthen mastery of foundational accounting concepts essential for professional practice.

title: Price Regulation in Consumer Financial Markets: The Case of Mortgage Escrow

detail.title: Price Regulation in Consumer Financial Markets: The Case of Mortgage Escrow
detail.abstract: We use the 2018-2024 Home Mortgage Disclosure Act data in a difference-indifference framework to evaluate the effects of regulating the interest rate lenders pay borrowers on mortgage escrow funds. Our analysis suggests the policy may not have its intended effect. Lenders offset much of their lost revenue with higher up-front fees. The greatest effect is on low-income borrowers. High-income borrowers are unaffected, suggesting a regressive cross-subsidy. The regulation also lowers the chances applications are originated, mostly from lender denials, and also with greatest effect on low-income applicants. Less origination indicates a distortion of trade signaling welfare losses from the policy.

reference: Eagle Intel Reports, 10 February 2026
title: A World Without Nuclear Arms Control? New START's Expiry and the Transition to a Multipolar Nuclear Order

detail.title: A World Without Nuclear Arms Control? New START's Expiry and the Transition to a Multipolar Nuclear Order
detail.abstract: The expiry of New START-the last Russian-U.S. nuclear arms control treaty-marks a further collapse of the nuclear arms control architecture arduously built during the Cold War. For the first time in decades, there are no legally binding ceilings on the great powers' nuclear arsenals. This paper examines the structural drivers behind this development and analyses the pathways, risks, and scenarios that characterize the emerging multipolar nuclear order. It traces how worsening great-power relations, Russia's deployment of exotic nuclear systems, China's rapid nuclear buildup, and a growing range of disruptive technologies-artificial intelligence, hypersonic glide vehicles, cyber weapons, and quantum computing-are reshaping the strategic environment in ways that existing treaty frameworks were never designed to address. The paper identifies three plausible scenarios: an unconstrained nuclear wilderness resembling the first nuclear age; a return to great-power strategic cooperation; and a more probable middle path in which non-treaty constraints, resource limits, and strategic complexity sustain a degree of stability. It concludes that New START's demise, while alarming, may paradoxically strengthen strategic stability by generating a level of uncertainty that diminishes leaders' confidence in achieving victory through nuclear escalation.

title: ARCHITECTURAL PATTERNS AND COMPONENTS OF INTERNAL DEVELOPER PLATFORMS: EVIDENCE FROM MULTIVOCAL LITERATURE

detail.title: ARCHITECTURAL PATTERNS AND COMPONENTS OF INTERNAL DEVELOPER PLATFORMS: EVIDENCE FROM MULTIVOCAL LITERATURE

keywords: of Computer Science Internal Developer Platforms

detail.abstract: Internal Developer Platforms (IDPs) have become a key enabler of modern platform engineering by providing standardized, self-service environments that simplify software development and deployment processes. As organizations increasingly adopt cloud-native architectures, microservices, and DevOps practices, the need for scalable and reusable platform structures has intensified. However, despite growing industry adoption, there remains limited consolidated understanding of the architectural patterns and core components that define Internal Developer Platforms across both academic and industry contexts. This study presents a multivocal literature review that synthesizes evidence from peer-reviewed academic publications and grey literature sources, including technical reports, engineering blogs, and real-world case studies. The objective is to identify and analyze the dominant architectural patterns and foundational components that constitute Internal Developer Platforms, as well as to understand how these structures support platform scalability, developer productivity, and operational efficiency. The findings reveal that IDPs are typically built using modular and layered architectures, often incorporating components such as service catalogs, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code modules, observability tools, and self-service interfaces. Common architectural patterns identified include platform-as-a-product, microservices-based platform design, and layered abstraction models that separate infrastructure concerns from developer-facing interfaces. These patterns collectively aim to reduce cognitive load, improve system consistency, and enable faster software delivery cycles. The study also highlights that while industry literature provides rich practical insights into platform implementation, academic research on the architectural standardization of IDPs remains limited and fragmented. This gap underscores the need for more empirical studies to validate architectural models and evaluate their long-term effectiveness. By integrating both academic and industry perspectives, this review provides a comprehensive overview of Internal Developer Platform architectures and contributes to a deeper understanding of how these systems are structured and evolved to support modern software engineering practices.

title: Biodiversity Loss, Firm Risk, and Bank Exposure: Evidence from Italian SMEs

detail.title: Biodiversity Loss, Firm Risk, and Bank Exposure: Evidence from Italian SMEs
detail.abstract: We study whether biodiversity loss affects the financial performance of Italian small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and whether these firm-level exposures generate indirect risk to the banking system. Our dataset is an unbalanced panel of approximately 449,800 Italian SMEs observed in 2014-2024, constructed by merging firm-level accounting information with high-resolution geospatial measures of biodiversity loss and climate-related shocks. The regression sample, after restricting to observations with non-missing values for the variables required in the baseline specifications, comprises about 327,200 firms and 1.86 million firmyear observations. We address endogeneity concerns by instrumenting biodiversity loss with exogenous drought and wildfire conditions, and we construct a novel bank exposure measure that links firms to nearby bank branches through distance-based credit allocation. Fixed-effects estimates suggest statistically significant correlations between biodiversity loss and firm outcomes, but these associations are not robust to instrumental-variable identification. In specifications using a highly relevant drought-based instrument, the estimated average effect of biodiversity loss on profitability, revenues, and costs is economically small and statistically indistinguishable from zero. At the same time, the smallest firms exhibit greater sensitivity: biodiversity loss is associated with lower profitability among microenterprises. Aggregating firm-level exposure through branch networks reveals substantial heterogeneity in biodiversity-related risk across banks, driven by differences in branch footprints and the geographic concentration of exposed SMEs. In general, the results highlight that nature-related risks may have limited average effects at the firm level while still generating uneven and localized exposure within the banking system, with implications for nature-risk monitoring and prudential policy.

title: Demographics, Innovation, and Cross-Border R&D Capital Allocation

detail.title: Demographics, Innovation, and Cross-Border R&D Capital Allocation
detail.abstract: Does population aging reshape national innovation capacity and the cross-border allocation of R&D capital? Using a panel of up to 140 countries (1990-2024), I estimate the relationship between demographic structure-captured by principal components of the age distribution (Z₁, Z₂, Z₃)-and multiple innovation indicators including R&D expenditure, patenting activity, high-tech exports, and cross-border FDI, conditioning on income level (log GDP per capita) and a Z₁ × income interaction. The most robust output-side finding is that aging predicts lower high-tech export share (Z₁ =-73.0, p = 0.012), surviving income conditioning virtually unchanged from the unconditional baseline (-75.3). The patent result, previously suggestive (Z₁ =-6.91, p = 0.032), loses significance entirely under income conditioning (Z₁ =-3.32, p = 0.314); the Z₁ × log_gdp_pc interaction (-0.229, p = 0.049) absorbs the effect, revealing that the patent-aging relationship was substantially an income proxy. On the input side, old-age dependency remains strongly associated with higher R&D spending (old_dep = +4.51***, R² = 0.335), attenuated 15% from the unconditional estimate (+5.31) but fully robust. Income level is independently significant for both R&D (log_gdp_pc = +0.186, p = 0.004) and high-tech exports (+6.34, p < 0.001). A new finding emerges for cross-border capital: non-OECD FDI inflows are strongly positively associated with aging (Z₁ = +82.4, p = 0.007), suggesting that aging developing economies attract foreign capital-a result masked in the full-sample specification. The demographic innovation penalty is concentrated in middle-income countries. These findings complement earlier work on demographic capital deepening (Papers 8-9) and provide the broadest crosscountry evidence available given innovation data coverage (47-63 countries spanning all income levels and regions).

title: Governing AI Trajectory in NHS Foundation Trusts: A Lifecycle Governance Framework for Quantifying the Financial Cost of Clinical AI Investment Trajectory Deterioration at Board Level

detail.title: Governing AI Trajectory in NHS Foundation Trusts: A Lifecycle Governance Framework for Quantifying the Financial Cost of Clinical AI Investment Trajectory Deterioration at Board Level

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is Founder and Director of AI Governance Direct Limited, which delivers AI governance services commercially. The methodology described in this paper forms part of that commercial offering.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded. The Picken Governance Institute / AI Governance Direct Limited.

detail.abstract: NHS foundation trusts are deploying artificial intelligence across diagnostic support, patient pathway management, and workforce scheduling at a rate that clinical governance frameworks are not equipped to assess. This paper presents a healthcare-specific application of PAAPM+ to NHS board-level clinical AI governance, extending CAPM-derived AI return assessment with a three-factor Lifecycle Multiplier to produce strategy-adjusted expected returns. The central governance instrument is the Governance Decay Premium (GDP_AI): a formally defined financial metric quantifying the value being destroyed by clinical AI governance trajectory deterioration before it reaches NHS financial statements. Applied to three AI systems in a synthetic NHS foundation trust, the framework identifies £187,400 in total governance value and £41,157 in combined annual GDP_AI invisible to every governance mechanism currently in operation.

title: NIEDERER NETWORK Humans as Fractal Beings A Theoretical Framework

detail.title: NIEDERER NETWORK Humans as Fractal Beings A Theoretical Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a theoretical framework for understanding human emotion as energy rather than state, moving through a shared medium of consciousness in spiral fractal patterns consistent with structures found throughout the natural world. Current psychological and neuroscientific models treat emotions as discrete, opposing, or linearly arranged experiences. This paper proposes a different architecture. Fear and faith are not opposites. They are a shared composite at different degrees, moving through The Shared Ocean in the continuous pattern of the spiral. Every human emotion is a current of that composite, a unique and constantly shifting recipe of both. No two people experience the same emotion identically. No single person experiences the same emotion twice in exactly the same way. The physical body is proposed as an avatar-an identity marker carried through the shared medium-while the individual spark of consciousness extends beyond it, overlapping with others through The Shared Ocean of collective consciousness. This shared medium operates as a fractal network, self-similar and recursive, following the same mathematical principles observable in nature.

title: What Countries Use AI, and What For? Intensity and Breadth of AI Adoption Across Over 100 Countries

detail.title: What Countries Use AI, and What For? Intensity and Breadth of AI Adoption Across Over 100 Countries
detail.abstract: How intensively do countries use generative AI, and how broadly does that usage spread across tasks? Using over 800 thousand Claude AI conversations from more than 100 countries during one week in February 2026, we document two dimensions of crosscountry AI adoption. On intensity (per-capita AI usage), countries with higher income, stronger scientic output, a more services-oriented economy, and more developed AI-policy readiness use AI more per capita. On breadth (how evenly usage spreads across task categories), per-capita adoption, country size, the stage of structural transformation, and labor-market participation are the main correlates. Mapping each country's AI usage on dierent tasks into an AI-diusion space, a network of broad task domains linked by revealed co-adoption patterns, we nd that lower-income countries concentrate more in a software core while higher-income countries activate an expanding periphery of legal, health, creative, and nancial tasks.

title: The Fiduciary Theory of Entropy: Collapsing the Uncertainty Coefficient (U c ) in Tokenized Real-World Assets

detail.title: The Fiduciary Theory of Entropy: Collapsing the Uncertainty Coefficient (U c ) in Tokenized Real-World Assets
detail.abstract: Global capital markets currently operate on "Paper Fiction"-retrospective, narrative based auditing that ignores the real-time kinetic decay of high-consequence assets. This paper introduces the Sovereign Oracle Protocol, a decentralized fiduciary framework that utilizes 8-decimal thermodynamic titration to eliminate the Uncertainty Coefficient (Uc). By defining a new physics-based discount rate (Φ), we present a deterministic formula for Adjusted Net Present Value (NPVadj) that serves as the immutable price floor for Real-World Asset (RWA) tokenization. This framework provides a regulatory "Safe Harbor" - the Paul Atkins Shield - allowing for presumptive compliance with SEC and EU MiCA standards through mathematical proof rather than manual oversight.

title: Exploring the Effect of Self-Efficacy on Burnout and Job Commitment of Elementary Teachers: A Basis for Wellness Program
affiliations: Angeles University Foundation and La Consolacion University Philippines

detail.title: Exploring the Effect of Self-Efficacy on Burnout and Job Commitment of Elementary Teachers: A Basis for Wellness Program

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of the Philippines. Informed consent was obtained from all individual participants included in the study. The protocol was approved by the Research Ethics Committee of La Consolacion University Philippines.
declarations.funderStatement: Personally funded

detail.abstract: This study aimed to determine the significant effect of teachers' self-efficacy on their burnout and job commitment. The key findings are as follows: among highly proficient teacher-respondents, the degree of self-efficacy was rated as "Quite a Bit" across four indicators: decision-making, school resources, instructional self-efficacy, and enlisting parental involvement while proficient teacher-respondents, ratings varied across the six indicators. Efficacy to influence, instructional self-efficacy, and efficacy to enlist community involvement were rated "Quite a Bit," while disciplinary self-efficacy, efficacy to enlist parental involvement, and efficacy to create a positive school climate were rated "Very Much." For level of burnout, highly proficient teachers were rated "High" in terms of career satisfaction. However, both groups generally reported a "Low" level of burnout concerning perceived administrative support and coping with job-related stress. Regarding attitudes toward learners, most teachers reported a "Moderately High" level of burnout. A significant difference in job commitment was found between highly proficient and proficient elementary teachers. However, no significant differences were observed between the two groups in terms of self-efficacy and burnout. Furthermore, job commitment was significantly affected by teachers' self-efficacy, whereas burnout was not. Based on these findings, a development wellness program is proposed for adoption by schools to support teacher well-being and professional growth.

title: Decomposing Marginal Utility: Experiential and Relational Components

detail.title: Decomposing Marginal Utility: Experiential and Relational Components
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a simple decomposition of marginal utility into two components: marginal experiential utility and marginal relational utility. Total utility is expressed as the sum of experiential utility, arising from improvements in lived conditions, and relational utility, arising from evaluation and comparison. Differentiation yields a corresponding decomposition of marginal utility into experiential and relational components. The contribution is to show that diminishing marginal utility may be interpreted as a compositional phenomenon: marginal experiential utility declines rapidly with wealth, while marginal relational utility diminishes more slowly or remains persistent. As a result, the marginal utility of wealth reflects not only curvature within a utility function but also shifts in the relative importance of its underlying components. The decomposition provides a simple and portable framework for analyzing the relationship between wealth and well-being.

title: Reading the Fed: Central Bank Text as a Forecasting Signal

detail.title: Reading the Fed: Central Bank Text as a Forecasting Signal
detail.abstract: We introduce a two-step framework for macroeconomic forecasting: Claude (Anthropic API) reads Federal Reserve FOMC minutes and Beige Books and returns structured five-dimensional sentiment scores, which enter as exogenous regressors in both a Bayesian VAR and a simple AR model. By separating text reading from forecasting, the design substantially reduces the memorization problem that undermines direct LLM forecasting. Evaluated out-of-sample over 2020Q1-2024Q4 across six targets-GDP growth, CPI and core PCE inflation, unemployment, the federal funds rate, and the 10Y-2Y spread-the LLM-augmented AR beats the plain AR in 11 of 12 variable-horizon combinations, with the largest gains during the 2021-2023 inflation surge where LLM sentiment signals led the quantitative data. A diagnostic experiment further reveals that score levels outperform first differences in stressed regimes, where the Fed's sustained tone carries cumulative signal across multiple meetings; first differences improve only in stable periods when level scores inherit institutional optimism. The forecasting value in central bank text is transmitted gradually, not in any single document.

title: Economic Fallout of US-Israel and Iran War on Critical Economic Indicators: A Contextual Analysis of the Select Asian Nations and the European Union

detail.title: Economic Fallout of US-Israel and Iran War on Critical Economic Indicators: A Contextual Analysis of the Select Asian Nations and the European Union

declarations.ethicsApproval: The study fully abides all the ethical standards and parameters .
declarations.funderStatement: There is no funding for this study from any institution, agency and government.

detail.abstract: This study examines the economics of the Gulf War and its subsequent economic impact on the investment, trade, inflation, and ecosystems of two prominent South Asian nations, including India and Japan, and the European Union. The ongoing military conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran has rapidly escalated into one of the most serious geopolitical crises of 2026. Although centered in the Middle East, its effects are globalparticularly for countries heavily reliant on energy imports, global trade routes, and regional stability. The two continents are significantly dependent on the oil imports from the Gulf countries and in return are exporting multiple merchandise to the region. The war-driven disruptions in the Gulf region have halted the oil imports to these countries and have fueled genuine economic uncertainty and a complex business environment in the region. The imminent fuel shortage has triggered multiple economic spillovers in the sample countries, which off late may depress their continued economic progressive momentum. By comparing vulnerabilities in energy security, trade, investment, and diplomatic responses, this study aims to highlight how such a conflict reverberates across regions and impacts their critical economic indicators. The present study's fresh introspection of a multitude of quantitative information of different economic indicators in these nations shows a swift decline in the global financial market and the slowed investment ecosystem and fear of emerging supply bottlenecks hint at the chance of a deep economic discomfort, inflationary tendency, and push income and employment slack in many sectors, coupled with a shift towards stockpiling of oil reserves and exploring alternative energy securing options while upholding geo-political equations.

title: Malicse -Thermodynamic Framework for Sustainability | 1 A Thermodynamic and Systems Theory Framework for Sustainability: Capitalism, Primitive Societies, and the Universal Law of Balance in Nature

detail.title: Malicse -Thermodynamic Framework for Sustainability | 1 A Thermodynamic and Systems Theory Framework for Sustainability: Capitalism, Primitive Societies, and the Universal Law of Balance in Nature
detail.abstract: This paper develops a unified scientific framework integrating ecological economics, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, and systems theory to formalize the conditions for environmental sustainability. We introduce the Universal Balance-Feedback Framework (UBFF), grounded in four universal laws-System Integrity, Balance in Nature, Feedback Dynamics, and Interconnected Nodes-and demonstrate that modern capitalist economies systematically violate these conditions through exponential consumption and technology growth. A rigorous thermodynamic derivation shows that economic activity necessarily produces entropy at a rate exceeding natural regeneration capacity, rendering infinite growth thermodynamically impossible in any finite biosphere. The framework is extended into a discrete dynamical system with Lyapunov stability analysis, demonstrating that only trajectories satisfying the balance constraint I(t) ≤ R converge to sustainable equilibria. The theory is validated against empirical data from the Philippines (PSA 2023, World Bank 2023) and global planetary boundary data (Rockstrom et al., 2009; Steffen et al., 2015). Simulation results distinguish collapse versus sustainable scenarios. Policy levers for restoration of balance are formally derived. This work identifies the UBFF Balance Principle as a unifying meta-theoretical contribution beyond existing IPAT and ecological economics literature.

title: Rising rent prices are Holding the United States back, especially the younger population

detail.title: Rising rent prices are Holding the United States back, especially the younger population
detail.abstract: The topic I will be discussing in this paper is how rising rent prices are affecting young adults and families in the United States. It is clear that there is a need for affordable housing. Throughout the whole United States, rent prices are rising and holding back younger generations from moving out on their own, and preventing others from having more disposable income, which in return is slowing the economy. Looking at a graph from reputable sources such as, "U.S. department of treasury" we can analyze how these rising rent prices are going to affect the United States as a whole. The shortage of housing and the increased demand is what is causing rising rent prices. A huge problem with rising rent prices is that they cause inflation and less money being spent on other essentials, which in return slows down economic growth.

title: From KYC to Exploitation: Structural Failures of AML in Fintech Platforms and the Need for Embedded Regulatory Design

detail.title: From KYC to Exploitation: Structural Failures of AML in Fintech Platforms and the Need for Embedded Regulatory Design
detail.abstract: This study aims to demonstrate that the failure of Anti-Money Laundering (AML) systems in fintech platform environments is not merely an operational deficiency, but a structural problem, and to propose the need for a shift in regulatory paradigms as a corresponding solution. Focusing on Know Your Customer (KYC) operational practices within platform-based electronic financial services, this study analyzes complex failure factors arising from the interaction of data input structures, operational processes, and organizational decision-making. The findings indicate that AML failures primarily stem from: (1) reduced data reliability due to lack of standardization in data inputs, (2) weakened risk detection capabilities resulting from throughput-oriented operational structures, and (3) governance frameworks that prioritize user experience over compliance. Furthermore, through cases such as multiaccount usage and multiple virtual account structures, it is confirmed that existing AML systems remain confined to expost monitoring and fail to provide effective preventive control. To address these limitations, this study proposes an Embedded Regulatory Design that integrates regulatory functions directly into transaction structures. This approach shifts AML from a surveillance-based, reactive model toward a pre-emptive, execution-based framework, offering a new regulatory direction suited to the digital financial environment.

title: FROM FORMAL EQUALITY TO SUBSTANTIVE JUSTICE: Deterrence, Income Inequality, and Legal Legitimacy in Fixed-Rate Fine Systems

detail.title: FROM FORMAL EQUALITY TO SUBSTANTIVE JUSTICE: Deterrence, Income Inequality, and Legal Legitimacy in Fixed-Rate Fine Systems
detail.abstract: This paper began with a traffic jam. In the United States and Turkey, across different cities and different years, I repeatedly observed the same pattern: when traffic came to a complete halt, the vehicle racing through the emergency lane was almost always a luxury car. The thought was simple but unsettling; this driver probably knows a fine is coming, and does not care. The same fine would not stop me either, but it would hit my budget disproportionately. For that vehicle, the amount was pocket change. That observation, and a second one; watching people slip through emergency subway exits in New York not out of indifference but out of a felt sense that the system had already failed them; motivated this paper's central question: does a fixed-rate fine system actually deter equally across income groups? The answer this paper develops is no, and the consequences of that asymmetry run deeper than is commonly recognized. The paper introduces the Deterrence Income Threshold Hypothesis (DITH): the genuine deterrent effect of a fixed-rate fine is inversely proportional to income, declining to symbolic levels above a certain socioeconomic threshold and thereby transforming legal compliance from a necessity into an economic choice. An original distinction follows: fixed-rate systems simultaneously cultivate privilege-driven violation in upper groups and normalize necessitydriven violation in lower groups. Empirical evidence from Ferguson, Missouri and California grounds the theoretical argument. Tyler's procedural justice framework provides the legitimacy mechanism. Comparative analysis of Finland and the United States tests the hypothesis across institutional contexts. A graduated hybrid reform framework is proposed, built around verified net income, a wealth adjustment coefficient, penalty bands, and alternative sanction options.

title: How Childcare Costs Affect Working Parents Macy Lee Parsons

detail.title: How Childcare Costs Affect Working Parents Macy Lee Parsons
detail.abstract: How do childcare costs affect the decisions parents make on working part-time, full-time, or not at all? This paper includes research and personal communication in the form of interview summaries to analyze what real parents decide to do about childcare today and what the data shows in trends. Overall, research shows that prior to free childcare in the state of New Mexico, more and more parents were staying home (especially if they had larger families) because they could not afford daycare. However, with the changing laws in the state of New Mexico, now dozens of mothers and fathers are returning to work because childcare is free.

title: The Way of Sowing: A Vision for Sustainability

detail.title: The Way of Sowing: A Vision for Sustainability
detail.abstract: This paper develops the idea of the "way of sowing" as an experiential and theoretical vision for sustainability. It begins from a personal encounter with restoration ecology at Colorado State University, where the author first watched Frédéric Back's animated film 'The Man Who Planted Trees' and later conducted fieldwork in the degraded landscapes of western Colorado under the guidance of Mark W. Paschke. Through this autobiographical narrative, the paper reflects on ecological restoration not merely as a technical procedure, but as a moral, cultural and intergenerational practice: one prepares the soil, selects native species, records both survival and failure, and then allows nature to do its part. In dialogue with the kingfisher fables by Vuong Quan Hoang, the paper reconnects these lessons with Eastern philosophical traditions-especially the Vietnamese synthesis of Confucian, Buddhist and Daoist values articulated through cultural additivity and the Culture Tower. The central argument is that sustainability cannot be reduced to green technology, policy design or finance. At its deepest level, sustainability requires a civilisational ethic of sowing: disciplined action, non-possessive giving, humility before nature, and trust in futures that one may never personally witness.

title: A Cap-and-Damp Framework for Credit-Cycle Stability Through Tradeable Maturity Mismatch Permits

detail.title: A Cap-and-Damp Framework for Credit-Cycle Stability Through Tradeable Maturity Mismatch Permits

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Procyclical maturity transformation through shadow banking now exceeds pre-2008 levels, amplifying credit-cycle oscillations in ways that may exceed the corrective capacity of discre tionary monetary policy. We propose the CLAMP (Credit Leverage Automatic Market Pricing) framework, which integrates an automatic PID monetary policy rule with a cap-and-damp market for tradeable maturity mismatch permits, enabling financial entities to internalize the systemic cost of maturity transformation through market-discovered prices. We derive the coupled ODEsystem, obtain the effective damping coefficient analytically, and conduct counterfactual analysis using open FRED and Z.1 data from the 2008 crisis. Across a 768-run parameter sweep, the counterfactual median reduction in peak-to-trough credit swing under CLAMP is approximately 27 percent and the median credit-volatility reduction is approximately 70 percent. Adiagnostic assessment of 2025Q4 conditions indicates that the short-term-funding size index reaches 224 on the 4-component shadow composite (repo, ABCP, MMF, CP) and 333 on the whole-market composite (which adds commercial-bank deposits), with both composites indexed to 2000–2003 average = 100 and weighted by stock-proportional 2005–2007 dollar shares; these levels surpass the 2007 pre-crisis peaks of 155 and 163 respectively. Forward projections under three crisis-trigger scenarios suggest CLAMP may reduce GDP drawdowns by approximately 34 to 51 percent across scenarios under the central calibration ( Aexp = 1.0), moderating to 19 to 30 percent under the conservative Aexp = 0.5.

title: Seasonal Employment and Its Impact on the Economy

detail.title: Seasonal Employment and Its Impact on the Economy
detail.abstract: This paper looks at how seasonal employment affects the economy in Farmington, New Mexico. Some jobs only happen during certain times of the year, like construction or tourism (Connie Mack World Series, Fair, Navajo Dam) and even retail during the holiday seasons, which causes employment to go up and down. I used data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) and San Juan County to see how unemployment changes over time. The results show that while seasonal jobs help during busy times, they can also make things less stable when work slows down. Overall, seasonal employment plays an important role in the local economy.

title: WEIRD versus WARED; What Joseph Henrich Left Unsaid!

detail.title: WEIRD versus WARED; What Joseph Henrich Left Unsaid!
detail.abstract: This article provides a critical reassessment of the psychological model known as WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialised, Rich, and Democratic), which was originally proposed in 2010 by Joseph Henrich and his colleagues. Drawing upon economic and geopolitical data spanning the years 2024 to 2026, it is argued that the assumed connection between economic development and Western individualistic psychology has been fundamentally severed. The emergence of new economic powers in the East, such as China and India, alongside innovative welfare models in Singapore and the nations of the Persian Gulf, signifies the formation of wealth without liberalism and a form of modern collectivism. On the other hand, the phenomenon of wealth precarity in the West has led to a return of subsistence stress levels and kinship dependencies that stand in direct contradiction to the original premises of the WEIRD model. Ultimately, by introducing the WARED (Wisdom-based, Ancestral, Relational, Experiential, and Deep-rooted) framework, the article explains the necessity of transitioning towards a model that reflects the psychological diversity of today's multipolar and digital world with greater precision.

title: Oil and Gas: Foundational Pillars to San Juan County's Economy

detail.title: Oil and Gas: Foundational Pillars to San Juan County's Economy
detail.abstract: This paper explores the effects that the oil and gas industries have on San Juan County, New Mexico's economy. By examining data like Gross Domestic Product (GDP), employment, and benefits to other industries in 2025, the results clearly show the impacts that oil and gas have in this area. These key industries have shown to have positive influence on all points of research, proving their undeniable importance.

title: Legitimacy and the Fluid Singaporean Welfare State

detail.title: Legitimacy and the Fluid Singaporean Welfare State

publicationDetails.detailsText: Sociology Compass: e70197

detail.abstract: This paper develops a theory of the fluid welfare state, in which legitimacy rather than efficiency constitutes the central constraint of welfare governance. Using a dynamic model of government–citizen interaction, we show that a state that adjusts its welfare messaging across social groups enhances legitimacy when the persuasive benefit exceeds the credibility cost. The framework is inductively derived from the case of Singapore, which exemplifies how a small, open, and fiscally disciplined East Asian productivist welfare state can sustain public trust through performance and communication rather than extensive redistribution. As welfare communication increasingly takes place through digital platforms and social media, the capacity to adapt these narratives can be a powerful tool for all regimes. The concept of the fluid welfare state therefore provides a framework for understanding how contemporary governments, particularly those facing fiscal and demographic constraints, can preserve welfare legitimacy through adaptive persuasion rather than expansionary spending.

title: Peranan Kesatuan Sekerja dalam Konteks Masyarakat Pasca Industri di Malaysia: Satu Kerangka Konseptual

detail.title: Peranan Kesatuan Sekerja dalam Konteks Masyarakat Pasca Industri di Malaysia: Satu Kerangka Konseptual
detail.abstract: Transformasi ekonomi global ke arah masyarakat pasca-industri telah mengubah corak pekerjaan, hubungan industri dan peranan kesatuan sekerja. Kesatuan kini berdepan tekanan akibat fleksibiliti pasaran buruh, digitalisasi dan pertumbuhan ekonomi gig yang mencabar model perwakilan tradisional. Artikel ini mensintesis secara kritis peranan kesatuan sekerja dengan fokus kepada Malaysia dan Sabah. Menggunakan pendekatan ulasan naratif, kajian ini meneliti literatur dari tahun 2014 hingga 2024 melalui pangkalan data utama, dan dianalisis menggunakan pendekatan tematik. Empat tema utama dikenal pasti: perubahan landskap kerja global, realiti kesatuan sekerja tempatan, kapasiti institusi dan penglibatan pemegang taruh, serta kerangka dasar dan perundangan. Dapatan menunjukkan bahawa walaupun keahlian dan pengaruh kesatuan menurun, institusi ini masih penting dalam perlindungan sosial, advokasi pekerja dan keseimbangan kuasa pekerjaan. Di Sabah, cabaran seperti dominasi sektor tidak formal, pergantungan kepada buruh migran dan jurang pembangunan menambah kerumitan fungsi kesatuan. Oleh itu, artikel ini mencadangkan konsep "kesatuan adaptif" yang menekankan inovasi, penggunaan teknologi digital dan kerjasama pelbagai pihak. Implikasi dasar menuntut reformasi institusi buruh yang lebih inklusif dan responsif terhadap perubahan pasaran kerja semasa.

title: History as Evolution: The Case of China *
affiliations: London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE)

detail.title: History as Evolution: The Case of China *
detail.abstract: This paper studies cultural change in historical China. I ask how major economic, political, and social transformations reshaped cultural expression, and how these changes accumulated in later textual records. I use historical poetry to construct time-varying measures of religious and moral themes, including Buddhism, Daoism, folk religion, and filial piety, as well as attitudes toward markets, merchants, and emperors, and emotional expression. The long-run series show substantial movement over time. Buddhism, Daoism, folk religion, and filial piety follow distinct trajectories; favorable references to markets and merchants rise around the Song; favorable references to emperors decline; and emotional expression shifts with the living-standards chronology emphasized in the Great Divergence literature. I then use disaggregated poetry data to study the Song commercial revolution. Counties with denser Song zhen networks, a measure of commercial-administrative infrastructure, show clearer increases in the salience and favorable evaluation of merchants than in attitudes toward markets themselves. Finally, I use local gazetteers to study cultural change in a narrower time window and across a broader set of counties, focusing on antisociality before and after the Taiping Rebellion. Counties exposed to Taiping occupation recorded higher post-1850 antisociality, even after accounting for earlier antisociality and dierences in gazetteer coverage.

title: Shrinkflation: Smaller Packages, Same Prices-Implications for inflation Measurement and Consumer Purchasing Power Author: Alexi Yazzie

detail.title: Shrinkflation: Smaller Packages, Same Prices-Implications for inflation Measurement and Consumer Purchasing Power Author: Alexi Yazzie
detail.abstract: This paper examines shrinkflation and its impacts on the inflation measurement in the US. Using data from the Federal Reserve Economic Data, the study analyzes CPI trends in food and household goods from 2015 to 2025. The paper will explore on how reductions in product size can act as hidden price increases. The finding suggests that shrinkflation may reduce consumers' real purchasing power while not being fully captured in traditional inflation measures.

title: Name Brand vs. Generic: Why Do We Pay More?

detail.title: Name Brand vs. Generic: Why Do We Pay More?
detail.abstract: This paper will explain why name-brand products cost more than generic store brands. I used real prices from a grocery store to compare similar items like cereal, bread, and chips. I also use basic economic ideas to explain why these price differences happen. The results show that companies charge more because of their brand name, advertising, and how people think about the product. Overall, this paper shows how brands affect prices and how people decide what to buy.

title: The temporal architecture of deliberation under emerging technologies

detail.title: The temporal architecture of deliberation under emerging technologies
detail.abstract: Standard treatments of time preference identify mortality risk, impatience, uncertainty, inflation, and income as determinants of the rate at which future states are discounted. These do not adequately account for the temporal compression characteristic of contemporary decision-making contexts: shortened memory horizons; accelerating response time requirements; fragmented attention in algorithmic content environments; and with AI-generated choice options that outpace the volitional capacity required to evaluate them. I propose an extension: information velocity-the rate at which informational inputs to deliberation are generated, revised, and superseded-operates as a distinct structural determinant of time preference. High algorithmic velocity drives high information velocity, producing institutional latency at a level where human deliberation remains essential for volitional choices about what there is the most reason to want. The effects of technological change and information velocity on time preference are not uniform. Some developments compress deliberative horizons; others extend them through temporal extension, exogenous institutional reference points, or biophysical reference systems resistant to informational compression. The distinction runs along the computational versus volitional knowledge axis, shifting analysis from how to accommodate technological change within existing discount rate frameworks to what such change is doing to the institutional conditions under which discount rates form.

title: Dialektik 'UpSkilling' dan Pendemokrasian Kemahiran: Analisis Konseptual Perubahan Teknologi Berpincang Kemahiran (Skill-Biased Technological Change) terhadap Modal Insan di Sabah

detail.title: Dialektik 'UpSkilling' dan Pendemokrasian Kemahiran: Analisis Konseptual Perubahan Teknologi Berpincang Kemahiran (Skill-Biased Technological Change) terhadap Modal Insan di Sabah
detail.abstract:
Transformasi teknologi global yang dipacu oleh kemajuan pesat dalam automasi, kecerdasan buatan, dan digitalisasi ekonomi telah memperkukuh fenomena “Skill-Biased Technological Change” (SBTC) yang secara sistematik meningkatkan permintaan terhadap tenaga kerja berkemahiran tinggi. Transformasi ini turut memperluas jurang ketidaksamaan dalam pasaran buruh global dan mencabar struktur pembangunan modal insan di wilayah membangun. Dalam konteks ini, pendekatan “upskilling” sering diketengahkan sebagai strategi dominan bagi meningkatkan daya saing tenaga kerja, namun pendekatan tersebut dikritik kerana cenderung mengabaikan kekangan struktural yang mengehadkan akses kepada peluang pembelajaran. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mensintesis secara kritis hubungan dialektik antara “upskilling” dan pendemokrasian kemahiran, dengan fokus terhadap implikasi SBTC terhadap pembangunan modal insan di Sabah, Malaysia. Pendekatan ulasan naratif digunakan dengan menganalisis literatur daripada pangkalan data Scopus, Web of Science, dan Google Scholar bagi tempoh 2010 hingga 2025, serta mengaplikasikan analisis tematik refleksif berdasarkan Braun dan Clarke (2006). Dapatan mengenal pasti empat tema utama, iaitu landskap global SBTC, ketidaksamaan kemahiran dalam konteks Sabah, kapasiti institusi, dan evolusi dasar pembangunan tenaga kerja. Sintesis menunjukkan bahawa keberkesanan upskilling adalah terhad tanpa pendekatan inklusif yang menekankan pendemokrasian kemahiran. Oleh itu, artikel ini mencadangkan kerangka hibrid yang mengintegrasikan kecekapan ekonomi dan keadilan sosial sebagai asas kepada strategi pembangunan modal insan yang lebih inklusif dan lestari.

title: Banks to Markets
affiliations: The University of Sydney - Discipline of Finance and

detail.title: Banks to Markets
detail.abstract: Households' increased allocation of savings outside banks raises the question of how this shift occurs and its effects on the banking sector. We show that local expansion of brokerage intermediation, measured as the local presence of securities brokers, reallocates household savings away from bank deposits. Using a staggered adoption of the Broker Protocol in a shift-share instrumental variables design, we find that a 1 percentage point increase in brokerage intermediation reduces bank deposits by 2.4 percent. These outflows coincide with higher local equity wealth, and banks do not offset by offering higher deposit rates or increasing funding from alternative sources. Banks that are more exposed to brokerage intermediation reduce small business lending. The results are not explained by stock market performance alone. Instead, they highlight a novel link between the evolving financial system and household portfolio allocation.

title: Home Field Advantage: Local Credit Specialization and Demand Capture

detail.title: Home Field Advantage: Local Credit Specialization and Demand Capture
detail.abstract: Community banks have declined by roughly half since 2000, yet causal evidence on what specialized local lenders contribute to real economic outcomes remains limited. I test whether the composition of local lenders affects who captures the gains from a positive demand shock. The 2005 Renewable Fuel Standard created an exogenous increase in ethanol-driven corn demand. I exploit this shock across U.S. Corn Belt counties that differ in farm-bank intensity (the share of local deposits held by FDIC-designated farm banks, a regulator-defined subset of community banks specialized in agricultural lending), using a propensity-score-matched difference-in-differences design on a comparison sample of roughly 300 counties. A one-standard-deviation increase in farm-bank intensity raises post-shock farm earnings by 9.5% (p = 0.003), with no differential pre-trends and effects emerging precisely in 2005-2006. The mechanism is informational rather than credit supply. Farm-bank lending grows less even as income grows faster, corn yields are unchanged, and borrower-side interest expense grows less only on the relationship-intensive operating-loan margin, not on the collateralized real-estate margin where borrowers can readily substitute to other lenders. This asymmetry distinguishes a relationship capital mechanism that prior work has hypothesized but rarely identified causally. The results imply that aggregate lending data systematically understate the value of specialized local lenders, and that community-bank consolidation may carry real economic costs that conventional credit-availability measures fail to capture.

title: Legal Tender -A Barbarous Relic in the Digital Currency Era

detail.title: Legal Tender -A Barbarous Relic in the Digital Currency Era
detail.abstract: We focus on the digital tender of central bank digital currency (CBDC). We first discuss, from an economic point of view, the approach of legal experts, as developed in two International Monetary Fund (IMF) papers. We then show that making CBDC legal tender is taken for granted but is predicated on a bold assumption, that of assimilating CBDC to a "digital form of cash", and that, in combination with aggressive pricing, it could lead to a loss in economic welfare. We finally conclude.

title: Improving the Black-Scholes Model Using Underlying Asset Skewness Measures 1

detail.title: Improving the Black-Scholes Model Using Underlying Asset Skewness Measures 1
detail.abstract: This study examines whether higher-moment adjustments improve Black-Scholes option pricing and hedging performance in the KOSPI 200 index option market. Using KOSPI 200 index options from 2015 to 2024, we compare the Black-Scholes benchmark with a kurtosis-only model and two skewness-adjusted specifications based on historical sample skewness and an option-implied asymmetry proxy. Performance is evaluated using pricing errors, discrete delta-hedging errors, and subsample analyses by moneyness and maturity. We find that the kurtosis-only model has lower MAE and RMSE than Black-Scholes in the full sample (MAE 2.0732 vs 2.0995). The same direction holds across ATM, ITM, OTM groups and across short and long maturities. Adding skewness on top of kurtosis does not help. Historical sample skewness raises MAE to 2.1944, and the option-implied asymmetry proxy raises it to 4.2300, with the worst errors in ITM and short-maturity contracts. The hedging results show the same pattern. In our KOSPI 200 sample, kurtosis is the only higher moment that consistently improves on Black-Scholes.

title: Regional-Global Models, Business Integration and Future Pathways SSRN WORKING PAPER | PREPRINT | MAY 2026

detail.title: Regional-Global Models, Business Integration and Future Pathways SSRN WORKING PAPER | PREPRINT | MAY 2026

keywords: Agri-Digital Transformation; Vision 2050; Secondary Data Triangulation; Proxy Indicator Methodology;

detail.abstract:
India has achieved a historic transformation in agricultural production, yet farmer incomes remain persistently low. This paper identifies the source of this paradox: a structural shift from production constraints to a Farmer Business Capability Gap—a deficit in the financial, market, institutional, digital, and aggregation capacities required to convert output into income.

To measure this gap, the paper introduces the Farmer Business Capability Index (FBCI), a five-dimensional composite framework capturing farmer readiness as market-integrated economic agents. Using proxy indicators across 15 Indian states, the analysis reveals a striking empirical pattern: capability, not production, explains income variation. A near-perfect rank correlation (Spearman ρ = +0.94) is observed between FBCI scores and farm household income, with key anomalies—such as Kerala, Rajasthan, and low-capability debt-heavy states—fully explained within this framework.

Comparative evidence from high-performing agricultural economies underscores the central finding: income growth in agriculture is driven less by what farmers produce, and more by how effectively they participate in markets.

Building on this, the paper proposes a National Farmer Business Platform (NFBP)—an integrated enterprise intelligence ecosystem—alongside complementary policy reforms in financial literacy, aggregation, export stability, and digital integration. A Vision 2050 roadmap outlines measurable targets for exports, income growth, import reduction, and value addition.

The paper argues that India’s next agricultural transformation will not come from producing more, but from enabling farmers to operate as informed, connected, and capable economic actors. It offers a conceptual framework, empirical grounding, and policy pathway for that transition.

title: Policy Momentum Harvesting in the Chinese A-shares Market

detail.title: Policy Momentum Harvesting in the Chinese A-shares Market
detail.abstract: It is understood that traditional momentum strategies have performed inconsistently in the Chinese A-shares market, but value strategies have performed well. This paper argues that such variability arises from regulatory policy cycles acting as exogenous shocks that conditionally drive momentum, amplifying trends during easing phases while disrupting them during tightening phases. In this context, momentum should be viewed as a time-varying and natural consequence of regulatory policymaking. We incorporate spanning tree networks to isolate momentum pockets during such regulatory shocks. Drawing upon data from 2010 to 2025, the objective is to explore a dynamic process through the application of minimum and maximum spanning trees within a case study framework. Our focus will be on six preselected regulatory events, which will be mapped onto equity market clusters identified through tree-based methods. We believe that the experiment will provide a renewed opportunity for researchers and market participants to reignite the development of a better understanding of the momentum anomaly, particularly during market dislocations in the context of Chinese A-shares. Our fundamental contribution lies in two aspects: first, we link market regime shifts to regulatory events and engage with relevant A-shares literature from a practical perspective; second, we provide a helpful empirical case study to hopefully inform academics and practitioners on the never-ending topic regarding the essence of the momentum factor.

detail.abstract: Price elasticity of demand (Ed) quantifies the responsiveness of quantity demanded to price changes, assuming other factors remain constant. Traditional methods of calculating Ed, such as the percentage method and point method, often produce mathematically inconsistent results in the computation of marginal revenue (MR) and total revenue (TR) changes when analysed bidirectionally along the demand curve. This paper critically reviews exiting methods of calculating price elasticity of demand such as percentage method and point method with the help of illustrative explanation and highlights inconsistencies in them and to overcome these inconsistencies, the midpoint (arc elasticity) method is introduced, which employs the arithmetic mean of price and quantity between two points on the demand curve. Using geometric and algebraic analysis, the paper shows that this method ensures mathematically consistent and direction-independent calculation of Ed, MR and TR changes. The findings provide a more reliable framework for both theoretical modelling and applied economic analysis, enhancing the accuracy of revenue projections and pricing strategies.

title: Virtual Human Capital: The Transition of Afghan Women from Formal Employment to Digital Entrepreneurship

publicationDetails.detailsText: International Journal of Creative Research Thoughts (IJCRT) 2026 IJCRT | Volume 14, Issue 2 February 2026 | ISSN: 2320-2882

detail.abstract: This paper explored the forced transformation of Afghan Female's human capital through a systematic exclusion from formal employment after the august 2021. With the usage of secondary sources evidence from UN agencies and recent academic literatures, they depicts that participation of female in acquiring education, healthcare, social activity and public sector tasks has been collapsed, with only 7 percent of women are employed. In response, women have redirected skills into informal digital and social commerce, now serving as the primary income source for over 80 percent of women-led households. The findings show that this shift represents survival-driven informalization rather than empowerment. Severe financial exclusion, lack of human resource structures, and fragile digital infrastructure constrain sustainability. Grounded in human capital and informal labour frameworks, the study argues that virtual work stabilizes short-term livelihoods but suppresses long-term returns and professional growth.

title: Licenze di tecnologia nel diritto della concorrenza UE: accordi e disaccordi tra regimi d’esenzione per categoria e linee direttrici

detail.title: Licenze di tecnologia nel diritto della concorrenza UE: accordi e disaccordi tra regimi d’esenzione per categoria e linee direttrici
detail.abstract: Il saggio esamina il coordinamento tra regolamento d’esenzione per categoria degli accordi di trasferimento tecnologico (“TTBER”), in scadenza il 30 aprile 2026, la proposta di riforma del 2025 e i regimi antitrust UE paralleli e complementari in materia di accordi verticali e di ricerca e sviluppo, nonché con le linee guida sulla cooperazione orizzontale. Dopo un breve inquadramento storico, l’analisi si concentra su tre profili di disallineamento normativo: i) criteri di riparto dell’esenzione non convergenti per gli accordi ibridi, a cavallo tra finalità distributive e trasferimento tecnologico, e definizioni non pienamente allineate dell’esclusiva contrattuale, che possono incentivare qualificazioni opportunistiche al fine di rientrare nel regime antitrust più favorevole; ii) disallineamenti sostanziali e temporali nella nozione di concorrenza potenziale, con possibili esiti incoerenti tra cooperazione a monte in ricerca e sviluppo e licensing a valle; iii) persistenti margini d’incertezza sugli elementi di cooperazione negli accordi di licenza, in particolare quanto a scambi informativi e negoziazione coordinata di più licenziatari. Per chiudere, il contributo propone riallineamenti mirati e criteri operativi volti a rafforzare la prevedibilità applicativa e la coerenza del quadro regolatorio.

title: The Soft Leadership Formula for Military People in the AI Age

detail.title: The Soft Leadership Formula for Military People in the AI Age
detail.abstract: We are on the cusp of something big today in the AI age. Finally, military people can find a softer side to their leadership by using artificial intelligence. By connecting with their artificial intelligence (AI) assistant, the military leader can discuss how to run a meeting, take on an innovative project, and be more prepared to build interpersonal skills. Artificial intelligence sums up what it is presented with, praises the military leader, then asks a pertinent question. With AI, several modes can be tapped, such as but not limited to: Assistant, Therapist, Language Tutor, and Storyteller. This article combines the mindsense idea with both the military leader and the softer side of leadership to incorporate the intuitive knowledge of having artificial intelligence at your side.

title: How Higher Cigarette Taxes Are Changing Smoking Habits in Farmington, New Mexico

detail.title: How Higher Cigarette Taxes Are Changing Smoking Habits in Farmington, New Mexico
detail.abstract: This paper looks at how rising cigarette taxes are affecting smoking habits in Farmington, New Mexico. I used price data from 2023 to 2026 for three cigarette brands, LD, Basic, and Marlboro along with interviews from local people and store employees. I am a smoker myself and never have I stopped thinking of taxes for my cigarettes. The results show that higher prices do make a difference, but not always in the way people expect. Some smokers cut back or think about quitting, but many just switch to cheaper brands or keep buying cigarettes anyway. All in all, cigarette taxes seem to have some effect, but they don't impact everyone the same way.

title: A Grammar of the Distinctive Competence Development at the Firm for the Solution of Systemic Problems (JIM, 2020)

detail.title: A Grammar of the Distinctive Competence Development at the Firm for the Solution of Systemic Problems (JIM, 2020)
detail.abstract: Competitiveness results from factors beyond the structural conditions and organisational boundaries, such as inter-organisational cooperation. Using evidence gathered in Brazilian credit unions, this work reveals a type of social process for generating organisational capabilities and economic goods in firms satisfying needs defined by social structures in order to solve market failures and structural deficiencies in their socioeconomic systems. An exploratory and descriptive multiple case study with longitudinal qualitative data collected from a sequence of decision-making events of deterministic nature has made possible theoretical refinements to the model of competence development in the firm. It relies upon a systematic, computer-supported Process Tracing technique using a formal language model. Two case studies showed that firms hold relationships of cooperation and contribution with partners and nonmarket structures in their organisational and environmental surroundings whenever their performance is constrained by competitive problems of systemic nature, for which of market price and state intervention.

title: Deconstructing China's AI ecosystem

detail.title: Deconstructing China's AI ecosystem
detail.abstract: China's growth in the field of artificial intelligence is quite distinct, with a coherent top-down state support system (Webster et al. 2017). As AI-related enthusiasm escalates, 'AI stocks' now account for approximately 44% of the S&P 500 market capitalization (Lock and Walters 2025). This aggravates the risk of formation of a potential speculative bubble, alluding to the theory of Kindleberger cycles (Morck 2021). This article examines the coherent self-fulfilling AI policy of China and then analyzes the challenges and structural vulnerabilities of the same.

detail.abstract: This study aimed to explore the challenges of teachers in instructional practices and their job performance. The results of the study are as follows: there were three (6) major themes identified regarding the challenges encountered by teachers in performing their job-related tasks in schools, (a) recognizing the challenge, (b) experiencing challenges of instructional practice, (c) encountering the most challenging experience, (d) categorizing the nature of instructional practices challenges, (e) mitigation strategies to address challenges, and (f) recognizing the challenges. Based on the findings, it is recommended that teachers may devote more time and give ample assessment recommendations to locate the least learning competencies of the learners, basis for remediation and intervention. Furthermore, their full and strict implementation of the department’s call to concentrate and focus on the pedagogical approaches of teaching specified in the instructional design of curriculum and to continue contextualize the curriculum based on the needs and locality of the learner.

detail.abstract: This case focused on Netflix, one of the distinguished companies in the digital streaming industry, and its top management team responsible for strategic growth, content investment, and corporate development as they faced a critical inflection point for the organization in that Netflix experienced its first reduction in subscribers in 2022, which coincided with the growing competition from Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, and HBO Max. The case focused on a strategic dilemma between whether Netflix should focus on internal optimization (strengthening original content, operational efficiency, and making use of advanced data analytics) or external growth (large-scale acquisitions). This tension has been articulated by the company's attempted acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, which raised concerns about financial risks, regulatory oversight, and possible misalignment with Netflix's innovation-driven and decentralized culture. Although the acquisition was ultimately abandoned, it highlights the broader issue of striking a balance between aggressive expansion and long-term sustainability in a highly dynamic market. The case discussed competitive strategy, digital transformation, and high-stakes decision-making under uncertainty and provided enough flexibility for instructors in strategic management, marketing, and digital business disciplines.

title: HANK After Cantillon: Two Hidden Premises and a Breakeven Condition

detail.title: HANK After Cantillon: Two Hidden Premises and a Breakeven Condition
detail.abstract: The Heterogeneous Agent New Keynesian (HANK) literature claims that unanticipated monetary expansions benefit the poor by eroding their nominal debt — the balance-sheet channel. This claim rests on two premises built into the standard framework by construction: that new money reaches all agents simultaneously, and in equal proportion. Both exclude the Cantillon effect — the permanent redistribution from late to early recipients when money enters at a specific point and propagates with a lag. We embed staggered and potentially asymmetric receipt into a Two-Agent New Keynesian (TANK) model and derive the breakeven debt ratio at which the two channels exactly offset. The breakeven condition is linear in the receipt gap, with a slope that is analytically exact — independent of nominal rigidity, baseline income, and the functional form of the price adjustment rule. Under symmetric injection, the breakeven ratio at the empirical midpoint transmission lag of 18 months falls below the observed household debt-to-income range of 10–16, allowing the balance-sheet channel to survive. Under the income-growth divergence ratio of five to one documented during the QE period, the breakeven ratio rises beyond any observed household debt ratio by a factor of three to five. The HANK distributional claim is not a theorem. It is the simultaneous, symmetric-injection special case of a more general condition, and the burden of demonstrating that the true parameter values lie in the region where the claim holds rests with its proponents.

title: India: The Emerging Market for the Twenty-First Century

detail.title: India: The Emerging Market for the Twenty-First Century
detail.abstract: India has more stock market history than any emerging market in the world. Data for East India Co. stock begins in 1601, domestic trading in India began in 1836, and by World War I, over 500 companies were trading daily in India, more companies than in any country in the world except for the United Kingdom, the United States, France and Germany. Shares that listed in Bombay, Calcutta and London before World War I behaved differently because each represented different sectors of the economy. India went through five bubbles as a result of wars inside and outside of India. Today, India has the fifth largest stock market in the world listing over 7,500 companies with a market cap over $5 trillion. Indian stocks have performed well during the twenty-first century, and there is no reason why India shouldn't continue to show high rates of growth in the years to come.

title: Autonomous, Agentic and Generative AI Systems -The Future of Business Technology: Triumph of Human Augmentation or Harbinger of Human Diminishment? A Critical Examination (2025-2035)
affiliations: and Nanjing University of the Arts

detail.title: Autonomous, Agentic and Generative AI Systems -The Future of Business Technology: Triumph of Human Augmentation or Harbinger of Human Diminishment? A Critical Examination (2025-2035)
detail.abstract: The rapid maturation of Agentic AI autonomous, goal-directed systems capable of multi-step reasoning, adaptive planning, tool integration, and independent execution and Generative AI, which creates novel content, code, designs, and insights, is fundamentally reshaping business technology. This article critically examines whether these autonomous systems represent a triumph of human augmentation delivering unprecedented productivity, innovation, and cognitive liberation or a defeat for human agency, through risks of skill atrophy, ethical erosion, accountability diffusion, and power concentration. Drawing on the most recent 2025-mid-2026 empirical evidence from Gartner, Stanford HAI, McKinsey, Deloitte, ABI Research, and others, the analysis reveals explosive growth alongside significant implementation challenges. Key data points underscore the momentum: Gartner projects that 40% of enterprise applications will feature task-specific AI agents by the end of 2026 (up from <5% in 2025), while the agentic AI market expands from approximately $7.6 billion in 2025 to $10.8 billion in 2026, with longer-term forecasts reaching $139-196 billion by 2034 (Gartner, 2025a; Fortune Business Insights, 2025). Generative AI spending is anticipated to reach $644 billion globally in 2025, a 76.4% increase yearover-year (Gartner, 2025c). Stanford HAI's 2025 AI Index Report documents record private investment ($109.1 billion in the US alone in 2024) and enterprise adoption rising to 78% of organizations (Stanford HAI, 2025). Through a systematic integrative review methodology and critical constructivist lens informed by philosophy of technology and STS, the article evaluates productivity gains (20-40% in general knowledge work; hundreds of percent in targeted processes), real-world deployments (e.g., Salesforce Agentforce, JPMorgan, Walmart), governance deficits (only ~20% of firms have mature frameworks per Deloitte, 2026), ethical risks, and workforce implications. Findings indicate outcomes are conditional: strong governance, human-centered design, and ethical stewardship can steer toward augmentation and flourishing; inadequate attention risks diminishment and unintended consequences. The article concludes with strategic imperatives for responsible integration, arguing that autonomous systems will ultimately reflect the values and choices embedded within them. By prioritizing hybrid human-AI symbiosis and proactive governance, businesses can harness these technologies as a genuine win for humanity rather than a subtle defeat. This balanced, forwardlooking analysis contributes to critical contemporary debates on the future of intelligent technologies in business.

title: AI-Driven Corporate Climate Risk Decision Systems for Global Enterprises: The CADS Architecture, Evidence, Governance, and Research Agenda

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a literature review and does not involve human participants, patient data, clinical trials, or primary data collection. No ethics approval was required.

detail.abstract: Corporate climate risk has become a multi-domain decision problem rather than a sustainability-reporting exercise. Global enterprises must connect physical hazards, transition pathways, greenhouse-gas measurement, supply-chain exposure, capital allocation, insurance, credit, operations, and disclosure into accountable management decisions. Artificial intelligence (AI) can improve climate-risk decision making by extracting information from unstructured disclosures, fusing geospatial and enterprise data, supporting scenario analysis, detecting emissions anomalies, and enabling evidence-grounded workflows. Yet the empirical literature also shows that climate signals are noisy, disclosure is uneven, emissions estimates are method-dependent, and generative models can produce unsupported claims. This integrative structured review synthesizes evidence from climate finance, corporate climate management, machine learning for climate, climate-related natural language processing, measurement-reporting-verification systems, and emerging AI and sustainability regulation. The paper contributes the Climate AI Decision System (CADS) architecture, an enterprise evidence map, governance controls, and a research agenda for AI-enabled climate-risk management. It argues that trustworthy climate AI requires explicit decision rights, source-grounded evidence, model-risk controls, Scope 3 and measurement-reporting-verification traceability, regulatory classification, human escalation, and assurance-ready audit trails.

title: Transportation Immunology: A New Assessment Paradigm and Validation in Nanning's Spring Festival
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Guilin University of Electronic Technology and Traffic Management Department of Nanning Public Security Bureau,

detail.title: Transportation Immunology: A New Assessment Paradigm and Validation in Nanning's Spring Festival
detail.abstract: Traditional traffic engineering relies on symptomatic measurements and event-driven passive responses, lacking a unified theoretical framework for system self-regulation mechanisms. The academic community has long overlooked systematic quantitative assessments of the Chinese Spring Festival—the world’s largest annual human migration which taking as a case for the empirical validation transportation immunology. This study proposes the Transportation Immunology interdisciplinary paradigm, redefining urban transportation systems as complex living organisms.This study developed a four-dimensional assessment framework for traffic health and an information entropy model to quantify antigen-antibody interactions. Empirical analysis of Nanning’s Spring Festival revealed a distinctive three-stage health pattern: critical state pre-holiday, healthy state during the holiday, and sub-healthy state post-holiday, with strong system resilience and rapid recovery capability.This study confirms that the framework effectively characterizes the full-cycle dynamic response of urban systems to extreme shocks, providing the transportation academic community with a novel theoretical paradigm and standardized quantitative assessment tool.

title: The effect of "free shipping" on consumer purchasing decisions online

detail.title: The effect of "free shipping" on consumer purchasing decisions online
detail.abstract: The concept of free shipping has drastically evolved since the inception of online shopping. With these changes also come goals that are sought in exchange for the changes. Many online retailers offer free shipping to increase the total amount consumers spend. Using the economic concepts of demand, consumer surplus, and price elasticity, I seek to explain how the offer of free shipping ultimately affects consumer purchasing decisions. Research has demonstrated that the incentive of free shipping increases consumer demand and consequently increases the amount that consumers spend as well. With this, it also increases the consumer surplus, as due to the aspect of shipping costs being removed, the consumers feel that they are receiving more value for what they are spending. Overall, the incentive of free shipping works as both an economic and psychological tool that many businesses offer to affect consumer purchasing decisions.
